We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by $2d_1$ and the magnetic field strength is $bλ$, the lower bounds have the form $e^{-bλd_1^2-Cd_1^{1+δ}}$ for every fixed $δ\in(0,1)$. No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.
Rigidity of algebraic sets with small distortion

We prove that for positive integers $k$, $n$, and $d>1$, there is a maximal $c(k,n,d)>1$ such that if $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a connected $k$-dimensional complex algebraic set with degree at most $d$ and $dist(X) < c(k,n,d)$, then $X$ must be a complex affine linear subspace, where $dist(X)$ denotes the distortion of $X$ and is given by the supremum of the ratios $d_{inner}(p, q)/d_{outer}(p, q)$ for all $p,q\in X$ with $p\not= q$. We also prove that $c(1,n,d)=\sqrt{2}$ for any positive integers $k$ and $n$. This result provides a sharp rigidity phenomenon for curves in the $c$-LNE category, showing that near-isometric behavior of the inner and outer metrics forces the curve to be as simple as possible.
On the denominators of signed harmonic sums

Let $\eps=(\eps_i)_{i\ge1}$ be a sequence with $\eps_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $v_n(\eps)$ be the positive denominator of $\sum_{i=1}^n\eps_i/i$ in lowest terms. We prove that $|\{1\le n\le x:v_n(\eps)\ne v_{n+1}(\eps)\}|=o(x)$ uniformly in $\eps$. In particular, the set of positive integers $n$ with $v_n(\eps)=v_{n+1}(\eps)$ has asymptotic density one for every sequence of signs. This answers a problem of Wu and Chen, \emph{J. Number Theory} \textbf{200} (2019), 397--406.

We introduce statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamic systems. Statistical decision theory integrates several statistical tasks, such as estimation, hypothesis testing, and classification. In this study, we consider statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamics, which unifies sensing, classification, and uncertainty relations. In particular, we focus on the minimax risk, the smallest achievable expected loss under the worst-case parameter choice, even with an optimal estimator. We derive lower bounds on the minimax risk using Le Cam's two-point method. The derived relationships can be used across a broader range of thermodynamic scenarios. To illustrate these relations, we study classification and distribution estimation problems in a Markov process. We demonstrate that the minimax risk provides lower bounds given by the dynamical activity in these problems. Furthermore, by examining particular dynamics, we establish that the resulting bounds simplify to uncertainty relations involving dynamical activity or entropy production.

In this paper we obtain the critical probability $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ for bootstrap percolation with the infection threshold $r=f(n)n^a$ on the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_{n}$, where $0<a<1$ and $f(n)=n^{o(1)}$. More precisely, we obtain the exact first-order and second-order terms of $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ by extending the main theorem of Balogh, Bollob{á}s, and Morris (2009).
The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator

We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=wλ$ for real or octonion $λ$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(wλ_1)λ_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $λ_2λ_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds
Snir Hordan; Harm Derksen; Mircea Petrache; Nadav Dym

Neural networks that respect the symmetries of point clouds commonly compute high-order representations of the rotation group to improve their expressivity. Such models are known to be universal, and thus able to separate any pair of point clouds, when using representations of sufficiently high order, yet no precise bound on this order, as a function of the number of points, was previously known. We establish the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations. By showing Tensor Field Networks and MACE can express all invariant polynomials of a given degree with sufficient representation order, we additionally derive the first explicit, quadratic bound on the representation order sufficient for these architectures to be complete, replacing previous existence results with concrete guarantees. We further show that, under local regularity assumptions, point cloud separation can be achieved with a message-passing-based model using invariants whose degree depends only on the size of a local neighborhood, rather than on the size of the full point cloud. Finally, we provide counterexamples showing MACE must compute high order irreducible representations to separate locally regular point clouds.
On a problem of Ma and Chen concerning minimal additive complements

Let $m\geq1$ be an integer and let $W=(m\mathbb N_0+X)\cup U\cup V\subseteq\mathbb Z$ be bounded below, where $X\ne\varnothing$, $[U]_m\subseteq[X]_m$, $[X]_m\cap[V]_m=\varnothing$, and $V$ contains no infinite arithmetic progression with common difference $m$. Here $[S]_m$ denotes the set of residue classes modulo $m$ represented by $S$. Suppose that $W$ satisfies the $\mathcal C$-condition modulo $m$. For $0\leq r<m$, let $V_r=V\cap(r+m\mathbb Z)$, and put $V'=\bigcup_{|V_r|=\infty}V_r$, where the union is over $0\leq r<m$. We prove that $W$ has a minimal additive complement if $V'$ satisfies the big-hole property modulo $m$. This answers a problem posed by Ma and Chen.
A robust finite element method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics using Whitney forms

A stabilized semi-discrete finite element scheme for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system is presented. The scheme uses the Whitney $2$-form and $1$-form for the fluid velocity and magnetic induction, respectively. The key ingredient is a magnetic curl-jump penalty term, which allows us to prove a pre-asymptotic error estimate of order $O(h^{1/2})$ with a constant depending on solution norms but not explicitly on the fluid viscosity and magnetic diffusivity.
A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem

We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4π$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.
Pointwise Wave--Damping for Linearized Vlasov--Poisson: Compactly Supported Radial Equilibria and Relativistic Applications
Haina Li; Quoc-Hung Nguyen; Zhilong Xue

We establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response Green function and the complete electric field of the linearized Vlasov--Poisson system in $\mathbb{R}_x^3\times\mathbb{R}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. Both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $L_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying Landau-damped component. The wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. The equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. The proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. The electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. An exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.
Rational Dyck Excursion Counts as Sums of Generalized Fuss-Catalan Products
Brecht Verbeken; Arne Vanhoyweghen; Vincent Ginis

For walks with jumps +p and -q, where p,q are coprime positive integers, we express the weak and strict rational Dyck excursion counts as finite weighted sums of generalized Fuss-Catalan products. Both sums run over the same partitions of q for every path size. Reversing the order of the steps and changing their signs transforms a returning walk with jumps +p and -q into one with jumps +q and -p, with the same heights in reverse order. This preserves both weak and strict excursions. Applying the formulas with p and q exchanged therefore gives sums over partitions of p, so we can choose the smaller of the two jump magnitudes. The indices of the Fuss-Catalan factors satisfy certain divisibility conditions that are determined by the jump magnitudes and the partition parts. The weak formula alternates in sign with the number of parts, whereas every term in the strict formula is positive. We prove both formulas by cutting unrestricted walks at their first and last visits to their lowest height. Expanding the resulting factors produces the partitions of q and the different signs. We also give equivalent binomial convolutions. Multiplying each Fuss-Catalan factor by q in the weak formula or p in the strict formula gives a positive integer. For q=1, the weak and strict counts reduce to Fuss-Catalan and shifted Raney numbers, respectively; for q=2 and q=3, the formulas yield explicit convolution identities.
Uniform lower bounds for the average length of finite Pierce expansions

For integers $1\leq a\leq b$, the length of the finite Pierce expansion of $a/b$ is the number of steps of the iteration $r\mapsto b\bmod r$ which starts at $a$ and ends at zero. Erdős and Shallit (1991) proved that the average of these lengths over $1\leq a\leq b$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log b$, and suggested that it is at least of order $\log b$. In this paper, we prove that the average length is at least $\sqrt{2\log b}-3(\log b)^{1/4}-11$ for every $b\geq2$. We also show that, for each $0<c<\sqrt2$, the proportion of numerators $a$ for which the length is less than $c\sqrt{\log b}$ tends to zero exponentially fast in $\sqrt{\log b}$, with an explicit rate. Our approach refines the interval-counting argument of Erdős and Shallit by restricting the product of the initial digits. As applications, we obtain similar bounds for reduced fractions and for numerators in a fixed congruence class.
Reduction of structure groups for noncommutative principal bundles

Let $G$ be a compact group and let $H \subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup. We study reduction of the structure group for noncommutative principal bundles, modelled by free C${}^*$-dynamical systems in the sense of Ellwood. We first describe how induction from $H$ to $G$ behaves on associated correspondences and their tensor structure. Using reconstruction, this leads to a Tannakian characterization of reduction of the structure group in terms of the associated tensor functor. For normal subgroups, we characterize reduction in terms of central equivariant homomorphisms and derive module- and $K$-theoretic obstructions. We conclude with a noncommutative $O(n)$-example which admits no reduction to $SO(n)$.
Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications

Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder bound for the map sending a Hölder potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.
Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces

A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.
Asymptotic Enumeration of $F$-decompositions in Typical Hypergraphs and of Universal Cycles
Danni Li; Bin Wang; Junxue Zhang

In this paper, we determine the asymptotic number of $F$-decompositions in typical hypergraphs. More precisely, let $F$ be a non-trivial $f$-vertex $k$-graph. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $F$-divisible $(n^{-ζ},h,p)$-typical $k$-graph $G$ has $n^{\frac{f-k+o_n(1)}{|F|}|G|}$ $F$-decompositions. As an application, we asymptotically enumerate universal cycles for $k$-subsets of $[n]$, or equivalently, tight Euler tours of the complete $k$-graph $K_n^k$. For every $k\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying $k\mid {n-1 \choose k-1}$, the number of such universal cycles is $n^{(1-γ(n)){n \choose k}}$, where $0<γ(n)=o_n(1)$. More generally, for $\ell\in[k-1]$, we show that a sufficiently typical $n$-vertex $k$-graph $G$ satisfying the corresponding divisibility condition has $n^{(k-\ell-γ'(n))|G|}$ Euler $\ell$-tours, where $0<γ'(n)=o_n(1)$.
Surfaces Associated to Zeros of Automorphic $L$-functions
Debmalya Basak; Cruz Castillo; Alexandru Zaharescu

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, Montgomery established results concerning pair correlation of zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Rudnick and Sarnak extended these results to automorphic $L$-functions and all level correlations. We discover additional geometric structures associated to the zeros of automorphic $L$-functions. In the case of pair correlation, these structures form certain surfaces which display Gaussian behavior. For triple correlation, these structures exhibit Laplace and Chi-squared distributions, revealing an unexpected phase transition.
General Periodic Conservation Laws Motivated by Traffic Modeling
Rinaldo M. Colombo; Mauro Garavello; Claudia Nocita

This paper deals with the well-posedness, in the spatially periodic setting, of a mixed system of nonlocal-local conservation laws modeling traffic flow where autonomous vehicles --- informed on traffic conditions over long distances --- interact with human-driven bulk traffic. We also provide a comprehensive well-posedness theory in the periodic framework separately for general local conservation laws and for systems of nonlocal conservation laws, together with a priori total variation bounds and stability estimates.
Powers and Functional Calculus for $m$-Selfadjoint and Skew $m$-Selfadjoint Operators
M. Faghih-Ahmadi; T. Bermúdez; K. Hedayatian; H. Zaway

We study powers and functional calculi of higher-order selfadjoint and skew higher-order selfadjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces. First, we compare the behavior of their powers with the corresponding theory for $m$-isometries. We prove that if $T$ is invertible and two powers $T^r$ and $T^s$ are, respectively, $m$- and $\ell$-selfadjoint, then $T^{\gcd(r,s)}$ is $\min\{m,\ell\}$-selfadjoint. In particular, invertibility yields the expected converse for consecutive powers. We also show that two consecutive skew $m$-selfadjoint powers must be non-invertible; in fact, nilpotent. For polynomials, we obtain coefficient characterizations under a cardinality assumption on the spectrum. Finally, for holomorphic functions we give spectral characterizations according to whether the spectrum is finite, or the domain of analyticity is a region, and we derive consequences for Möbius transformations and $m$-isometries. Several examples illustrate why the spectral hypotheses cannot be omitted.
Simultaneous Matrix Multiplication by Tensor Contraction Aggregation

We present an interpretation of the fast matrix multiplication algorithms of Coppersmith and Winograd as aggregations of tensor contractions. This point of view provides a direct connection to older constructions by Pan and to more recent work on bilinear algorithms for symmetric tensor contraction. Further, we provide a new simple approach for exact aggregation of tensor contractions, each one yielding an independent matrix-matrix product. These constructions and border rank adaptations thereof do not come close to improving the best known bounds on $ω$ (the matrix multiplication exponent), but provide explicit moderate-size fast matrix multiplication algorithms that achieve a better exponent than Strassen's algorithm and have potential practical value. These results imply improvements to the best known bounds on the rank and border rank of a fixed number of independent square matrix products. In particular, using $\langle m,m,m\rangle$ to denote the matrix multiplication tensor for matrices of dimension $m$, we obtain constructions that give bounds such as the border rank bound \[ \underline R\!\left(\langle n^2,n^2,n^2\rangle^{\oplus9}\right) \le (n+1)^6+6(n+1)^5, \] and the exact rank bound \[ R\!\left(\langle n^3,n^3,n^3\rangle^{\oplus14}\right)\le (n+1)^9. \] We quantify the accuracy of such constructions in finite precision, and provide border-rank constructions that reduce cost with limiting retained fractions of accuracy at least $1/2$, $1/3$, or $1/4$ relative to the classical matrix-multiplication approach under the stated error model.
Constrained modularity maximization in complex networks via branch-and-price
Jaewoo Kim; Seungyeop Lee; Jaemyung Ahn; Euihyeon Choi; Jeong-Hoon Kim

Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. We study constrained modularity maximization with restrictions on the number of communities, must-link and cannot-link relations, and general resource constraints. While fast heuristics can provide high-quality solutions, they generally lack optimality guarantees, whereas exact mathematical-programming approaches can become computationally demanding as the network size and constraint complexity increase. We develop a unified optimization framework offering complementary heuristic and exact solution methods. These include a constrained Louvain heuristic for feasible solution generation, a column-generation heuristic with graph-partitioning-based pricing, and exact branch-and-price algorithms using mixed-integer linear programming and sparse mixed-integer quadratic programming formulations for the pricing subproblem. We develop a cutting-plane procedure providing independent upper bounds to assess solution quality when exact optimization cannot be completed. Experiments on 11 unconstrained networks with up to 1,005 nodes and 30 constrained instances with up to 379 nodes demonstrate the complementary roles of these methods. The column-generation heuristic rapidly improves the constrained Louvain solutions across the tested constraint classes, while branch-and-price using the sparse quadratic formulation solves 29 of the 30 constrained instances to optimality within a one-hour time limit. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. Overall, the framework guides method selection to balance computational time, solution quality, and optimality guarantees.
Vorticity growth beyond bounded relative vorticity for axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl

We establish upper bounds for vorticity and related quantities in axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl in $\mathbb{R}^3$, assuming that the initial relative vorticity $ω_0/r$ belongs to $L^1\cap L^p$ with $3<p\le \infty$. For each fixed $p \in (3,\infty]$, we obtain polynomial-in-time upper bounds for the radial moments, the radial velocity, and the $L^p$ norm of vorticity. We then consider initial data with unbounded relative vorticity whose growth near the axis is controlled by $Φ(\log \tfrac{1}{r})$ for a subexponential profile $Φ$, so that $ω_0/r$ belongs to $L^p$ for every $p<\infty$ but not to $L^{\infty}$. For such data, we derive profile dependent upper bounds for the vorticity maximum. In particular, for any polynomial function $Φ(s)=s^k$ with $k\ge 0$, we show that $\|ω(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is bounded by $(1+t)^{\frac{4}{3}+k} (\log (2+t) )^{\frac{2k}{3}}$. Moreover, for initial data satisfying $ω_0/r \in L^1\cap L^p$ with a fixed $p\in (3,\infty)$, under additional symmetry and vertical confinement assumptions, we obtain a subexponential-in-time upper bound for the vorticity maximum, thereby improving the classical exponential bound for such data.
Commutative Counterexamples to Arveson's Hyperrigidity Conjecture

We construct counterexamples to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative $C^*$-algebras. In each example, every irreducible representation of the $C^*$-envelope is a boundary representation, but hyperrigidity fails. The first example is the operator system of continuous affine functions on an infinite-dimensional weighted $\ell^p$ ball. In the second infinite-dimensional example, we start with commuting operators and construct a nontrivial dilation. The final example comes from a compact truncated epigraph of a strictly convex function and yields a finite-dimensional operator system.
Beyond Finite-Sum Optimization: A Primal-Dual Method for Decentralized Finite-Max Optimization
Zhouxing Luo; Lei Wang; Xin Liu

Many decentralized systems are judged by their worst-performing agents rather than their average performance. We study finite-max optimization over a connected undirected network, where each agent knows only its own smooth, possibly nonconvex objective. Quadratic regularization yields a smooth finite-sum representation with a scalar dual variable and locally computable clipped weights. We develop an alternating primal-dual gradient tracking (APDGT) method, using neighbor communication without any global or centralized projections. Under smoothness and level-boundedness assumptions, a localized Lyapunov analysis with vanishing regularization establishes bounded primal iterates and Clarke stationarity of every accumulation point of their network average. The averaged sequence contains an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, measured by near-active gradients, within $O (\varepsilon^{-3})$ iterations. Synthetic tests and decentralized logistic regression on Fashion-MNIST illustrate convergence behavior and potential improvements in worst-agent performance.
On sharp stability of the BCC quantizer

We prove sharp nonlinear stability estimates for the squared-distance quantization energy of the body-centered cubic lattice. The reference Hessian has optimal coercivity constant \(1/96\) relative to nearest-neighbor displacement differences, uniformly over all finite-index periods. We classify all equality modes and prove cubic cancellation on their span. This yields nonlinear stability in a neighborhood independent of the period, including volume-preserving strain. The loss in the sharp energy coefficient is at most quadratic for each fixed period and exactly linear when all periods are allowed. We also determine the transition between these regimes. Finally, we prove global optimality and uniqueness of BCC, up to rigid motions, among two-site configurations with rectangular period cells of fixed volume.
Global strong solutions to the aligned 2.5D non-resistive full MHD system with high temperature and a strong magnetic field
Yachun Li; Zixuan Qu; Zhaoyang Shang

We study the Cauchy problem for an aligned vertical-field reduction of the full compressible non-resistive MHD equations in two space variables. The shear and bulk viscosities are proportional to $θ^α$, and the heat conductivity is proportional to $θ^β$. For $2<α<β<α+2$, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the background temperature and the comparable magnetic background are sufficiently large, while the positive density background is fixed. The velocity and temperature perturbations belong initially to $H^2$, and the transported magnetic perturbation belongs to $H^1\cap D^{1,4}$; their absolute norms may be bounded by an arbitrary fixed constant. Alignment is essential and implies a small density perturbation relative to the magnetic background. Our proof combines relative energy estimates, uniform in the background temperature and magnetic field, with coupled estimates for the material derivatives of the velocity and temperature. These bounds control the source terms in the damped magnetic-gradient equation, allowing us to close the global a priori estimates without a separate large-time decay assumption. We construct the global strong solution by smooth approximation and Sobolev energy estimates for the approximating solutions, and prove uniqueness by an energy estimate for the difference of two solutions.
On the Nonoccurrence of Gradient Restart in Nesterov Accelerated Gradient Method
Chenglong Bao; Liang Chen; Jiahong Li; Defeng Sun

Gradient restarting often improves the practical performance of accelerated gradient methods for unconstrained convex optimization problems, but a general theoretical guarantee of such improvement remains unclear. In this paper, we construct smooth, strongly convex objectives with Lipschitz-continuous gradients and corresponding initial points for which gradient restart never occurs, both for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and for its ordinary differential equation model. From these examples, we conclude that strong convexity and smoothness alone do not guarantee that gradient restart improves the convergence behavior of the accelerated method or its continuous-time model. In particular, for the continuous-time example, the objective gap is asymptotic to $1/(πt^3)$. We therefore obtain a negative answer to the open problem raised by Su, Boyd, and Cand{è}s [\textit{J. Mach. Learn. Res.}, 2016, 17(153), 1--43] of whether gradient restart guarantees linear convergence of the continuous dynamics for smooth strongly convex objectives.
The binomial distribution maximises entropy among sums of negatively related indicators with fixed mean and support

We show that the binomial distribution supported on $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ and with mean $np$ for some $0<p<1$ maximises entropy within the class of sums of negatively related indicator random variables with this mean and support. Our results generalise the main result of Yu (2008), who showed that this binomial distribution maximises entropy within the smaller class of ultra-log-concave random variables of order $n$. Our proof makes use of a Markov chain construction of Yu (2008), together with a stochastic ordering argument.
On multilinear forms for mod \(p\) representations of \(\operatorname{GL}_2\) over a \(p\)-adic field
Hao Liu; Haoran Wang; Yuting Yang

Let \(F\) be a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q_p\), for any prime \(p\), and let \(L/F\) be a ramified quadratic extension. We compute the spaces of \(\mathcal O_L^\times\)-equivariant linear forms on the representation \(\operatorname{ind}^G_{KZ}σ/(Φ-λ)\). The only nonzero cases arise from one-dimensional quotients. Consequently, the restriction of an infinite-dimensional irreducible smooth mod \(p\) representation of \(\operatorname{GL}_2(F)\) with a central character to \(\mathcal O_L^\times\) has no character quotient. We apply this vanishing result to show that a finite tensor product of smooth mod \(p\) representations of \(\operatorname{GL}_2(F)\) admits no nonzero invariant linear form whenever at least one factor is infinite-dimensional and irreducible with a central character.
Lightning Algorithm for Inhomogeneous Modified Helmholtz Equations on Cornered Domains and Their Applications

We develop in this paper an efficient solver for the inhomogeneous modified Helmholtz equations in two-dimensional complex domains with particular attention to resolving corner singularities. We represent the solution as a summation of a particular solution and the solution of the modified Helmholtz equation. Built upon suitable domain embedding methods, we compute the particular solution using the Fourier spectral method and/or Legendre--Fourier spectral method. To treat the corner singularities, we develop a lightning algorithm by employing an expansion of the modified Bessel functions of the second kind, coupled with tapered exponentially clustering poles, to approximate the corner singularities, and using an expansion of the modified Bessel functions of the first kind to approximate the smooth part of the solution. Finally, we determine the unknown expansion coefficients by solving a least-squares problem to satisfy the boundary conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that root-exponential convergence can be achieved for the modified Helmholtz equation with corner singularities. To further demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm, it has been successfully applied to solve some typical linear and nonlinear parabolic equations. We have also made a first attempt in extending the lightning algorithm to a three-dimensional modified Helmholtz equation.
The irrationality exponent of the lemniscate period: A determinant proof with a Lean 4 formalization

Let $Ω=2\int_0^1(1-t^4)^{-1/2}dt$. We prove that, for every real $ν>2$, there is $Q\geq2$ such that $q^{-ν}<|Ω-p/q|$ for every integer $p$ and every integer $q\geq Q$. Consequently $Ω$ is irrational and its irrationality exponent is two. The proof combines elliptic separated-weight interpolation, arithmetic denominator estimates, and an analytic determinant bound on a square complex-multiplication grid. The determinant comparison uses the same selected source columns on both sides. We give the integral-to-lattice normalization, the exact local-coordinate and common-multiplier transport, and the parameter order that makes the two bounds incompatible. The accompanying Lean 4 development proves the endpoint without additional hypotheses. Numbered formal references link the mathematical argument to exact declarations in the complete source distribution; an appendix gives the pinned build environment and the dependency audit.
Exact cost of the Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem in one dimension

We study the random Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem: finding a Hamiltonian cycle of maximal total cost through any set of $N$ cities on a line, where each edge cost is a function of its Euclidean length. We characterize the maximizing cycles for convex increasing, concave increasing, and convex decreasing cost functions. For points sampled independently and uniformly from the unit interval, we derive explicit expressions for the average maximal cost for arbitrary $N$ and asymptotic expansions with power-law edge costs.
The Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary

We establish local existence for the nonlinear Israel--Stewart equations describing a relativistic viscous fluid with a physical vacuum free boundary. Compared with ideal fluids with a physical vacuum, the relaxation equation for the bulk viscosity introduces further derivative loss. The problem is compounded by the degenerate nature of the equations of motion on the free boundary. In this work, we construct solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces via a Nash--Moser iteration. Since the domain moves, the iteration is carried out in Lagrangian coordinates, while the linearized operator at each iterate is inverted on the Eulerian domain with the local well-posedness of the linearized equations established in our earlier work.
Saturation degree of powers of graded ideals
Le Tuan Hoa; Hop Dang Nguyen; Ngo Viet Trung

Let $I$ be a non-nilpotent graded ideal of a standard graded algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring. We show that the saturation degree sdeg $I^n$ is asymptotically a constant function or a linear function whose slope is one of the generating degrees of $I$. Furthermore, we give sufficient (and necessary) conditions for a numerical functions to be the function sdeg $I^n$ of an ideal $I$ generated by forms of the same degree. Our results may provide a better understanding of the initial behavior of the regularity function reg $I^n$.
On Exact Dihedral Angle Sum Ranges for Orthocentric and Isogonic Tetrahedra

Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. We introduce a framework that transforms discrete optimization into continuous optimization over parameterized probability distributions. The framework reveals a common distributional structure behind several methods that have largely developed independently, including continuous reformulations for multilinear binary optimization, Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning, the cross-entropy method, mean-field variational optimization, and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm. It enables flexible and modular algorithm design, for example, by using neural networks to incorporate contextual information or by enforcing convexity of the lifted problem. Mixed-integer programs have found applications in many real-world problems but remain difficult to solve at scale. Well--posedness and homogenization of a waste--protein clearance model in cortical tissue

We give the classification of C-spaces (i.e., compact homogeneous spaces admitting an invariant complex structure), up to finite cover and equivariant diffeomorphism, of dimension 6, 8 and 10. The conditions for the existence of a balanced, pluriclosed, CYT and LCK Hermitian metric are established for dimensions 6 and 8.

For $dγ_n=π^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12Δ+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_γ=DL^{-1/2}Π_0$, where $Π_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_γ$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. Let $C\subset\R^n$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, $n\ge1$, and let $T\in\I_n(X)$, where $X=\spt T$ is compact. Suppose $ι:\partial C\to X$ is an isometric embedding for the Euclidean chord metric and \[ \partial T=ι_\#\cur{\partial C},\qquad \M(T)=\Leb^n(C). \] Then $ι$ extends to a surjective isometry $I:C\to X$ satisfying $I_\#\cur C=T$. No map from the filling to the convex body is assumed.

It has been studied in both non-stationary online learning, which aims to minimize dynamic regret against time-varying comparator sequences, and universal online learning, which seeks to adapt to unknown loss curvature. Prior work obtained gradient-variation bounds using different techniques tailored to each setting. We propose a simple and unified method based on surrogate losses with a quadratic penalty on decision movement, yielding gradient-variation bounds in both settings. For non-stationary online learning, the method induces an optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction, enabling a broad class of algorithms to match the rate established by Zhao et al. (2024). Finally, we apply our method to online games and improve on existing guarantees.
Wiener's criterion and resolutivity for the $p$-parabolic equation

We characterize boundary regularity for $u_t=Δ_p u$ in arbitrary bounded open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ for $n\ge2$ and $p\in(2n/(n+1),2)\cup (2,\infty)$. We prove equivalent Wiener criteria in terms of capacitary potentials on prescribed cylinders and in terms of intrinsic capacities. Both require divergence at every positive obstacle height. Independently, we prove Perron resolutivity for continuous data on the full topological boundary of every nonempty bounded open set for all $n\geq 1$ and $p>1$. For $2<p<n$, examples show that divergence at every sufficiently large height does not imply regularity.

We study sign bias between hyperbolic double cosets with $ad>0$ and $ad<0$ in appropriate cocompact Fuchsian groups. We prove that an eventual bias can only favour $ad<0$, and construct examples exhibiting such a bias. When the normal-derivative periods of all nonconstant eigenfunctions with eigenvalue at most $1/4$ vanish, we prove an $Ω_\pm(X^{1/2})$ result and show that the counting difference takes both signs in every sufficiently large interval $[X,CX]$, for some fixed $C>1$.

Solutions of second-order elliptic PDE problems on nonconvex or cracked domains with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions typically lie outside $H^2(Ω)$. Furthermore in specific settings where the geometric structure of the support matters, the experimental results show that using a diffusion-based augmentation kernel outperforms the Gaussian one.
Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness are algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication

We continue our investigations on pointwise multipliers for spaces of dominating mixed smoothness. In this paper we prove that under a certain conditions Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness form algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication.

In 1996, Michaux and Villemaire showed that any nontrivial expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +)$ defines new unary sets. We conjecture that the same holds over the structure $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$, and we prove a partial result in this direction. To do so, we first show that every nonempty sparse $k$-automatic set is a Presburger-definable image of some Cartesian power of $k^\mathbb{N}$. Using this characterization, we prove that if an expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$ defines the same unary sets, then every set of sublinear growth definable in the expansion is already definable in $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$.
From Inverse Vandermonde Matrices to the Shift Structure of the Dirichlet Eta and Beta Functions

We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the inverse of Vandermonde matrices with nodes drawn from the quadratic sequences u n = n 2 and u n = (n -1 2 ) 2 . We derive new limiting formulas for the entries of the inverses, expressed through the even and odd central factorial numbers. These formulas are then used to study the asymptotic behavior of a ratio of determinants involving a modified Vandermonde matrix. For each node sequence, the corresponding determinant ratio converges uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane to an explicit expression involving the Dirichlet eta or beta function. We then study a family of related functions and, using an inversion theorem, exhibit their shift structure: the shifted values of the eta and beta functions are recovered as finite linear combinations of the family, which yields an integral form of these values as integrals of polynomials related to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials against generalized (half-)Clausen functions. A unified form of the shift representation, valid for an arbitrary base point z with Re(z) > 0, brings the eta and beta families under a single theorem. On the critical line the representation is unitary and the values on the two sides are complex conjugates.
One-Dimensional Symmetry Reductions of the Monge-Ampère Equation on Some Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones in $\mathbb{R}^4$
Amir Valiakhmetov; Ewsey Obzherin; Alexey Chernov; Roland Hildebrand

Motivated by non-symmetric conic optimization, we construct six explicit families of semi-homogeneous proper convex cones $K$ in $\mathbb R^4$. For each family, a specified three-dimensional subgroup of linear automorphisms of $K$ has generic orbits of codimension one. This yields an orbit invariant $t$ and reduces the Monge-Ampère equation $\det F''=e^{2F}$, defining the canonical barrier on $K$, to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) with independent variable $t$. The families include asymmetric power, rotational-power, exponential, and nonabelian-type cones. For the power and exponential cases we derive first integrals and parametric solutions of the ODE. The reductions open the way for computing the canonical barrier on these cones numerically.
Power-of-two cycles in projective cubic graphs of large edge-width

Heckman and Krakovski proved that every 3-connected cubic planar graph contains a cycle of length 2^m for some 2 $\le$ m $\le$ 7. We extend this to 3-connected cubic graphs embedded in the real projective plane with face-width at least three and edge-width at least 48; the cycle may moreover be taken contractible. The argument passes to the spherical double cover, where the planar theorem provides the cycle inside a subgraph of diameter at most 47, and the condition on the edge-width guarantees that this subgraph projects injectively.
Topological mapping class groups of non-simply connected 4-manifolds

We construct topological isotopy invariants of homeomorphisms of non-simply connected 4-manifolds using the topological Dax invariant of disks and the Freedman-Quinn invariant of spheres. Our invariants are effective for various non-smoothable 4-manifolds without assuming that the fundamental groups are good. They detect infinite-rank free abelian direct factors of the pseudoisotopy-trivial and homotopy-trivial mapping class groups, and give lower bounds on the Prüfer rank of the Torelli groups modulo homotopy-trivial mapping classes, including examples of infinite Prüfer rank. Our method is also useful for smooth 4-manifolds. We construct stably smoothable homeomorphisms of the Enriques surface and many Dolgachev surfaces that act trivially on homology but are not homotopic to the identity.
On Special Arithmetic Gamma Values and Thakur's Gauss Sums: From $\infty$-adic to $v$-adic

In this paper, we establish an explicit algebra isomorphism between the normalized $\infty$-adic arithmetic gamma values and their $v$-adic counterparts. The construction relies on Thakur's arithmetic Gauss sums, which arise naturally from the Gross-Koblitz-Thakur relations. Our result demonstrates the phenomenon that Gauss sums, commonly regarded as "finite" analogs of gamma functions, serve as a bridge connecting the $\infty$-adic and $v$-adic gamma values.
Universal coding with the exhaustive peres transform

Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure is completed into a bijection of $\bits^N$: the recursion runs to exhaustion, nothing is discarded, and every input splits into fair bits and residual bits. The residual strings form a complete prefix code that determines the number of ones of the input, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual for every exchangeable law. For a Bernoulli source the likelihood factorises exactly, in decoding order, into a factor $1/2$ per fair bit and a Bernoulli factor per residual bit, with biases obtained by iterating two explicit maps. The number of fair bits per input symbol tends to the entropy almost surely, also on larger alphabets. Code B stores the fair bits and codes only the residual with an arithmetic coder; its ideal length is that of the two-part code, at most $\log\_2(N+1)+1$ bits above $-\log\_2\Pr\_θ(s)$ for every input $s$ and bias $θ$. Code C uses Rice codes instead. In experiments up to $N=2^{20}$ its mean regret stays below $200$ bits, where a Rice coder on the raw input loses a fixed fraction of the entropy on skewed sources. For sources with memory, the Burrows--Wheeler transform of the reversed string arranges all context orders in one tree of intervals; coding the leaves of a pruned tree as Bernoulli strings adapts to every Markov order up to its depth, and on suffix-closed trees the leaf weights determine the split points.
Decomposing the Action of Macdonald Operators for Classical Types

We study Macdonald operators associated to classical root systems of types $B_N$, $C_N$, and $D_N$. We provide explicit formulas for decomposing the cumulative action of these operators as the sum of the actions of lower-rank operators and auxiliary operators. We also discuss the same idea in the elliptic case, also known as Ruijsenaars operators, and show that under the trigonometric limit, the identity reduces to type-$A_N$ decomposition.
Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
Zhuowen Guo; Rongzhong Xiao; Shuhao Zhang

Let $(X,\mathcal B,μ)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(μ)$ and $G\in L^q(μ)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$. Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.
Basis Selection For Analog Coded Computing Under Differential Privacy Constraints
Aaditya Sharma; Rimpi Borah; J. Harshan

In analog coded computing, encoding basis functions are typically chosen to guarantee exact reconstruction and improve numerical stability. However, the same basis functions also determine the statistical geometry of the observations available to colluding workers, and hence directly influence the privacy of the underlying data. This suggests that basis selection should not be viewed solely as a reconstruction or numerical conditioning problem, but rather as a joint privacy and accuracy co-design problem. Motivated by this observation, we revisit Analog Lagrange Coded Computing (ALCC) and show that the full orthogonality constraints imposed by the conventional Lagrange basis are stronger than what is required for exact recovery. We retain only the interpolation constraints necessary for the data bearing basis functions and require the noise bearing basis functions merely to vanish at the data recovery points. This yields a parameterized family of generalized polynomial encoding bases that preserves exact reconstruction while introducing additional design degrees of freedom. We then derive a basis-dependent characterization of differential privacy for colluding workers and formulate a privacy-calibrated numerical optimization problem that jointly selects the data and noise basis functions to reduce reconstruction error while satisfying a prescribed \((ε,δ)\)-DP requirement. The resulting framework therefore treats the encoding basis itself as a privacy-design variable, rather than selecting a fixed closed-form basis a priori. The same design philosophy is also compatible with alternative privacy metrics such as mutual-information leakage. Numerical results show that, at the same privacy level, optimized basis functions substantially reduce floating-point reconstruction error relative to conventional ALCC.
Semiclassical measures for quantized elliptic and parabolic symplectic linear maps of the multidimensional torus

We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, $ξ$) = Q($ξ$)/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. We prove that the set of semiclassical measures associated to a periodic matrix A coincides with the set of invariant probability measures of A. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.
Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
Louis Carillo; Lo{ï}s Delande; Boris Nectoux

Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.
Biconservative hypersurfaces in space forms with harmonic curvature
Ram Shankar Gupta; Andreas Arvanitoyeorgos; Marina Statha

A biconservative hypersurface $M$ in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ is a hypersurface whose normal part of the vector $Δ\vec{H}$ vanishes. We study such hypersurfaces with harmonic curvature or parallel Ricci curvature, and prove that have constant mean curvature. Also, by combining our results with previous results of H.B. Lawson Jr. and M. Umehara we obtain that if $M$ is a biconservative hypersurface in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ with parallel Ricci tensor or harmonic curvature, then the shape operator $\bold{A}$ of $M$ is covariant constant, i.e. $\nabla\bold{A}=0$.
Homotopy distributions for Vietoris-Rips complexes of random circle samples

We determine the distribution of the homotopy type of the Vietoris-Rips complex of a fixed number of independent uniform points on a circle. An exact identity expresses each binomial moment of a periodic-orbit count as one probability for circular gaps, multiplied by a constant avoidance factor. We evaluate these probabilities by finite lattice-point counts and interpolation, obtaining explicit formulas for every sample size and every real scale. On an explicit rational partition, the probabilities are continuous piecewise polynomials of degree at most one less than the sample size. We also determine the homotopy distribution in the first transition window above each positive critical fraction $c_t=t/(2t+1)$. In this window the number of critical periodic orbits converges to a Poisson law with explicit intensity, yielding the limiting probabilities of the preceding odd sphere, the contractible type, and every wedge multiplicity of the critical even sphere.
A Sarkisov Involution from a Rational Cubic Curve on a Quartic Double Solid

Building on an earlier classification of smooth weak Fano threefolds of Picard number two with small anticanonical morphism, we prove that Case~28 of the table of E1-E1 links from that classification is geometrically realizable. We construct the link by blowing up a smooth rational cubic curve on a degree-two del Pezzo threefold $V_2$, realized as a quartic double solid. A lattice calculation on an anticanonical K3 surface shows that the anticanonical morphism of the blow-up is small, and the covering involution of the anticanonical double cover realizes the flop. The resulting Sarkisov link is a birational involution with the numerical invariants of E1-E1 Case~28.
Second-Order Cover Time of Random Regular Graphs

Let $G_N$ be a uniform random $d$-regular graph on $N$ vertices, with $d\ge3$ fixed. Cooper and Frieze showed that the cover time of simple random walk on $G_N$ is asymptotically $θ_dN\log N$, where $θ_d=(d-1)/(d-2)$. We prove that, in probability over the graph and uniformly in the starting point, $(T_{\rm cov}-θ_dN\log N)/(θ_dN)$ converges in distribution to a standard Gumbel law, confirming a prediction of Tishby, Biham, and Katzav [40]. The proof reduces late points to avoidance probabilities of finite sets via factorial moments, estimates these by Green-matrix capacities, and compares the latter with capacities on the infinite $d$-regular tree. We also obtain Gumbel limits for lazy, continuous-time and finitely many independent walks. For the unvisited set, we prove weighted laws of large numbers, spatial Poisson limits in the cover-time window, and joint Poisson limits for fixed tree-component shapes in their disappearance windows.
Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
Zekai Li; Mauricio Barahona; Philipp Thomas

Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.
Waveguide Deployment Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems
Yanqing Xu; Zhiguo Ding; Xiu Yin Zhang; Tsung-Hui Chang

Most existing studies on pinching-antenna systems optimize the antenna positions or activation states under a prescribed waveguide deployment, where mutually parallel waveguides are commonly adopted. However, it remains unclear whether, and under what conditions, such a deployment is optimal from a communication-performance perspective. To fill this gap, this paper investigates long-term waveguide deployment optimization for pinching-antenna systems over a rectangular service region. We first consider the fundamental two-waveguide case and derive a closed-form sufficient condition, jointly determined by the waveguide height and the service-region aspect ratio, under which a deployment parallel to the longer side of the service region is globally optimal. We then consider the general multi-waveguide case, where the orientation and offset of each waveguide are jointly optimized without prescribing any deployment pattern, and develop an adaptive exchange algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. We further show that, within the parallel class, the waveguides should be aligned with the longer side of the service region, while in the large-height regime, the globally optimal unrestricted deployment asymptotically concentrates all waveguides on the centerline along the longer side. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithm and reveal how the preferred deployment geometry depends on the waveguide height and service-region shape. In particular, nonparallel deployments can provide noticeable gains in intermediate-height regimes, whereas parallel or center-concentrated deployments become favorable in other regimes.
Fate of Arnold tongues and canards in Mobius systems with noise

We consider a class of noisy dynamical systems on the two-dimensional torus whose phase evolution is governed by Mobius transformations. In the deterministic limit, these systems favor phase-locking that is described by the band-gap structure of an associated Schrodinger equation with a periodic potential. We use the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin method to characterize this structure in the slow-fast limit. Then we show that large-deviation theory describes fluctuations of the finite-time rotation number, whereas weak-noise escape actions determine the exponential scale of rare phase slips. These estimates provide quantitative criteria for metastable phase-locking and melting of Arnold tongues over a prescribed observation time. We derive sufficient conditions for stochastic trajectories to follow prescribed canard segments. With controlled entrance errors, exponential amplification of fluctuations along repelling branches leads to an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence in the slow-forcing limit.
Semigroup of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables
Fr{é}d{é}ric Bayart; Maofa Wang; Xingxing Yao

This paper considers discrete and continuous semigroups of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables. For discrete semigroups generated by a single operator, the asymptotic behaviour is analysed. Strongly continuous semigroups are studied, and in particular it is shown that the classical Berkson-Porta theorem fails in this context. As an application, we show that any bounded composition operator is strongly reducible on the Fock space and that it is mean-ergodic.

We introduce the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings and begin the development of their theory over an arbitrary base scheme $S$, in analogy to that of higher coverings in an $\infty$-topos. We show that for $n=0$, our notion recovers Morel's $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings between simplicial sheaves. Under suitable assumptions, we then provide a Galois-theoretic classification of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings. Finally, we answer a question of Morel concerning a geometric criterion for $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings in the negative.
A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category

We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(σ_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $σ_2$ is the Galois automorphism $ζ_{117}\mapstoζ_{117}^2$.
Gabriele Buriola; Giacomo Cozzi; Antonia Dammrau; Anton Freund

We establish a general result on the proof-theoretic strength of well-ordering principles in reverse mathematics. The novelty is that our result gives information over base theories as weak as $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, while previous results of Arai, Pakhomov-Walsh and Buriola-Weiermann required the stronger base theory $\mathsf{ACA}_0$. On the way, we strengthen a result of Carlucci-Mainardi-Rathjen about the ordinal analysis of theories of the form $\mathsf{RCA}_0+\text{``$α$ is a well-order"}$.
On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces

We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.
Energy Equality, Vectorial $L^1$ Contraction, and Mixed-Norm Stability for Parabolic Systems with Rough Skew-Symmetric Potentials

We consider Dirichlet parabolic systems with measurable, real skew-symmetric zero-order potentials on bounded Lipschitz domains in three dimensions. Although skew-symmetry formally removes the potential from the energy balance, singular coefficients may leave the product $CU$ merely integrable, so testing the equation with the solution is not justified. We overcome this obstruction through bounded-gradient entropy identities and stable approximation. For $C\in L^r(0,T;L^q(Ω;\mathbb R^{m\times m}))$ with $1\le r\le\infty$, $6/5\le q\le\infty$, and $2/r+3/q\le7/2$, we establish existence and uniqueness in the full energy--distributional class, exact energy equality at every pair of times, Euclidean-vector $L^1$ contraction, and strong convergence of both solutions and coefficient--solution products under strong coefficient approximation. We compare a vectorial entropy proof with a derivation by scalar entropies and spherical averaging, and explain the narrower roles of temporal regularization, convex invariance, and adjoint transposition. An application to diffusion--precession gives quantitative stability under $L^1$ perturbations of prescribed magnetic fields for bounded initial data, including singular fields outside the main mixed-norm range.

For each $n\geq 4$, we show that the infimal Willmore energy of a non-orientable surface of odd genus immersed in $\mathbb{S}^n$ is attained by an index $(n+1)$ minimal surface in this class. For $n=4$, we obtain in addition the analogous conclusion for surfaces with non-zero Euler number. The proof uses the fact that such surfaces represent a non-trivial cobordism class together with an observation of M. Gromov relating the conformal area in $\mathbb{S}^n$ to minimal fillings in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$.
Two-Dimensional Euclidean Free Fermi Fields from Grassmannian Stochastic Analysis
Claudio Dappiaggi; Francesco Carlo De Vecchi; Pietro Tullio Falzoni; Paolo Rinaldi

Motivated by Nelson's Euclidean Markov-field construction, we develop a counterpart for the massive two-dimensional free Dirac field. Starting from a Gaussian white noise with values in a Grassmann algebra on a non-commutative probability space, we construct the associated Brownian motion and a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck field. The resulting Euclidean Fermi field is realized as a tempered distribution on spacetime test functions, with values in the underlying algebra. Its mixed two-point functions reproduce the Euclidean Dirac fundamental solution. Time-zero fields are obtained by conditional expectation onto the past filtration generated by the noise, while their covariance is the reflected Euclidean Dirac kernel. We show that conditional expectation is compatible with Wick ordering and maps Euclidean Wick polynomials to the corresponding time-zero Wick polynomials. The Euclidean time-translation semigroup is then constructed on time-zero fields and Wick sectors, with generators given by the one-particle Hamiltonian and by its second quantization.
Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision

We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.
Invertible non-cyclic functions in the little Bloch space

This paper presents a method for exhibiting functions $F$ in the little Bloch space $\B_0$ which are invertible, in the sense that $1/F$ also belongs to $\B_0$, and yet fail to be cyclic for the forward shift. The functions obtained in this way give rise to shift-invariant subspaces in $\B_0$ of index two, of a special type. The approach rests on a harmonic-measure criterion for non-cyclicity. This criterion gives a new manifestation of a principle of Borichev and Hedenmalm, and applies in a broad class of spaces of analytic functions.
Well-posedness threshold of the 2D Euler equations in Hölder spaces on infinite sectors

We study existence and uniqueness for the 2D incompressible Euler equations on infinite sectors of acute angle $β$, focusing on vorticity in Hölder-type spaces. In the inifinite sectors, for every $β$, H"older regularity cannot be expected without decay at infinity. Moreover, the corner causes Schauder-type estimates to fail at sufficiently high regularity. We then apply this theory to standard $C^{k,α}$ spaces and show that $k+α=π/β-1$ is the well-posedness threshold. Above this threshold, we construct initial data that exhibit instantaneous loss of regularity. At the threshold, the problem is well-posed if and only if $π/β$ is not an integer. We prove that the partition division operator $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k$ preserves e-positivity, resolving a conjecture of Alexandersson and Dai. For $μ\vdash kn$ and $ν\vdash n$, we express the coefficient of $e_ν$ in $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k(e_μ)$ as a normalized sum of positive rational weights over closed walks on a finite directed graph of $k$-restricted partitions. The proof combines the Pieri rule and a root of unity factorization for Macdonald polynomials. As a corollary, we recover the h-positivity of the symmetric functions $A_{n,k}$ of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.

Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.

The random $k$-XORSAT matrix is an $m\times n$ random matrix $\mathbf A$ over $\mathbb F_2$ that represents a random instance of the $k$-XORSAT problem. Each row of $\mathbf A$ contains precisely $k\geq3$ non-zero entries in random positions. The rows are drawn independently. The matrix $\mathbf A$ is known to have full row rank for $m/n$ below the random $k$-XORSAT satisfiability threshold, which is known explicitly [Dubois, Mandler~2002; Pittel, Sorkin~2016]. Motivated by a problem from quantum game theory and refining a result of Cooper, Frieze and Pegden (2019), we determine the limiting distribution of the rank of $\mathbf A$ beyond the satisfiability threshold.
Flip classes and elementary expansions of vertical-strip LLT polynomials

After the substitution $q\mapsto q+1$, vertical-strip LLT polynomials are weighted sums of strict $P$-partition generating functions indexed by orientations of decorated unit-interval graphs, with weight $q^{\mathrm{asc}(θ)}$. A flip moves an ascending edge across a triangle while keeping its long edge. We show that the sum over every flip class is elementary-positive: it equals the sum of the elementary symmetric functions given by the highest reachable vertices of its orientations. This answers Hwang's question on the Schur positivity of LLT flip-class sums, and it holds for circular unit-interval graphs as well. Summing over classes gives a new proof of the elementary expansion of Alexandersson and Sulzgruber, and its circular analog, which was open. We also obtain a flip-class refinement of the elementary expansion of LLT cumulants.
Young Parabolic PDEs and the Martingale Problem for Young SDEs

Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the martingale problem associated with the hybrid Young--Lyons--Itô differential equation admits a unique solution in the natural class of solutions satisfying Krylov-type estimates, thereby establishing probabilistic weak well-posedness. Our proof relies on an analysis of the associated Kolmogorov equations, which are Young-type parabolic PDEs with irregular coefficients. The resulting theory for such Young-type parabolic PDEs is also of independent interest.
The Wandering Must Continue: Pure Mathematicians as Rangers of the North

Pure mathematics is an honest barometer of a civilization's scientific capacity, maintaining an unwritten culture of rigor, intellectual honesty, and precision whose primary service is not merely theorems, but human judgment. In an era of automated theorem generation and formal verification, this essay argues that establishing a result and understanding why it holds remain distinct achievements that require deliberate institutional protection.
Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups

We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2ν_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2ν_n(G)=0\), and \(π_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.
Efimov effect in an internal spectral gap of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian

We prove the existence of an Efimov sequence in an internal gap of the essential spectrum of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian. The system consists of two identical spinless fermions and one distinguishable particle on \(\Z^3\), with repulsive pair interactions. For each fixed fermion-to-third-particle mass ratio \(γ>γ_*\approx13.6069657\) and total quasi-momentum near \(π\mathbf1\), the mixed zero-range coupling is tuned to a simultaneous upper-threshold resonance. Sufficiently strong nearest-neighbour repulsion between the fermions separates the upper fermion-pair two-cluster spectrum from the free three-particle band. Infinitely many discrete eigenvalues accumulate at the lower endpoint of the resulting gap, which coincides with the free upper edge. We establish logarithmic eigenvalue-counting asymptotics with the same positive coefficient as at zero fermion--fermion coupling. This coefficient also governs accumulation above the essential spectrum throughout the closed weak-coupling interval, including its critical endpoint. We classify the channel spectrum near the free upper edge for all nonnegative fermion couplings.
Singular Stability Estimates for Passive Gamma Emission Tomography of Spent Nuclear Fuel

We study the joint recovery of attenuation and source coefficients from the attenuated X-ray transform, motivated by passive gamma emission tomography of spent nuclear fuel. Both coefficients are constant on known, disjoint disks of equal radius representing fuel rods. The surrounding moderator has known attenuation and zero source. We use tangential singularities of the data to give a sufficient condition on the geometry and coefficients for unique joint reconstruction from full data. For rods arranged on parallel rows separated by more than one rod diameter, with source coefficients uniformly bounded away from zero, we derive explicit reconstruction formulas and stability estimates for both coefficients. The estimates use a singular seminorm determined by two functionals per rod, computed from angular data near selected tangencies. Numerical experiments examine the approximation of these functionals from discretized data.
Sphere Theorems for $\frac{10}{3}$-Positive Curvature Operator of the Second Kind

In this paper, we prove that every connected closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq4$ with $\frac{10}{3}$-positive curvature operator of the second kind is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We also obtain a classification of connected closed Riemannian manifolds with $\frac{10}{3}$-nonnegative curvature operator of the second kind. The key step is to show that $\frac{10}{3}$-positivity implies the PIC1 condition. Finally, we give an example showing that $\frac{10}{3}$ is optimal for deducing PIC1 from $α$-positivity.
Hadamard well-posedness and nonuniform dependence for the incompressible free-boundary ideal MHD equations

We prove local Hadamard well-posedness for the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations without surface tension under the Taylor sign condition. For every $5/2<s<4$, the result holds on bounded fluid domains whose closures are diffeomorphic to the closed ball, with the velocity, magnetic field, and boundary in the standard $H^s$ spaces. No additional regularity in the magnetic direction is required. The proof rests on a fourth order geometric energy inequality whose coefficients are controlled by these $H^s$ norms, the fixed geometric bounds, and the Taylor lower bound. A harmonic extension of the boundary normal provides the coefficient control needed at this regularity. We also prove that, near every admissible initial state and at each positive time in a common local existence interval, the Eulerian solution map is not uniformly continuous on any nonempty open subset of a sufficiently small data neighborhood. The construction combines localized magnetic oscillations prescribed at the observation time with time reversal and Galilean translations.
Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz-based convergence analysis with approximate weakly convex subdifferentials: bundle, quadratic penalty, and moving balls approximation methods
Jiefeng Xu; Guoyin Li; Ting Kei Pong

The Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) property has been widely used for establishing global sequential convergence and analyzing local convergence rate of optimization algorithms. Most existing analysis frameworks rely on the construction of a suitable KL potential function such that along the sequence generated, it admits sufficient descents and its exact subdifferentials are suitably controlled by successive changes of the iterates.
