Further, for each admissible height $s$, we construct $s$-residual intersections of complete intersection ideals and height three Gorenstein ideals that are set-theoretic complete intersections in any characteristic. Finally, we pose a general question of independent interest concerning the behaviour of arithmetic rank.
Zhuoni Chi; Shurui Liu; Ping Nie

We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.
Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations

We study optimization over a finite composition of implicit response maps generated by smooth potentials with strongly monotone signed gradients. This class includes chains mixing strongly convex minimization and strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses. We propose a fully first-order method based on recursively perturbed response solves. The central issue is stability under inexact response solves: a downstream adjoint error changes the perturbation vector of the next upstream perturbed problem. We establish coupled bounds for the forward response errors and backward errors in the scaled response differences whose coefficients remain bounded as the perturbation parameter $δ$ decreases. A triangular Lyapunov construction combines these bounds with the $O(δ)$ bias of the exact perturbation estimator. For the warm-started method with finitely many inner iterations, this gives $\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nablaΦ(x^k)\|^2 \leq O(K^{-1})+O(δ^2).$ Thus, for fixed problem data and finite depth, $δ=O(ε)$ yields an $O(ε^{-2})$ outer-iteration dependence. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.
Blow-up of damped semilinear wave equation with short range potential and critical power nonlinearity
Ikeda Masahiro; Tu Ziheng; Wang Chengbo

The present paper is devoted to the study of a semilinear wave equation with spatially dependent scattering damping and a short-range potential, with particular focus on determining the critical exponent for the power-type nonlinearity. By employing the test function method, we establish wave-type blow-up results and derive lifespan estimates at the critical level. The main contribution of this work lies in providing a uniform asymptotic analysis for a family of test functions, which is achieved through a detailed investigation of a parametric second-order elliptic equation. As a further novelty, we relax the radial symmetry condition conventionally imposed on the coefficients $D$ and $V$ by resorting to the comparison principle in conjunction with a monotone exhaustion argument.

We propose the Factorial Separation Conjecture (FSC), a strict strengthening of earlier factorial gap conjectures: \[ |n!-m^k|>n \] for all integers $n\ge8$ and $m,k\ge2$. The inequality excludes every displacement up to and including the factorial index. We prove the conjecture unconditionally for exponents divisible by three, for even exponents at least four, and for every exponent at least two when the largest prime divisor of the base is at most $n+2$. For exponents divisible by five, we prove the finite interval $8\le n\le1100$ and all sufficiently large indices, with an effective but uncomputed threshold. The conclusion for every $n\ge8$ and every exponent divisible by five is proved under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for a specified family of Dedekind zeta functions. Here GRH asserts that their nontrivial zeros have real part $1/2$. The arguments combine valuations, cyclotomic factorizations, cubic reciprocity, character estimates and explicit formulas. All finite comparisons are justified in the text. The general conjecture remains open.
The classification of taut surface singularities via representations from logarithmic vector fields

We study logarithmic vector fields on exceptional cycles through finite-dimensional representations and recover Laufer's classification of taut normal complex surface singularities. For graphs with two nodes, restriction maps define representations of a fixed quiver, with dimensions bounded independently of the number of components and their self-intersections. We identify restriction cohomology with an extension group and use interval decomposition to reduce its vanishing to interpolation on a rational chain. These calculations determine the classification conditions, and vanishing on every analytic realization proves sufficiency, including the nonrational cases. The obstruction cycles also give a uniform criterion: a graph is taut if and only if $H^1(5E,S_X|_{5E})=0$ for every analytic realization, where $S_X$ is the ambient logarithmic tangent bundle. We prove that five is the smallest positive integer for which this criterion holds for all graphs.
Phase diagram and fluctuations in the cubic mean field Ising model
Van Hao Can; Viet Tinh Dang

We study the cubic mean field Ising model with three body and two body interactions and an external field. Our main result is a complete classification of the global maximizers of the variational pressure in the full three-parameter region $(K,J,h)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$. We identify a coexistence surface with two nondegenerate global maximizers and a critical curve with a unique quartically degenerate maximizer; elsewhere the maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. This extends the phase diagrams previously obtained on two-parameter subfamilies \cite{CMO24,O24}. As applications of the general results in \cite{CR}, we give explicit magnetization fluctuation theorems and asymptotic distributions for one-parameter maximum likelihood estimators in the resulting regimes.
PMR-Aided Shifted-Pruning SCL-Flip Decoding for CRC-Aided Polar Codes
Niloufar Hosseinzadeh; Mohammad Morsali; Mohsen Moradi; Hessam Mahdavifar

We propose a posterior-mass rescue (PMR)-aided shifted-pruning SCL-flip decoder for CRC-aided polar codes. After CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) and differential-metric shifted-pruning recovery fail to find a CRC-valid candidate, PMR locally continues discarded prefixes stored during the initial CA-SCL pass, ranked by estimated posterior mass, without increasing the shifted-pruning retry budget. Simulation results for a (128, 64) code with the Reed-Muller (RM) rate profile and a (256, 128) code with the polarization-weight (PW) rate profile, both using an 11-bit CRC, show lower observed FER than SCLF-Diff (T = 15) and the considered literature baselines under the evaluated recovery budgets, with observed FER close to that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20). At the reported moderate and high SNRs, the average reconstruction-aware path-step count is within a few percent of that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20), while at 2.0 dB it is 9.4% and 4.3% higher for the two codes, respectively. The proposed decoder also has a larger worst-case path-step bound.
Cohomology and Representation Theory for Lie Superalgebras

In this paper the authors describe two general frameworks for studying algebraic supergroup and Lie superalgebra representations. These encompass the well-known rational representations for a reductive algebraic group and the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}$ for semisimple Lie algebras. Many of the important developments will be surveyed and a blueprint for these new approaches will be provided. The existence of odd elements simply add an additional layer of difficulty. The authors prove that the calculation of the sheaf cohomology in the super setting for the rational category is equivalent to understanding the Lie superalgebra cohomology. This generalizes the well-known fact that the classical Bott-Borel-Weil theorem is equivalent to Kostant's theorem. Furthermore, for the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}^{\mathfrak p}$ where ${\mathfrak p}$ is a principal parabolic, the authors show that the characters of simple modules can be obtained by looking at natural generalizations of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials given by extensions between simple modules and costandard modules arising from the underlying costandardly stratified category.
Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1

We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.
Which Immersions into Euclidean Space are Boundary Immersions?

Here we study the problem of whether a given codimension one immersion $f$ of a closed and connected manifold into Euclidean space can be extended to an equidimensional immersion $F$ of some compact manifold $M$ whose restriction to the boundary parameterizes the image $S$ of $f$. Such an extension $F$ exists if and only if (i) simple conditions on orientations and wrapping numbers are satisfied and (ii) a distinguished finite subset of the first cohomology of $S$ with coefficients in a certain sheaf of finite groups contains the preferred point.
Non-existence of negative weight derivations on Jacobian algebras
Bingyi Chen; Zhiwen Liu; Stephen S. -T. Yau; Huaiqing Zuo

Let $S=\mathbb K[x_1,\cdots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables with positive integer weights over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero. Let $f\in S$ be a weighted homogeneous polynomial such that the Jacobian algebra $$A=\left.S \middle/ \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\cdots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\right)\right.$$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K$-vector space. We prove that $A$ has no nonzero negative weight derivation, which confirms a conjecture of the third author. An immediate consequence of this conjecture is the micro-local characterization of quasi-homogeneous singularities.
Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations

We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.
Anytime-Valid Inference in Linear Models with Clustered Outcomes: Exact Multivariate Tests and Cluster-Robust Confidence Sequences

We extend anytime-valid inference for linear models from independent scalar outcomes to units that contribute a vector of dependent outcomes. We develop a parametric and a nonparametric treatment. For the Gaussian multivariate linear model with an unstructured error covariance, we derive a closed-form Bayes factor under the right-Haar prior and a matrix-normal mixture alternative and prove that it is an exact e-value at every sample size and a test martingale in the invariant filtration. To our knowledge, this Bayes factor is new in the generality considered here: a d x q coefficient matrix, nuisance regressors and an arbitrary fixed positive-definite prior precision under the right-Haar nuisance prior. It yields sequential Hotelling and MANOVA tests with exact confidence sequences. Under a common within-cluster design, the cluster-robust Wald statistic of a pooled regression is equal to Hotelling's T^2 statistic computed from the per-cluster least-squares summaries, giving an exact Gaussian benchmark with G-1 degrees of freedom. For general clustered population least-squares projections, the corresponding sandwich statistic is an asymptotic e-process, without Gaussian, common-design or linearity assumptions. Each treatment includes growth and first-order expected stopping-time results; under stronger regularity, direct comparisons of expected log evidence identify a fixed mixture precision that maximizes expected log growth through constant order within a specified family, for a specified frequentist alternative. Applied to randomized experiments with several outcomes, the robust procedure gives asymptotically anytime-valid joint tests, confidence ellipsoids and simultaneous confidence sequences for the vector of average treatment effects from ordinary least-squares estimates and cluster-robust standard errors.
Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow

We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.
Negative Values of Wahl's Second Chern Number for Normal Surface Singularities

We disprove Wahl's 1993 vanishing conjecture, open for more than thirty years, which asserts that $c_2^w(X)=0$ for every nonquotient normal surface singularity. Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with a nontrivial involution having $r>0$ fixed points, and put $d=2g(C)-2$. If $d>r$, the union of the diagonal and the graph of the involution in $C\times C$ has negative definite intersection matrix and can be analytically contracted to a normal surface singularity $(X,o)$. A direct relative Chern-class computation and Wahl's residue formula give $c_2^w(X)=-r(d+r)/(d-r)$. An explicit curve of genus four gives $c_2^w(X)=-4$. Branched double covers of a fixed curve of genus two yield examples with $c_2^w(X_m)=-2m(m+1)$, so these values are unbounded below. We give the construction and intersection calculations in detail, as well as a line-bundle filtration realizing the negative value.
On solutions to tropical Monge-Ampère equations
Omid Amini; Matthieu Piquerez; Lyuhui Wu

This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and Kähler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, θ)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical Kähler form $θ$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Ampère equations on Berkovich spaces.
Mixed Unfitted finite element approximation of band structures in photonic crystals
Yuyan Zou; Luke G. Bennetts; Hailong Guo

Photonic crystals are periodic dielectric structures whose optical properties are characterized by Maxwell eigenvalue problems with discontinuous material coefficients. For arbitrarily shaped inclusions, their numerical solution remains challenging due to costly mesh generation and remeshing as the geometry changes. In this paper, we address this challenge by developing a mixed unfitted finite element method based on the Floquet-Bloch transform. Our method uses a uniform background mesh independent of the inclusion geometry, thereby avoiding interface-fitted meshing and allowing us to impose the periodic boundary condition through a direct identification of degrees of freedom. A key feature of our construction is that the resulting finite element pairs preserve the de Rham commuting relation for the shifted operator. This structure enables us to establish an inf-sup condition uniformly with respect to the cut position and, in particular, to rule out spurious modes. We further establish optimal convergence of the eigenvalues and eigenspaces, with constants independent of both the mesh size and the position of the interface. Finally, we present extensive numerical experiments in two and three dimensions to validate our theoretical results and demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method.
Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures

Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.
Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances

If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.
Geunyoung Kim; Sam Nelson; Puttipong Pongtanapaisan

We introduce a new family of weighted quiver-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and link, surface-knots and surface-links, and immersed surface-knots and surface-links associated to finite biquandles. We derive several polynomial invariants from these quivers via decategorification. We provide examples to illustrate the computation of the invariant as well as toy examples showing tables of invariant values for small biquandles.
Minimal immersions by first eigenfunctions of Riemann surfaces with large conformal automorphism groups. The Klein quartic

Minimal immersions of closed surfaces into spheres by first eigenfunctions play an important role in both the theory of minimal surfaces and spectral geometry. In this paper, we establish the existence of equivariant conformal minimal immersions of this type for Hurwitz surfaces and other families of %Riemann surfaces with large automorphism group. Finally, we explicitly construct a conformal minimal equivariant immersion of the Klein quartic into the unit sphere $S^{7}$ by first eigenfunctions. Ths immersion is a natural candidate for maximizing the normalized $λ_1$ among closed genus-3 surfaces.
Equivariant deformation theory and deformations of homogeneous varieties

We show that, in characteristic $p$, almost all projective homogeneous varieties under a reductive group and with non-reduced stabilizer do not lift to characteristic $p^2$. To this end, first we develop a general framework for equivariant deformation theory, leading to practical criteria ensuring that the deformations of a scheme come with deformations of a group scheme action. Second, we establish a formula to compute the cohomology of equivariant vector bundles over projective homogeneous varieties with non-reduced stabilizer, enabling us to determine the $G$-module structure of the first cohomology groups of their tangent bundles.
Two Generalizations of the G_0 Dichotomy
We give classical proofs of the generalizations of the $\mathbb{G}_0$ dichotomy to $κ$-Souslin digraphs and uniformly analytic sequences of digraphs indexed by $κ^{\mathbb{N}}$.
Infinitesimally polar Killing foliations via geometric resolutions
Francisco C. Caramello Jr.; Laura Ribeiro dos Santos

We establish the strong Molino conjecture for complete infinitesimally polar singular Riemannian foliations and identify their Molino sheaves with those of their geometric resolutions. The resolution preserves basic and equivariant basic cohomology and transverse curvature bounds. These comparisons yield orbifold models and approximations of leaf-closure spaces, Euler localization, closed-leaf existence and Euler positivity under positive curvature, and transverse sphere theorems. Maximal defect gives a closed-ball leaf-closure space. Further applications include fundamental-group growth bounds and closedness under nonpositive transverse Ricci curvature that is negative definite at one regular point.
Integrable distortion I: Weil--Petersson circle homeomorphisms and the Schoen conjecture

A circle homeomorphism $β:\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is Weil--Petersson if it has a quasiconformal disk extension whose Beltrami coefficient is square integrable for hyperbolic area. We minimise the hyperbolic anti-holomorphic energy \[ E_2(h)=\int_\mathbb{D}η(h)|h_{\bar w}|^2,dA, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \int_\mathbb{D}\frac{|μ_f|^2}{1-|μ_f|^2},dA_η,\quad f=h^{-1}, \] over all monotone Sobolev maps with boundary values $β$. For Weil--Petersson data, the unique minimiser is a real analytic hyperbolic harmonic diffeomorphism, globally quasiconformal and asymptotically conformal, with an explicit dilatation bound in terms of any admissible barrier's energy. We prove that a circle homeomorphism is Weil--Petersson if and only if it admits a finite-distortion homeomorphic extension satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{K}_F-1),dA_η<\infty. \] For every $p>1$, the boundary values of a finite-distortion homeomorphism satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}|μ_F|^p(1-|μ_F|^2)^{-p_*/2},dA_η<\infty \] lie in Guo's $p$-integrable Teichm"uller space $T^p$. A capacity estimate for boundary moduli for the quasisymmetric ratio yields a derivative-free characterisation of $T^p$, essentially Bishop's theorem when $p=2$. The minimum defines a M"obius-invariant boundary energy, quantitatively comparable to the weighted square norm of the minimiser's Hopf differential. For arbitrary quasisymmetric data, we prove Markovi'c's theorem (the Schoen conjecture) by approximation with our smooth quadratic minimisers. Mori's theorem and the mean-value property of a logarithm verify the averaged-distance hypothesis in Riestenberg--Smillie's interior comparison, giving explicit displacement, energy-density and dilatation bounds in terms of the quasisymmetry constant. The nonquadratic ($p\neq2$) theory is developed in Part~II.
Elliptic closed geodesics on non-negatively curved Finsler manifolds

In this paper, we prove that if a compact simply-connected manifold $(M,F)$ with a bumpy irreversible Finsler metric $F$ whose flag curvature $K$ satisfies $K\ge 0$ and $H^*(M;\Q)\cong T_{d,n+1}(x)$ for some $d\in2\N$ and $n\in\N$ carries exactly $\frac{dn(n+1)}{2}$ (the number of closed geodesics in Katok's example) closed geodesics, then there are at least $2$ irrationally elliptic closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

We introduce a relational Alexandroff topology associated with the strong Goldbach conjecture on the set of even integers greater than or equal to six. The construction is induced by a multivalued map encoding Goldbach representations and leads naturally to a notion of relational reachability. For arbitrary binary relations, we show that singleton closures coincide with reachable sets and that the common intersection of all singleton closures consists exactly of the globally reachable points. In the Goldbach setting, this yields a topological characterization of the conjecture in terms of the distinguished point \(6\). In particular, the strong Goldbach conjecture is equivalent to the associated relational space being non-\(wR_0\) and connected. We also obtain compactness and supercompactness criteria in terms of the set of possible Goldbach exceptions.
On Huppert's $ρ$-$σ$ conjecture for primes in the orders of elements

Let $G$ be a finite group, let $ρ(G)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $|G|$, and let $σ(G)$ be the maximal number of distinct prime divisors of the order of an element of $G$. Let $ρ(n)=\max\{ρ(G) \mid G \text{ solvable}, σ(G)=n\}$. We prove that $ρ(n)\le 4n-1+π(2n)$ for all $n$, and, with the help of a computer, that $ρ(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\le 16$. In particular, $ρ(n)\le\lfloor 9n/2\rfloor+2$ and $ρ(n)\le (101/22)n$ for all $n$, and $ρ(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\ge 58$. This improves the bound $ρ(n)\le (17/3)n$ due to Yang, and it shows that the bound $ρ(n)\le 5n$ stated by Bellotti, Keller and Trudgian holds, although its original proof contains a gap. Moreover, we show that $ρ(n)\ge 3n$ for all $n\ge 4$, which proves one half of a conjecture of the second author stating that $ρ(n)=3n$ for $n\ge 4$. We also derive a consequence for character codegrees and, conditionally, for arbitrary finite groups. The proofs of the main results do not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
A Reduced-Order Model for the High-Field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System Based on a Micro-Macro Decomposition

We develop a projection-based reduced-order model for the high-field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. Based on a micro-macro decomposition, the proposed Micro-ROM applies proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-Galerkin reduction only to the microscopic fluctuation while retaining the macroscopic density on the full spatial grid. The field-dependent Maxwellian and collision operator introduce additional computational costs that cannot be eliminated by Galerkin projection alone. To remove the dependence on the velocity-grid resolution during online simulations, we approximate the projected Maxwellian terms using precomputed Chebyshev expansions of functions of the local electric field and exploit a separable discretization of the collision operator to assemble the reduced collision matrix exactly from precomputed blocks. A first-order implicit-explicit scheme is employed to evolve the reduced coefficients and the density. The resulting method conserves discrete mass and formally recovers a discretization of the limiting high-field model as $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$. Its online computational cost per time step is independent of the velocity-grid resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across a range of parameters, including the high-field regime.

We prove that given an analytic supermanifold $X$ over a complete field on which the additive supergroup $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ of super-dimension $0|n$ acts freely (in an appropriate sense), the quotient $X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ exists as an analytic supermanifold, and the canonical morphism $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is an $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. A stronger version of this result is proven for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds, whereby $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is a trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. Previously, Polishchuk [18] established an algebro-geometric analogue, which proves that a superscheme $X$ with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action gives rise to a locally trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-torsor $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$. This result is proven here in an alternative, elementary way. To all of these, a Hopf-algebraic approach is effectively employed.
On simplicial maps with non-zero Hopf invariant

In general, it is interesting to investigate the complexity of simplicial maps under various topological constraints. In this paper, we consider maps between (triangulated oriented rational homology) manifolds with non-zero Hopf invariant and establish bounds on the simplicial complexity of the fiber of a regular point. The lower bound, which is cubic in the dimension, is proved via a refinement of a theorem of S. Eilenberg. The upper bound is notable in that it is uniform with respect to the Hopf invariant.
Pablo D. Carrasco; Davi Obata; Radu Saghin; Jiagang Yang

We study the statistical properties of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with a two-dimensional center exhibiting mixed behavior, without assuming a dominated splitting inside the center. We introduce the notion of an expanding on average for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism and, under a center jacobian assumption, we prove the existence of finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures, and show the strong positive recurrence property, which implies that each SRB measure, up to a period, satisfies exponential decay of correlations, among other strong statistical laws. We apply our results to several examples.
Self-Supervised In-Context Operator Learning for Optimal Mixing in Incompressible Flows
Weiwei Hu; Rongjie Lai; Ziqian Li

We develop a self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing in incompressible flows, aimed at overcoming the computational limitations of classical PDE-constrained optimal control. The objective is to design velocity fields that efficiently homogenize a passive scalar while minimizing kinetic energy, quantified through the $\dot H^{-1}(Ω)$ mix-norm. Classical methods solve a separate optimal control problem for each initial condition using iterative forward-adjoint procedures, leading to substantial computational costs and limited scalability. In contrast, we propose to learn the solution operator that maps initial scalar fields to optimal mixing controls directly. The proposed self-supervised method does not require access to supervised labels, thereby significantly reducing the data-generation burden of supervised operator-learning methods. Our framework integrates a Lagrangian reformulation of the transport equation with a transformer-based neural operator architecture. The transport dynamics are represented through characteristic ODEs, enabling particle-based Monte Carlo optimization, while the learned velocity field is parameterized in a divergence-free spectral basis enforcing incompressibility and no-penetration conditions exactly. Numerical experiments on parametric families of initial conditions in two and three spatial dimensions demonstrate robust generalization to unseen regimes and approximately exponential decay of the mix-norm. The learned controls also transfer consistently to independent Eulerian finite-volume simulations, validating the physical fidelity of the learned operator. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing and among the first data-driven approaches for optimal mixing in fully three-dimensional incompressible flows.

We show that the index of a uniformly random seaweed meander satisfies a central limit theorem and is asymptotically equidistributed with respect to any modulus. We also extend work by Archer, Geary, and Laudone on the enumeration of seaweed meanders whose compositions have restricted parts. Finally, we give a connection to billiards in triangular shapes, which is related to a result of Eu, Fu, and Hsu.
Energy Estimate and Convergence of Weak Solutions of a Class of Nonlinear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
Adriana Neumann; Patrícia Gonçalves; Maria Chiara Riciiuti; Oslenne Araújo

We establish strong convergence in $L^2([0,T]\times[0,1])$ of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear PDEs with Robin boundary conditions to weak solutions of the corresponding Neumann and Dirichlet problems as the boundary parameter $κ$ tends to $0$ and $\infty$, respectively. Our approach relies on a particle system whose hydrodynamic limits yield the Robin problem for each fixed $κ>0$. An energy estimate derived from the microscopic stochastic dynamics provides the key bounds for passing to the subsequent limits $κ\to0$ and $κ\to\infty$, thereby obtaining the Neumann and Dirichlet problems.
We present some results concerning the geometry and dynamics of closed locally symmetric spacetimes.

We give a theta-function and projective-geometric account of the four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras. We define a family of quadratic algebras by declaring that their relations are precisely the two-tensors vanishing on the graph of a translation automorphism on a quartic complex elliptic curve and the vertex pairs where the vertices are the singular points of the four singular quadrics that contain it. We then use Jacobi's addition formulas for theta functions to produce a set of six explicit relations that coincide with Sklyanin's RLL-relations associated to Baxter's elliptic solutions to the 2 x 2 Yang-Baxter equation. We use the geometric definition to show that these algebras coincide with Feigin and Odesskii's four-dimensional elliptic algebras. Our approach agrees with that of Rains-Ruijsenaars theta function perspective on the four-dimensional Sklyanin agebras. For example, the rank-two secant-line relations of Levasseur-Smith coincide with their two-variable theta function relations. We give explicit theta-function formulas for the degree-two central elements, previously obtained by Levassuer-Smith, that annihilate various families of line modules.
Heights of small CM cycles on Unitary Shimura Varieties

We compute the heights of small CM cycles on unitary Shimura varieties for general choices of the one-dimensional Hermitian subspace $W$ defining the embedding. The formula contains the logarithmic derivative of a quadratic Hecke $L$-function and explicit local terms depending on the choice of $W$. We prove this formula and an arithmetic Siegel--Weil identity by comparing the holomorphic projection of a mixed theta--Eisenstein derivative with arithmetic intersections of special divisors.
On quandles with isomorphic enveloping groups
We give a method to construct two injective connected finite quandles of different cardinal with isomorphic enveloping groups.
The blow-up of the cubic fourfold along eight planes is Fano

We prove that the blow-up Z_m of a smooth cubic fourfold along m <= 8 planes, pairwise meeting at distinct points and satisfying explicit generality conditions, is a smooth Fano fourfold of Picard rank rho(Z_m) = m+1 <= 9; in particular, we obtain three new families of smooth Fano fourfolds with rho > 6 that are not a product of surfaces. Complementary to this result, we show that a smooth cubic fourfold as above exists. Moreover, we study the birational geometry of Z_m and show that it corresponds exactly to that of a smooth del Pezzo surfaces S_m, obtained as the blow-up of P^2 along m <= 8 points in general position. Namely, Z_m and S_m have isomorphic Mori cones, pseudo-effective cones with same Mori chamber decomposition, and there is a one-to-one correspondence between the contractions of Z_m and the contractions of S_m. Lastly, we study the anticanonical linear system of Z_m and prove that it is basepoint free if and only if m <= 7. For m = 8 and a special configuration of planes, we show that the anticanonical base locus Bs(|-K_{Z_8}|) has dimension 2 and contains a smooth del Pezzo surface of degree 1.
Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier-Stokes flows with rotationally invariant curl of the force
Benjamin Ingimarson; Igor Kukavica; Qi Xu

We answer a question of Constantin, Ignatova, and Vicol concerning regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions to the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations. For suitable weak solutions that are smooth before a terminal time and have a force uniformly bounded in $C_x^2$, we replace spatial analyticity of the force by rotational invariance of its curl. Under the same anisotropic Type II bounds on the angular mean and exact axial symmetry on a possibly collapsing core, the solution is axisymmetric on the entire cylinder and regular at the putative singular point. No time regularity or quantitative lower bound on the core radius is required. The proof combines unique continuation for linear Stokes systems with a Baire category argument and the axisymmetric regularity theorem due to Constantin, Ignatova, and Vicol.
Stability and Stabilization of Kronecker-Sum-Coupled Multilinear Systems
Ziqin He; Ruoying Wang; Shenghan Mei; Yidan Mei; Xin Mao; Can Chen

Coupled dynamical systems with multi-dimensional state structures arise in many applications such as spatiotemporal processes and large-scale interconnected systems. However, existing studies primarily focus on matrix-based coupled systems or tensor-based dynamical systems without couplings. The properties of coupled tensor-based systems remain largely unexplored. In this article, we study Kronecker-sum-coupled multilinear systems under the transform-based tensor product framework. We establish fundamental tensor spectral properties showing that stability can be characterized through lower-dimensional subsystem dynamics together with slice-wise matrix stability in the transform domain. We further develop optimization conditions for state-feedback stabilization and show that the stabilization problem can be decomposed into independent subsystem problems. Finally, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed framework and demonstrate its substantial computational advantages over unfolding-based approaches using both synthetic systems and multi-inertia motor systems.
Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
Mats Boij; Juan C. Migliore; Rosa M. Miró-Roig; Uwe Nagel

For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.
The Bourgain, Brezis, Mironescu localization for deterministic obstacle problems

We study the asymptotic behaviour of families of fractional energies normalized according to the Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula and defined on functions satisfying a pinning condition on possibly aperiodic families of small obstacles. The result of the simultaneous limit depends crucially on the critical rescaling chosen for the obstacles.
Partially Adaptive Robust Optimization for Uncertain Fluid Processing Networks
Roi Ben-Gigi; Evgeny Shindin; and Shimrit Shtern

This paper studies the problem of controlling fluid approximations of processing networks under uncertainty. Classical robust formulations for such models rely on static (here-and-now) control decisions that must remain feasible for all realizations of uncertainty, often leading to highly conservative solutions. We propose a partially adaptive robust optimization framework that incorporates observed system information into the control policy at the planning point, enabling less conservative and more responsive decisions while retaining worst-case guarantees. Our approach begins by modeling the fluid network dynamics as a Separated Continuous Linear Program (SCLP) in the server-effort formulation. We introduce continuous-time extensions of the budgeted uncertainty set and develop three families of uncertainty structures appropriate for fluid-flow systems. For each family, we derive the corresponding robust counterpart. Since these robust counterparts include uncertainty in the objective, they cannot be solved directly by the classical SCLP--Simplex method. To address this challenge, we develop a hybrid algorithm that integrates an extended SCLP framework with the Saddle-Point Frank--Wolfe (SP--FW) method. This hybrid approach combines tractable continuous-time optimization with efficient saddle-point updates, yielding feasible and near-optimal partially adaptive robust solutions. The resulting methodology advances robust fluid control by enabling uncertainty-aware, dynamically informed decision policies while preserving computational tractability.
Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families

We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_λ)$, $λ\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(λ,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $ν(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $ν(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_λ(z)=z^d+λ$, $λ\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.
Degree Stability of Parallel Greedy Matching in Random Graphs

We study a natural synchronous greedy matching process in Erdős-Rényi random graphs $\mathbb{G}(n,p)$ and give a rigorous analysis of this parallel stochastic dynamics. The process evolves as follows: in each round, every unmatched vertex proposes to a uniformly random neighbour, and mutually proposing pairs are matched and removed from the graph, after which the process repeats on the residual graph. We consider the density regime $p=Θ(\log^{1+ε} n/n)$ for any constant $ε>0$, which lies just above the threshold for the existence of a perfect matching. We show that, with high probability, for $Θ(\log^{1+ε} n)$ rounds, every unmatched vertex keeps a constant fraction of its initial degree in the residual graph, simultaneously for all vertices and all rounds. By then, the process has matched a constant fraction of the vertices. Our analysis tracks fine-grained invariants that control the evolution of individual vertex degrees, rather than directly tracking the global degree distribution. At the local level, we analyze the per-round degree loss of a vertex via a neighbourhood-exposure martingale. We show that structural sparsity of $\mathbb{G}(n,p)$ yields $O(1)$ variance and thus the per-round degree loss is strongly concentrated around its conditional expectation. At the global level, these local concentration bounds control the increments of a martingale tracking cumulative degree loss over many rounds, allowing us to show that vertex degrees remain stable for $Ω(\log^{1+ε} n)$ rounds.
A Method for Linearization of Systems of Quadratic Equations
A. A. Pak; A. S. Pak

Integrating physical conservation laws into deep neural architectures remains a central SciML challenge. Soft-penalty approaches, including many PINNs, may be sensitive to loss weighting and optimization; generic DEQ and implicit-layer solvers may require instance-dependent iteration counts. We study a norm-linearization scheme for networked systems with linear continuity constraints and nonlinear quadratic or power-law energy balances. We derive sharp universal and finite-$n$ bounds on relative variance and, via the weighted Kantorovich inequality, relate them to worst-case single-step squared-norm distortion when target and operating states have a bounded multiplicative ratio. Euler's theorem shows that the scheme is Newton's method for degree-one norm differences $u_i(\mathbf{x})-v_i(\mathbf{x})=0$. Recasting raw degree-$α$ balances as norm differences removes radial curvature, yields a degree-zero homogeneous Jacobian, eliminates the affine Newton term, and row-equilibrates the loop Jacobian at equilibrium. Under regularity and nonsingularity assumptions, this gives local quadratic convergence for Darcy-Weisbach ($α=2$) and Hazen-Williams ($α=1.852$) models. We implement dynamic sign partitioning in a FlowDEQ layer using a reduced incidence matrix and implicit-function adjoint differentiation.
TIGER: Tunable-Geometry Accelerated Gradient Sliding with Adaptive Safeguards under Similarity
Darina M. Dvinskikh; Anton G. Novitskii; Ewsey R. Obzherin; Alexander V. Gasnikov

We study distributed composite optimization under function similarity when synchronized gradient queries dominate local computation. We propose TIGER, an accelerated gradient-sliding method in problem-adapted Bregman geometry. The method applies to constrained non-Euclidean domains, allows the communicated correction term to be nonconvex, and terminates each local subproblem using a computable stationarity residual. Each iteration reuses one synchronized correction gradient during the local solve and makes a second query to construct the composite subgradient for the mirror step. Under relative strong convexity and cocoercivity of the stabilized model error, the communication complexity is $O((1+\sqrt{δ_ω/μ})\log(1/\varepsilon))$, where $μ$ is the relative strong-convexity parameter and $δ_ω$ is a geometry-adjusted similarity parameter. The analysis recovers the Hessian-similarity rate in Hilbert geometry and provides an explicit finite bound on $δ_ω$ in entropy geometry on a truncated simplex. We also introduce Adaptive TIGER, which selects the stabilization coefficient and the similarity estimate during the run. Under uniform backtracking bounds, the adaptive method has the same asymptotic communication order as fixed-parameter TIGER, including the queries spent on backtracking. Numerical experiments compare Adaptive TIGER with several applicable first-order methods on entropic Wasserstein barycenter problems using the Fashion-MNIST dataset.
Torelli theorem for the moduli spaces of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves
Soham Ghosh; Ting Gong; Max Lieblich

We prove Torelli theorems for moduli space of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic $\neq 2$. A twisted Hitchin construction recovers the curve in higher rank and degree, with partial recovery of the twisting class. For rank two with trivial determinant, we recover the curve and the Brauer class from the moduli stack through an ordered Kummer cover and its polarized Jacobian torsor. For odd determinant on hyperelliptic curves, residual gerbes give a relative Desale--Ramanan construction without an actual determinant line bundle over the ground field. An intrinsic polarized Fano torsor recovers the curve and the class, and a corrected polarization obstruction recovers the determinant gerbe. We also give a twisted Newstead construction in genus two, with an explicit descent condition for its converse, and period--index applications. This is the second part in a series of two papers.

We extend the recent work of Caster--Guyer--Samper (2026+) to establish a combinatorial interpretation of the $\textbf{cd}$-index for all $S$-partitionable posets, which includes all polytopes and $S$-shellable spheres. This interpretation is inductive on rank, but does not require passing to the order complex of the poset. We also provide topological interpretations of each $\textbf{cd}$-monomial. Furthermore, we establish a recurrence on the $\textbf{cd}$-indices of shelling components of the $d$-simplex that does not require the use of André permutations, a unimodality result for $\textbf{cd}$-words ending in $\textbf{d}$ for shelling components of the $d$-simplex and the $d$-cube, and provide two families of subdivisions of the boundary of the $d$-simplex whose sequence of $\textbf{cd}$-indices is unbounded on all but the monomial $\textbf{c}^{d+1}$ and all but the two monomials $\textbf{c}^{d+1}$ and $\textbf{d}\textbf{c}^{d-1}$.
From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory

Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.
An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality

In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $τ$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $τ$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $τ$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.
KernelPack-JAX: a meshless differentiable GPU framework for node generation and forward and inverse PDE problems
Alberto Cattaneo; M. Keith Ballard; Robert M. Kirby; Grady B. Wright; Varun Shankar

We present KernelPack-JAX, a meshless, differentiable, GPU framework in JAX for solving forward and inverse PDE problems in domains whose boundaries, including internal obstacles, are given only by samples of their smooth pieces. Our node generator is based on a new stacked representation of piecewise-smooth boundaries, in which a parametric partition of unity of each smooth piece induces the supports of a curl-free implicit partition of unity of the whole boundary. This representation keeps the edges and corners of the boundary and classifies every point of space without a global fit. Boundary and interior nodes are then selected by a parallel greedy independent-set algorithm that reproduces sequential Poisson-disk sampling exactly. We discretize elliptic and parabolic problems with radial basis function-generated finite differences (RBF-FD) on stencils selected by a new visibility heuristic to avoid crossing the boundary, with ghost nodes for the boundary conditions. In addition, our framework exposes a GPU sparse direct solver to JAX as a differentiable linear solve, so that Jacobians of time-dependent problems cost a small multiple of a forward solve. We derive error estimates that separate consistency from stability and bound the parameter error by the forward error. We demonstrate high-order convergence for Darcy flow, reaction-diffusion, and advection-diffusion in 2D and 3D domains, including one with an internal obstacle, and show that the recovered parameters largely follow the forward errors. We also present timings for every stage.
On elements of degree $g$ in the separating semigroup of a real curve of genus $g$
G. B. Mikhalkin; S. Yu. Orevkov

Let $C$ be a separating real algebraic curve of genus $g$ whose real locus consists of $r$ components and let $S=\mathrm{Sep}(C)$ be its separating semigroup. An element $δ\in S$ is called extendable if $δ+\mathbb N_0^r\subset S$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{n\in\mathbb Z\mid n\ge 0\}$. We prove that an element of $S$ is extendable if it is realizable by a separating mobile divisor of degree $g$ and projective rank 1.
Acceleration of Generalized Conditional Gradient Methods

We develop an adaptive acceleration of generalized conditional gradient methods for convex objectives with a strongly convex regularizer. A computable primal--dual residual certifies Lyapunov decrease without evaluating the regularizer or any Hessian. Each iteration accepts a balanced accelerated trial when the residual is nonpositive; otherwise it takes a mirror-descent step with doubling backtracking and sets the auxiliary parameter explicitly from the dual decrease and the stopping gap. Under uniform strong-convexity and smoothness bounds on the relevant sublevel set, the method converges globally at a linear rate. Near a nondegenerate minimizer, balanced trials pass above a fixed curvature threshold. The adaptive curvature updates then guarantee a positive fraction of accelerated steps and a local accelerated rate. The method applies directly to entropically regularized Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) steps whose energies contain nonlocal interaction terms with nondiagonal Hessians. Experiments on JKO steps for granular media and for Poisson--Nernst--Planck systems, in one and three dimensions, show that the method reduces both oracle calls and computing time by a large fraction compared with generalized conditional gradient methods with fixed or adaptive step sizes.
Topological Quantum Gates on FCIs with Bounded Quantum Geometry

Two-band 2D fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) have recently been shown, in principle, to admit unusual anyonic order, associated with Bloch Hopfions localized in momentum space. Here we show that bounding the integrated quantum metric along one primitive Brillouin-zone cycle may refine this topological order to $|C|$ distinct braiding observables, cyclically permuted by lattice translations, for Chern numbers $|C| > 1$. The cyclic structure entails mildly non-abelian braiding phases and otherwise matches the spectral flow exhibited by the FCI's hybrid Wannier states, with the metric bound equivalently a bound on the states' real-space spread. We give a classification of quantum gates in principle implementable on this topological order; among them we find the non-Clifford T-gate and the non-Clifford entangling CCZ-gate. This points to novel pathways to fault-tolerant quantum processes within the known orbital structure of FCIs, potentially informing experimental searches towards hardware for future topological quantum computers.
\textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer

We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.
Improvement of the Crossing Lemma for the odd-crossing number

A graph is called $1$-planar if it can be drawn in the plane so that every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. It is known that the maximum number of edges of $1$-planar graphs is $4n-8$. We prove the following generalization. A graph is $1$-odd-planar if it can be drawn in the plane so that every edge is crossed {\em an odd number of times} by at most one other edge. We show that the maximum number of edges of $1$-odd-planar graphs is also $4n-8$. As a consequence, we improve the constant coefficient in the Crossing Lemma for the odd-crossing number.
Advancing the Theory of Sheffer Sequences via Dual Padé Rational Approximants

Sheffer sequences offer an operational framework that unifies a wide range of classical polynomial families. In this article, a rational approximation is developed for both the amplitude and the delta-operator symbol in the exponential generating function. The resulting Padé Sheffer polynomials are shown, within the umbral calculus framework, to retain the Sheffer structure. Explicit operational representations are obtained, together with finite-order differential recurrences and closed-form connection constants characterizing the deviation from the underlying polynomial family. An important consequence of the construction is that rational generating indicators reduce the usual transcendental Lagrange inversion problem to a finite multinomial computation. The framework also suggests an interpretation in terms of weighted finite automata, linking polynomial constructions with state-space dynamics for unbounded combinatorial partitions.
An A-B-C Coordinate Encoding for Exact Boundary-Cycle Extraction on Hexagonal Lattices

We study an integer-coordinate encoding of boundary incidences for finite subsets of the regular hexagonal tiling. Each selected cell contributes six ordered records with endpoints in two role-distinguished classes, point and tail. Identical records from neighboring cells cancel, and the surviving records form a disjoint union of cycles, including the exterior boundaries of disconnected components and the boundaries of holes. We derive the actual even- and odd-row record formulas from the A--B--C transforms used in Hexagones 2.0, prove exact shared-edge identities and the global role-qualified incidence structure, and thereby obtain an unconditional correctness theorem for the abstract coordinate construction. We compare the encoding with an independent exact cube-coordinate half-edge hashing implementation, proving an incidence isomorphism and checking 504 finite regions. We give an expected-linear-time indexed algorithm and distinguish it from the historical fixed-capacity C traversal, whose sentinel and closure conventions do not inherit the theorem automatically. The claim is a compact coordinate realization of a known planar boundary principle, not historical priority or a new three-axis lattice.
Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets

We propose to model singular data clouds by subanalytic sets, and develop an approach to semi-supervised learning in this setting. It relies on a Morrey-type embedding for Sobolev spaces relative to globally subanalytic measures with possibly singular support. As an illustration, we present a greedy method based on a Monte Carlo approximation of the Sobolev norm of the candidate solutions. We report numerical experiments on point clouds sampled from real algebraic varieties, as well as a test on a classification problem based on MNIST images downsampled into $7\times7$.
Mixing time of the tranvection walk on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$

We consider a Markov chain on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$, the space of $n \times n$ matrices with determinant $1$ and entries in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p$ a prime number. At every time step, the chain updates by adding one row (or its negation) to another. By way of a log-Sobolev inequality, we show the mixing time of this chain is at most of order $O(n^2p^2(\log n +\log \log p))$.
Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits

Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $Σ$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $Σ$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $Σ$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $Σ$, we identify the capacity deficit of $Σ$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $Σ$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.
Distinctness and Algebraic Degrees of Inverted Kloosterman Sums

We study the distinctness and algebraic degrees of inverted Kloosterman sums over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_p$. For each $d\geq 2$, we prove that the $(d-1)$-dimensional sums over $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ are equal precisely when their parameters are Frobenius conjugate, provided that $p\equiv 1\pmod d$, $p>2d+1$, and $p$ does not divide the nonzero integer $2(d+1)^d-\binom{2d}{d}^2$. For two-dimensional sums over $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$, the same conclusion holds for $2\leq r\leq 5$, $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, and $p>3r+1$. In both cases we determine the algebraic degree of every sum in terms of the minimal polynomial of its parameter. The proof combines a cyclic-carry analysis of a Gauss-sum expansion with the recovery of power traces from a formal logarithm.
Jonah Berean-Dutcher; Clay Cordova; Julio Parra-Martinez; Richard Tuddenham

We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.
Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
Nanda Poddar; Debabrata Das; Suman Chakraborty

Longitudinal dispersion in a yielding fluid depends on the velocity distribution and on how the flow is maintained. We study a neutral tracer in pressure-assisted electrokinetic and magnetohydrodynamic flow of a Casson fluid through a slit microchannel. The nonlinear stress and velocity equations determine the yielded layers, the unyielded core and the axial flow. Mei's multiple-scale homogenization of the advection-diffusion equation then separates transverse relaxation, mean drift and longitudinal spreading, yielding the Taylor-Aris auxiliary problem and effective diffusivity. An exact pressure-driven solution gives cubic decay of the mean velocity and eighth-power decay of the dispersion enhancement near flow arrest. Under fixed pressure and electrical forcing, increasing the yield parameter from $Y=0$ to $0.7$ moves the optimum Hartmann number from $Ha_p=0.696$ to $2.634$, while the corresponding normalized diffusivity decreases from $D_T^{\mathrm C}=1.454$ to $1.015$. At fixed mean throughput and $Ha_p=1$, the trend reverses: $D_T^{\mathrm C}$ increases from $1.000433$ to $1.002311$. The homogenized energy identity traces this difference to the velocity departure from the sectional mean, including that within the unyielded core. Analytical limiting solutions, direct concentration calculations, numerical convergence studies and a coupled Casson shear test support the reduced-flow predictions. An electrolyte-based dimensional assessment identifies the magnetic optima as theoretical forcing states for representative aqueous microchannels. These results are relevant to predicting longitudinal tracer spreading in microchannels carrying fluids with a yield stress, whether pressure or throughput is controlled.
Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers

We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.
Categorical Torelli theorem for smooth Fano varieties

Let $X$ be a smooth Fano variety and $H$ an ample line bundle with $-K_X=rH$ and $r\le\dim X-2$. We prove that the appropriately defined Kuznetsov component of $X$ with respect to $H$, together with its rotation functor, determines $(X,H)$ when $H$ is very ample, and more generally when $H$ is globally generated and the image of the morphism defined by $|H|$ has a hypersurface as projective dual. As a consequence we prove Perry's conjecture, which predicts that a smooth Fano variety $X$ is determined up to isomorphism by the orthogonal complement $\mathcal{O}_X^{\perp}$ of its structure sheaf in $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$, for all smooth Fano varieties of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundle, and more generally with globally generated anticanonical bundle whose image has a hypersurface as dual. We also prove it when a multiple $-qK_X$ is very ample and the corresponding embedding is cut out by equations of degree at most $(\mathrm{dim} X-1)/q$. The idea is to read off $X$ from its hyperplane sections. We show that the Kuznetsov component with its rotation functor contains the residual categories of all hyperplane sections of $X$, singular ones included. The sections whose categories are not smooth form the projective dual of $X$, and classical projective duality recovers $X$. When $H$ is not very ample, the nodes of a single tangent hyperplane section, defined over a function field and detected by its singularity category, recover $X$ as a finite cover of its image. Applications include Fano hypersurfaces, all prime Fano threefolds of index one and genus at least three, cyclic covers of quadrics, Fano complete intersections and Gushel--Mukai varieties.
Polynomial bounds for the stability of associated primes of monomial ideals

Let $I$ be a nonzero proper monomial ideal in ${\rm k}[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, and let $d$ be the maximal degree of a minimal monomial generator. We prove that the index of stability of the associated primes of its ordinary powers satisfies \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\frac{(4e)^{r-1}}4\,d^{r-1}\qquad(r\ge3), \] while ${\rm astab}(I)=1$ for $r=2$. If $I$ has $s\ge2$ minimal generators, we also obtain \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\min\{r,s\}(s-1)d^{\min\{r-1,s-2\}}. \] The first estimate answers Hoa's question on polynomial bounds. The proofs reduce stabilization to integer optimization for a matrix whose last row records the power of the ideal. We bound the degrees of its circuits and Graver basis elements and prove proximity estimates for optimal solutions in fixed fibers. A Steinitz rearrangement and a lattice-point count in the difference body of a simplex give the generator-independent bound. The matrix estimates hold for arbitrary indexed integral configurations in a simplex and real linear objective functions. The stability bounds hold over an arbitrary field, without normality or equigeneration assumptions.
Efficient estimation of measures of functional dependence

Measures of functional dependence that characterize both independence and perfect dependence have attracted growing interest. Despite their appealing theoretical properties, existing rank- and graph-based estimators can suffer from substantial bias under general dependence, limiting their usefulness for statistical inference. Moreover, a systematic and practically accessible framework for mitigating such bias while achieving semiparametric efficiency remains largely unavailable. In this paper, we develop a general framework for efficient estimation of measures of functional dependence through sample-splitting and cross-fitting. Our approach enables systematic bias reduction and semiparametrically efficient inference, and thus offers a flexible and theoretically grounded alternative to existing rank- and graph-based methods.
Torsion Cycles in Projective Threefolds:From Serre's Construction to Artin-Mumford

The torsion subgroup of third integral cohomology is a birational invariant of smooth projective complex threefolds; its nonvanishing obstructs stable rationality. We recall a proof using Hironaka's elimination of indeterminacies and the integral blowup formula. The Godeaux--Serre construction and Poincaré duality imply that every finite abelian group is the third integral cohomology group of a smooth projective complex threefold. This classical realization also has a description through families of concurrent plane lines. Their incidence threefolds have smooth normalizations, obtained by an explicit blowup and described as projective-line bundles over smooth surfaces. The Lefschetz theorem determines the fundamental group of these surfaces, and the projective bundle formula computes the third cohomology. The resulting threefolds are birational to products of surfaces with the projective line, and their torsion three-cycles are represented by sphere bundles over loops. Examples and the comparison with the unirational Artin--Mumford threefold explain the role of the base surface and the distinction between smooth blowups and resolution of a singular space.
Maksym Chaudkhari; Kate Juschenko; Kyrylo Muliarchyk

We prove that Thompson's groups $F$, $T$ and $V$ are sofic. As a corollary, all of them are also hyperlinear and not permutation stable. The proof relies on an explicit construction of sofic approximations to $F$ and $V$. Moreover, the construction allows us to obtain effective quantitative bounds on the parameters of sofic approximations.
Symmetry algebra of a charged harmonic oscillator in the field of the Dirac magnetic monopole

A charged particle bound by an isotropic harmonic potential to a Dirac magnetic monopole, with the centrifugal term that makes the orbits close, has degeneracies beyond rotational invariance: for integer $q$, the product of the electric and magnetic charges, the levels are those of the oscillator with the states of angular momentum $l<|q|$ removed. The conserved rank-2 tensor $T$ built from the ladder operators that accounts for them was identified thirty-five years ago, but the algebra it generates with the angular momentum $\mathbf{J}$ was not obtained. We obtain its relations in covariant form and identify it. It is polynomial but not quadratic, and the shift $T'=T+2(H-1)J^{(2)}$ by the quadrupole of $\mathbf{J}$, and only this one, makes all commutators polynomials in $\mathbf{J}$. In each sector of fixed energy and $J_z$, $(\mathbf{J}^2,T'_{zz})$ generates a cubic algebra of Heun--Racah type whose parameters are symmetric, up to a scalar shift, in the magnetic charge and the magnetic quantum number. At $q=0$, $T$ is the algebraic Heun operator of the pair (Casimir of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$, quadrupole of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$): the symmetry algebra is the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$-covariant extension of a Heun--Racah algebra. We define it abstractly and classify its multiplicity-free finite-dimensional representations at the energies of the system: besides the levels, they include, for nonzero integer $q$, a second family carried by the states the monopole removes, the kernel of the Newman--Penrose operator. All relations are derived from the dynamical algebra of the ladder operators and hold for integer and half-integer charges alike.
A conservative reduced collision model for the Boltzmann equation

The evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in solving the Boltzmann equation owing to the high dimensionality and the nonlinear structure of the collision term. In this work, we develop a conservative reduced collision (RC) model within the discrete velocity framework. The bilinear collision operator is approximated through a kernel tensor preassembled using problem-dependent reduced bases for the distribution function and the collision term. Consequently, online evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is reduced to tensor contractions. Exact discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy is enforced by constructing the collision basis in the orthogonal complement of the space spanned by the discrete collision invariants. The resulting model can be incorporated into existing deterministic Boltzmann solvers. Numerical experiments on the spatially homogeneous relaxation, the steady channel and lid-driven cavity flows, and an unsteady diffusion problem show that the proposed RC model attains the accuracy of the fast Fourier spectral method (FSM) at moderate ranks. Since the kernel tensor is assembled once in the offline stage, the online cost of each solve is reduced by orders of magnitude, so that the total cost is substantially lower even when the offline stage is included.

We determine the $G$-birational rigidity of the $G$-Fano variety $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ for all finite subgroups $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1)$.
Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold

We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper \(q\)-colorings on sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs \(\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)\). We prove that, whenever \(q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d\), Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over \(\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)\) for all sufficiently large integer \(n\). This improves the previous bound \(q = (α^* + o_d(1))d\) where \(α^* = 1.7632...\) is the unique solution of \(x = \exp(1/x)\) on \([1, \infty)\) by Efthymiou, Hayes, Štefankovič, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bezáková, Galanis, Goldberg, and Štefankovič (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.
Entropy Stable Element-Local Continuous-Discontinuous Residual Correction Summation-By-Parts Discretization
Zelalem Arega Worku; David C. Del Rey Fernandez

Residual correction provides an efficient alternative to two-point volume flux differencing for enforcing entropy stability in high-order discretizations of hyperbolic partial differential equations. We develop an element-local residual-correction summation-by-parts (SBP) method that combines continuous-SBP (C-SBP) and discontinuous-SBP (D-SBP) coupling on conforming meshes. The construction retains continuous assembly without simultaneous approximation terms (SATs) wherever suitable, restricts SATs to selected discontinuous facets, and permits the coupling to change in time as a foundation for adaptive discretizations.
