The scalar entropy defect and a graph-based distribution vector acting on conservative variables are computed entirely from element-local data, without neighboring states, auxiliary gradients, or correction SATs. The same correction applies to every facet partition, including the pure C-SBP and D-SBP limits. For fixed partitions, we establish conservation and entropy identities for each element residual, exact global conservation, entropy stability up to an explicit regularization defect, and design-order consistency. Changes in the partition are handled by a mass-weighted orthogonal projection that preserves conservative moments and convex admissible sets, does not increase entropy, and does not amplify error in the broken norm. Numerical experiments in one to three dimensions show that the hybrid method retains the smooth-solution accuracy of its D-SBP endpoint under repeated repartitioning. The nonlinear tests demonstrate robustness comparable to Hadamard-form two-point-flux discretizations, particularly when coupled with artificial dissipation.
On the maximally edge-connected square graphs with degree sequence conditions

Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a finite connected simple graph. The edge-connectivity $λ(G)$ of $G$ is the minimum number of edges that must be removed to make $G$ disconnected. We call $G$ maximally edge-connected when $λ(G)=δ(G)$, where $δ(G)$ is the minimum degree of $G$. The square graph $G^2$ of $G$ is the graph with vertex set $V(G)$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G^2$ precisely when their distance in $G$ is at most two. In this paper, first we prove that if $λ(G)\geq4$ and $λ(G^2)<δ(G^2)$, then $λ(G^2)>λ(G)^{3/2}-\frac54λ(G)$, which extends the result in \cite{ChenXu} from the edge-connectivity range $4\leqλ(G)\leq7$ to $λ(G)\geq4$. Then we show that $G^2$ is maximally edge-connected if one of the following conditions hold: (i) $δ(G)\geq\lfloor(n+2)/4\rfloor$, or $δ(G)\leq\lfloor(n+2)/4\rfloor-1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{2k}d_{n+1-i}\geq k(n-4)-2δ(G)+3$, where $k$ is an integer satisfying $2\leq k\leqδ(G)+2$ and $d_1\geq d_2\geq\cdots\geq d_n$ are the degrees of $G$; (ii) $d_{n-δ(G)}+d_n\geq(3n-9)/4$.
Inequalities for Higher-Order Logarithmic Differences of Boros--Moll Coefficients
Cindy C. Y. Gu; Yafeng Liu; Matthew H. Y. Xie

Let $d_i(m)$ denote the coefficient of $x^i$ in the Boros--Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. We prove that the sequence $\{d_{i-1}(m)d_{i+1}(m)/d_i(m)^2\}_{i=1}^{m-1}$ is strictly log-concave for every $m\ge4$, settling a conjecture of Chen and Gu. For every $m\ge 3$, we show that the consecutive ratios $d_i(m)/d_{i-1}(m)$ form a strictly log-convex sequence for $1\le i\le\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1$ and a strictly log-concave sequence for $\lfloor m/2\rfloor\le i\le m$, as conjectured by Zhao. For every integer $i\ge 0$, we prove strict infinite log-monotonicity of the sequence $\{d_i(m-1)d_i(m+1)/(\binom{m}{i+1}d_i(m)^2)\}_{m\ge i+1}$, strengthening another conjecture of Zhao. We further show that every positive real power of the binomially normalized ratio sequence is a Hausdorff moment sequence with a strictly totally positive Hankel matrix. We also obtain asymptotic formulas for forward differences of arbitrary fixed order, resolving a conjecture of Jiang and Wang. For integers $i\ge 1$, we prove that the sequence $\{2^n d_i(i)/d_i(i+n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ is an infinitely divisible Hausdorff moment sequence and that the Hankel matrix $[1/d_i(i+j+k)^τ]_{j,k\ge 0}$ is strictly totally positive for every $τ>0$. For the integral interpolation, we show that the Hausdorff moment property of the normalized reciprocals holds precisely when the positive real coefficient index is at least $1/4$.
The Corners of Ramanujan: Partial- and False-Theta Companions to Third-Order Mock Theta Functions
George E. Andrews; Mohamed El Bachraoui

Most of the traditional third-order mock theta functions occur naturally as specialized values of partition-rank generating functions. The same finite rank kernels also occur in the ordinary and odd unimodal-rank series studied previously in the literature. We organize a parallel collection of corner series by retaining these kernels and replacing their quadratic core weights by linear peak weights. Their root-of-unity specializations are governed by partial and false theta identities recorded in Ramanujan's Lost Notebook; in one exceptional case the corner companion is itself a mock theta function. The classical rank series and Ramanujan identities are used as inputs. Our new results include exact two- and three-color partition identities with sparse theta discrepancies and an oriented three-dimensional corner with a distinct tower. In both color cases, positive decompositions separate the colored companion into copies of the relevant odd-corner series and a corresponding decorated even-corner series. Thus both sparse discrepancies become signed differences between natural corner families. Burson's boxed modular involution provides a common rank-refined model for the two corrections, whose surviving fixed points produce the exceptional quadratic sequences. For the side rank of the three-dimensional corners we obtain an exact formula at $z=-1$, a strict parity bias, quartic and cubic root-of-unity rank-difference identities, and exact equidistribution modulo $3$ on the progression $6n+5$. The cubic identity also gives exact congruence formulas on the progressions $6n+2$ and $6n+3$. We further classify the associated binary triangular support modulo every integer and derive general congruence families.
Oriented Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{HP}^n$

Let $M$ be either $\mathbb{CP}^n$ or $\mathbb{HP}^n$. We prove that the family $\overline{\mathcal{F}}=\{Σ_σ\}_{σ\in M}$ of minimal geodesic spheres in $M$ characterizes the Fubini-Study metric $\overline{g}$, that is, $\overline{g}$ is the only metric that makes these real hypersurfaces minimal. This result is related to the recent theory of Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces $(M,g,\mathcal{F}=\{Σ_σ\})\in\mathcal{Z}$. It is conjectured that the only Zoll metric in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ is $\overline{g}$. We present evidence that suggests a similar rigidity of $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$ in this context of minimal hypersurfaces. Namely, we show that a direct adaptation of Guillemin's Theorem for conformal deformations of Zoll metrics in $\mathbb{S}^2$ is not possible for $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$, when $p=2n-1$ is a prime number.
Generalized quaternion groups of order $4p$ are $4$-BCI-groups

For a finite group $G$ and a subset $S\subseteq G$, the bi-Cayley graph $\operatorname{BCay}(G,S)$ has vertex set $G\times\{0,1\}$ and edges $\{(x,0),(sx,1)\}$ for $x\in G$ and $s\in S$. The group $G$ is called an $m$-BCI-group if, for all subsets $S,T\subseteq G$ with $|S|\leq m$, the isomorphism $\operatorname{BCay}(G,S)\cong\operatorname{BCay}(G,T)$ implies that $T=gS^α$ for some $g\in G$ and $α\in\operatorname{Aut} G$. We prove that, for every prime $p$, the generalized quaternion group $Q_{4p}$ is a $4$-BCI-group. For $p\geq5$, the proof uses regular coverings and voltage assignments: we pass to quotient graphs modulo the Sylow $p$-subgroup and lift isomorphisms between them.
A dual variational principle for the Moser-Trudinger inequality: existence, uniqueness and stability of extremals

For $p>1$, with $p'=p/(p-1)$, we prove the sharp dual inequality $$ \int_0^1-\log\left(1-\frac{\left|\int_0^xf(y) dy\right|^{p'}}{x}\right) dx\leq\mathsf{K}_p, \qquad \|f\|_{L^p(0,1)}\leq1, $$ where $\mathsf{K}_p$ is the logarithm of the optimal value in Moser's one-dimensional formulation of the Moser-Trudinger inequality. The dual functional follows from the Gibbs variational principle, monotone transport and the Legendre transform. Its supremum is attained, giving a dual proof of the existence theorems of Carleson-Chang (1986) and Hudson-Leckband (2002); the classical concentration threshold is realized by equality cases in Hoelder's inequality. For $p=2$ we prove, with rigorous computer-assisted estimates, that the nonnegative dual maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. Hence the extremal of the Moser-Trudinger inequality on a disk $D$ is unique up to sign, confirming conjectures of Adimurthi-Karthik-Giacomoni (2016) and of Chen-Lu-Xue-Zhu (2026). The positive extremal $u_*$ is nondegenerate, and, writing $\mathcal{M}_D(u)=|D|^{-1}\int_De^{4πu^2} dx$, we obtain $$ \mathcal{M}_D(u_*)-\mathcal{M}_D(u) \geq c \min_{\pm}\|\nabla(u\mp u_*)\|_{L^2(D)}^2 $$ for all $u\in H_0^1(D)$ with $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(D)}\leq1$. Here $c>0$, and the exponent two is optimal, giving a quantitative stability theorem of Bianchi-Egnell type.

We extend the tangency construction of López de Medrano, Verjovsky and Meersseman from diagonal abelian actions to non-abelian Samelson groups. For these groups the tangency locus is a moment-map zero set: the commutator term in the leafwise Hessian vanishes there, and under an admissibility hypothesis, Kempf--Ness convexity gives a global transversal whose projectivization is a compact complex manifold. The construction includes compact rotation groups and groups with non-closed central rotations. In the latter setting we construct explicit families of complex dimension $2m-3$, $m\geq5$, which are $4$-connected and admit no symplectic form. Their meromorphic function fields are rational of transcendence degree $m-2$, although every holomorphic map to a projective space is constant. We compute their connected automorphism groups and show that they admit no maximal torus action. They are Hopf-surface bundles over compact complex quotients of stable Grassmannian loci; these bases give related examples already in complex dimension five. The families demonstrate that the non-abelian tangency construction reaches beyond compact complex manifolds with maximal torus actions.
The inviscid limit of 2D Navier-Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse

We study the inviscid limit of the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with initial vorticity given by three point vortices whose inviscid trajectories collapse self-similarly at $t=1$. For every fixed $0<γ<1$, we prove that the solution is approximated by a superposition of Lamb--Oseen vortices centered at the point-vortex positions, with an $L^1$ error of order $O(ν^{1-γ})$, uniformly for $0<t\le T_ν=1-ν^γ$. We use coordinates adapted to the self-similar collapse and study a long-time inviscid limit problem on the interval $0<s\leγ\log(1/ν)$, with a time-dependent rescaled diffusion coefficient $η(s)$ that tends to zero as $s\to\infty$.
Mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim beyond the polylog quotient
David Corwin; Ishai Dan-Cohen; Martin Lüdtke

We develop an algorithmic approach to mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim theory for the full unipotent fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, beyond the polylogarithmic quotient used in previous work. The key step is computing the cocycle evaluation map in the presence of a nontrivial motivic Galois action, using relations among motivic multiple zeta values. This yields explicit Kim functions involving multiple polylogarithms, as well as an algorithm for solving the $S$-unit equation whose halting is implied by certain natural conjectures.
Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas

Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.
Isotropy of symplectic involutions and motivic equivalence for groups of type $\sf{C}$
Demba Barry; Charles De Clercq; Anne Quéguiner-Mathieu

We extend to arbitrary characteristic a theorem due to Karpenko and Tignol on the isotropy of symplectic involutions after generic index reduction; as a consequence, we also prove the existence of critical varieties for semi-simple algebraic groups of type $\sf C$ over arbitrary base fields. The latter result relies on a characteristic-free argument, which involves the computation of the mod $2$ Tate trace of the variety of isotropic ideals of reduced dimension $2$ for a symplectic involution.
Improved algorithms for computing the matrix logarithm based on the double-exponential formula

Tatsuoka et al. proposed an efficient algorithm for computing the matrix logarithm using the double-exponential (DE) formula. Its discretization error decreases exponentially as the number of quadrature nodes grows, and its nested grids allow previously computed values to be reused when the mesh is refined. They also reported that their approach is more robust than Gauss--Legendre quadrature for ill-conditioned matrices. We propose two algorithms based on the DE formula. The first adaptively refines the mesh while reusing previously computed values and requires no matrix norm computations. The second uses a rigorous error bound to select the number of quadrature nodes a priori. Numerical experiments show that both methods attain lower errors than Tatsuoka et al.'s method at comparable elapsed times over the tested ranges.
Studying proof data with proof theory: the case of AI-generated mathematics

I present a method for analyzing large collections of formally verified mathematical proofs (e.g. OpenAI's) grounded in some historical and philosophical musings on mathematics in the age of AI. Many of the quantities involved, such as the size of a proof term or the number of redundant steps, are already computed by work on improving automated provers, where they serve as targets. My aim is to turn them into measurements of proofs themselves: compared against a reference library and against each proof's own cut-free form, checked against theorems they must obey, and controlled for how the proofs were compiled. With these instruments, I measure how (much) machine-generated mathematics diverges from human mathematics, and find that AI-written formal proofs realize far less of the logical compression available to them than human mathematicians do (31% against 73% in mathlib, and 55% against 86% on proofs that call no automation). These figures are broadly in line with reports from those who build provers and proof-improvement tools that AI-written proofs are often longer than they need to be.
A coupling normal form for reversible center-center Hamiltonians with application to the restricted three-body problem

Near a reversible center--center equilibrium, the Birkhoff normal form does not describe the families bifurcating from the continued tori, while resonant normal forms capture these bifurcations through a reduced system. For such equilibria with a reflection symmetry, we develop a coupling normal form in which the bifurcating families also appear as tori of action normal forms. Along a selected coupling direction, the first slow harmonic is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. We prove that the coupled recursion determines unique even counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form, and an exact counterterm factorization. The factorization gives a scalar recovery constraint, whose trivial factor corresponds to the Birkhoff normal form. At every finite order, a symmetric pair of bifurcating branches leaves the trivial branch at a critical curve and carries approximately invariant tori and circles with explicit residual estimates. Applied to the spatial circular restricted three-body problem, the construction yields approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori.
Entropy hypocoercivity and query complexity for the bouncy particle sampler

We study convergence in relative entropy of the bouncy particle sampler with Gaussian velocity refreshment, for a target $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with $U$ $m$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth, and condition number $κ=L/m$. For initial laws with bounded density relative to equilibrium, we show that the relative entropy decays exponentially up to an arbitrary additive error $δ$, with a rate that depends only logarithmically on the density bound and on $δ$. From a Gaussian cold start and with a suitably chosen refreshment rate, the relative entropy falls below $δ$ after time $\widetilde O(\sqrt{d/m})$. Combined with exact simulation by windowed thinning, this gives an expected gradient-query complexity of $\widetilde O(d\sqrtκ)$, improving the $\widetilde O(d^2\sqrtκ)$ bound based on $L^2$ hypocoercivity.
Large deviations for the largest eigenvalue of a polynomial in Gaussian matrices
Alice Guionnet; Jonathan Husson; Jana Reker
In this article, we prove that the spectrum, the norm, and the largest eigenvalue of a self-adjoint polynomial $P$ in $k$ independent matrices from the GOE satisfy a large deviation principle.
Giuseppe Cannizzaro; Harry Giles; Fabio Toninelli

We construct an infinite-dimensional diffusion on the space of interlaced particle configurations on Z x R, a process we call the dynamical bead model. The process (self-)interacts through instantaneous reflection and preserves the bead measures of [C. Boutillier, Ann. Probab., 2009]. Through the height function correspondence, our process is equivalent to a reversible interface in (2+1) dimensions. We provide compelling evidence that at large space-time scales the interface exhibits diffusive behaviour, as we compute exactly its diffusivity matrix and show it is non-degenerate and independent of time.
A noncommutative weak $L_1$-estimate for rough singular integrals
Guixiang Hong; Liang Wang; Xumin Wang; Bang Xu

In this paper, we establish a noncommutative version of Andreas Seeger's weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for singular integral operators with kernels satisfying angular $L\log L$ integrability and an averaged radial Dini condition. The strategy for obtaining the sharp integrability condition involves not only some new estimates of the off-diagonal good and bad functions in Parcet's noncommutative Calderón-Zygmund decomposition but also certain essential modifications of Seeger's kernel decomposition and estimates.
The Calderón Problem for Quasilinear Currents

We study the Calderón problem for smooth quasilinear current laws on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq3$. Under the stated structural assumptions and analyticity conditions, the interior current law is determined by local Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps, up to a partial-boundary-fixing diffeomorphism and a Hall-effect-type invisible current. The two obstructions come from the linearized inverse problem, which is solved by combining boundary determination for magnetic Schrödinger operators with analytic continuation in solution coordinates. Higher-order linearization and a boundary argument involving products of three solution gradients then determine the remaining Taylor coefficients.
Can Quantum Entanglement Increase the Capacity of a Classical Relay Channel?

We show positive and negative results on classical relay channels with entanglement assistance, revealing a sharp contrast between strictly causal and causal relay encoding. First, we consider van der Meulen's setting of a unit-delay relay, with strictly causal encoding. We show that the standard cutset upper bound continues to hold with entanglement assistance, and deduce that entanglement does not increase the capacity for several classes of relay channels. Second, we consider a zero-delay relay, where the encoding is causal. We present an example in which entanglement enables rates that exceed the cutset upper bound by at least 12.5%. Namely, entanglement shared between the source and relay significantly increases the capacity of a classical zero-delay relay channel.

We provide a complete classification of the rational $2$-adic Tate modules $V_2(E)$ of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}_2$ with potentially good reduction. The classification is given in terms of the filtered $(φ,\mathrm{Gal})$-modules associated to $V_2(E)$ via Fontaine's functor $D_{pcris}^{*}$.
A gentle introduction to approximating high-dimensional integrals with lattice rules and a maybe-not-so-gentle introduction to the relevant function spaces for QMC integration

These lecture notes give both a practical and theoretical introduction to high-dimensional integration with lattice rules. We introduce lattice points and rules in combination with accompanying Julia code. Next we introduce the typical function spaces used in the literature. We compare classical Sobolev spaces with Sobolev spaces of dominating mixed smoothness. We derive lower bounds and show that the curse of dimensionality is unavoidable for these unweighted function spaces. Next we switch to weighted periodic spaces and derive a constructive upper bound using the component-by-component construction for the generating vector of a lattice rule. We pick periodic spaces because they are a perfect match with lattice rules. The upper bound shows that under suitable conditions on the weights we obtain dimension-independent worst-case error bounds. We then use embedding constants to transfer these bounds to some common norms for these periodic spaces.
Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
Zhonghua Liao; Qi Lü; Xu Zhang

We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) for the free wave equation does not guarantee internal observability in the presence of a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable, and a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_Ω=L^2(Ω)\times H^{-1}(Ω)$ on every finite interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane; this local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. For comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

The Bellaterra automaton gives three involutions of every set of binary words of a fixed length. We identify their Schreier graph at level $n$ with a cubic arithmetic graph over $\Q(\sqrt{17})$, and prove that every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue satisfies the Ramanujan bound. In particular, this proves Malyshev-Pak's Conjecture that the Bellaterra graphs form a family of two-sided expanders.
Critical limits of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps

We study connected planar maps with a fixed number of numbered faces, whose vertices carry integer labels such that the minimum label along the boundary of each face is one. Each face has its own positive weight, and an edge shared by two faces receives the geometric mean of their weights. For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of faces, we prove that the suitably rescaled generating function converges locally uniformly as the face weights approach the critical value $1/12$, possibly at different positive rates. The limit is a finite, continuous sum of integrals over cubic schemes. Each scheme edge carries a Green kernel for a singular differential operator on the positive half-line, and each face contributes one insertion of the derivative of the tree scaling profile. The main difficulty is obtaining uniform estimates for small vertex labels, where the minimum-label constraints of different faces can interact. A positive corner-marking expansion reduces this problem to establishing uniform bounds on the contributions of marked configurations, both for small and large vertex labels. These estimates prove integrability of the surviving diagrams and show that coincident marks and noncubic schemes contribute only lower-order terms.
Projective Decomposition and Intersection Cohomology of Rigid Spaces

We prove a rigid analytic analogue of the Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne decomposition theorem for projective morphisms over $p$-adic fields, with $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-coefficients for every prime $\ell$, including $\ell=p$. As an application, we show that the $p$-adic intersection cohomology of every proper rigid analytic space is de Rham. We also establish an independent criterion for de Rham intersection cohomology with local coefficients in terms of the dimension of the boundary, yielding further results for curves, surfaces, and finite covers. For finite coefficients of characteristic different from $p$, we obtain isotropic analytic upper bounds for singular support and prove that singular support is analytic and Lagrangian for complexes supported in dimension at most one.
Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method

Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.
Local rigidity of conformally Euclidean metrics for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation at fixed energy

We prove local rigidity of smooth conformally Euclidean metrics $g_0$ on smooth compact domains $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge3$, for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation $(-Δ_g -k^2)u =0$ at a fixed energy $k^2>0$ which is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-Δ_{g_0}$ in $M$. Any smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ in $H^s(M)$, with integer $s>n/2+1$, and having the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, is its pullback by a smooth diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. The proof uses a Helmholtz embedding to fix the gauge and a compactness argument together with a characterization of the kernel of the linearization.
Sharp concentration levels and extremal functions for a planar Choquard-type Trudinger--Moser inequality

Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth bounded domain and let $0<α<2$. We study the exponential Choquard functional \[ \mathcal{F}_β(u)=\int_Ω\int_Ω \frac{e^{βu^2(x)}e^{βu^2(y)}}{|x-y|^α}d xd y \] on the unit Dirichlet ball of $H_0^1(Ω)$. We establish the sharp boundedness threshold $β_*=(4-α)π$ and prove attainment of the critical supremum. More precisely, we determine the exact concentration level at every point of $\overlineΩ$ in terms of the regular part of the Dirichlet Green function. The concentration upper bound follows from the classical planar Trudinger--Moser concentration formula and the sharp Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality, after separating the background contribution. A test function obtained by matching a logarithmic profile to the Green function attains this bound asymptotically. Its exact Dirichlet normalization produces a strictly positive lower-order correction, which rules out concentration of maximizing sequences. We also prove the Euler--Lagrange equation, positivity, and regularity of extremals.
Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type

Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.
Model Theory and Algorithms for One-Relator Groups

We study the elementary theories and algorithmic properties of one-relator groups. We give a first-order sentence characterizing Baumslag-Solitar-freeness in this class. For fixed $|m|>1$, we regularly interpret $\BS(1,m)$ as a definable subgroup in every one-relator group containing it. We uniformly, regularly and injectively interpret integer arithmetic in countable groups of cohomological dimension at most two. We obtain one uniform interpretation for all one-relator groups containing a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. Every fixed finitely presented group is regularly interpretable in these groups, and their elementary theories are undecidable. We also describe the GBS overgroups of a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. For the unimodular groups we construct finite-index direct products of free groups and $\Z$, and reduce the elementary theory of $\BS(k,k)$ to that of a free group with a named periodic automorphism. Using the recent Open AI result that BS-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic we obtain a terminating algorithm recognizing this class and obtain consequences. From the virtual compact specialness result of another Open AI paper, we obtain an effective construction of virtual free-by-cyclic presentations for hyperbolic one-relator groups, the free kernel may have infinite rank. For classes of torsion-free one-relator groups in which CSA implies toral relative hyperbolicity, we give a uniform algorithm deciding CSA and, in the affirmative case, the existence of a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^2$.
Variance Reduction Note 2: The Convergence of SPIDER

The stochastic path-integrated differential estimator (SPIDER) tracks a gradient by accumulating small, shared-sample gradient differences and periodically refreshing the estimate. This second expository note on recursive variance reduction explains SPIDER-SFO and gives a self-contained proof of its expected first-order stationarity guarantee. The argument combines an epochwise mean-square error bound with descent under a clipped, normalized update. It yields $O(ε^{-3})$ stochastic gradient evaluations in the online setting and $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ component gradient evaluations for a finite sum, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. All refresh costs are included. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.
Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs

We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves. When the atlas is regular, the de Rham cohomology agrees with the sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf, just as in the smooth case. We compute it for several examples, including a torus graph and a graph resembling a sphere, and recover the cohomology of the corresponding surfaces.
Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs

By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.
A Common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph

Let G be a simple connected graph with the vertex set V (G) and the edge set E(G) such that |V (G)| = n and |E(G)| = q. The common neighborhood graph con(G) of G has the same set of vertices as that of G and uv is an edge in con(G) if u and v have at least one common neighbor in G. By a signed graph S, we mean a graph G whose edges has been assigned sign plus or minus. In this paper, the concept of common neighborhood graph has been initiated in the realm of signed graphs, that is, we define a common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph.
A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate

This paper presents an original mathematical and computational framework for modeling the efficacy of methylphenidate as an optimal control policy acting on the nonlinear dynamics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Neural processes in ADHD are conceptualized as stochastic processes with trajectories that inherently converge towards stable, yet dysfunctional patterns associated with clinical symptoms. The pharmacological intervention is mathematically formalized as an external control signal that reassesses the system's drift and redirects these trajectories towards neurotypical regimes. To bridge these theoretical stochastic models with empirical clinical data, latent representations are inferred using a novel deterministic hybrid deep learning architecture, combining a one-dimensional convolutional neural network and a Vision Transformer, trained on preprocessed functional magnetic resonance imaging data.
De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems

Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erdős--Rényi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.
New Bernstein functions and subordination representations for time-nonlocal evolution equations

This paper establishes subordination representations from multi-term time-fractional differential equations to single-term ones, a direction complementary to the previously known subordination from single-term to multi-term equations; combining the two complementary directions also yields subordination representations between two multi-term equations. The crucial step is to prove that certain implicitly defined functions are Bernstein functions. We show that the quotient $\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jλ^{α_j}\big)/\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jα_jλ^{α_j}\big)$ is a Stieltjes function whenever $0\leqα_1-α_m\leq 1$, and consequently that the inverse function of $λ=\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jφ^{α_j}\big)^{1/β}$ is a Bernstein function for every $0<β\leqα_m$. As applications, we obtain subordination representations with a clear probabilistic meaning: from multi-term to single-term time-fractional diffusion-wave equations, between abstract nonlocal-in-time equations with kernels of type $(\mathcal{PC})$ (including equations of tempered stable type), and between nonlocal-in-time telegraph equations. A necessary and sufficient condition for $[(λ+b)^β-b^β]^γ$ to be a Bernstein function also yields a negative result: in general, no such subordination exists from an $α$-stable type dynamics to a tempered $β$-stable one when $α<1$.
Li Gao; Marius Junge; Zhendong Xu; Hao Zhang

We derive $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.
Maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity of finite element methods for stochastic parabolic equations in polygonal domains
Genming Bai; Jianbo Cui; Buyang Li

We prove that a spatial semidiscrete finite element method preserves the stochastic maximal regularity of the heat equation on bounded convex polygonal and polyhedral domains in dimensions two and three. A main difficulty is to establish suitable Green-function estimates for stochastic convolutions, whose paths generally lack classical time derivatives. Besides, the failure of the Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (BDG) inequality at the endpoint $p=\infty$ creates additional difficulties. Our approach leverages a hidden symmetry structure of the discrete Green's function, which enables the use of a key integration-by-parts type formula. Then the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^p$ regularity with $p\in [2,\infty)$ is obtained from the discrete local energy estimates and interpolation inequalities. To extend further the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity with the full range of integrability exponents, i.e., $p\in (2,\infty), q\in [2,\infty)$ or $p=q=2$, we also show that the discrete convolution kernel satisfies the stochastic Hörmander's condition, allowing the application of a stochastic version of the Calderón-Zygmund theory.
The associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
Jing Guo; Nengqun Li; Yuming Liu

For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$, one can associate a graded algebra (denoted by $\mathrm{gr}(A)$) with the radical filtration of $A$. An interesting question is to compare the representation theories of $A$ and $\mathrm{gr}(A)$. When $A$ is a Brauer graph algebra with defining Brauer graph $Γ$, we have described the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ in terms of the information of $Γ$. In this paper, we describe the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ when $A$ is a biserial fractional Brauer graph algebra - a notion that properly generalizes a Brauer graph algebra - in terms of the information of the defining biserial fractional Brauer graph $Γ$ of $A$.
Inverse Zero-Sum Problems: The Property C and Property D Conjectures

Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We give negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai \cite[Open Problems 1.2]{GHST07} in 2007, and disprove the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger \cite[Conjecture 7.2]{GG06} in 2006.
Cellular bases of mirabolic Hecke algebras
Jian Chen; Yan Liu Jinkui Wan; Xirui Yu

We prove that the mirabolic Hecke algebra $\mathscr{H}_{n,R}(q)$ over a commutative ring $R$ is cellular by constructing explicit cellular bases. When $R=\mathbb{K}$ is a field, we also establish a Morita equivalence between $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$ and a direct sum of Hecke algebras associated with symmetric groups. As applications, we classify the irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules and obtain a semisimplicity criterion. Finally, when $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}(q)$, we show that the cell modules arising from one of our cellular bases coincide with Siegel's irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules.
Volume-dependent geometry and symmetry transitions of torsion optimizers in infinite cylinders

We study relative torsional rigidity in infinite cylinders, addressing two geometric questions raised by Caldiroli, Iacopetti and Pacella on the shape of volume-constrained optimizers. The torsion problem has Dirichlet conditions on the free boundary and Neumann conditions on the fixed lateral wall. At small volumes we establish a two-term expansion of the optimal energy, curvature selection, and quantitative convergence of optimizers to boundary half-balls. We also obtain a uniform expansion for the exact torsion states on the explicit curved half-ball comparison domains. At sufficiently large volumes, every optimizer is exactly a finite cylinder, without convexity of the cross-section or an a priori free-boundary regularity assumption. The normalized optimal value is strictly decreasing up to a finite global transition threshold and constant thereafter. We distinguish this threshold from the local spectral stability threshold and prove coexistence of cylindrical and noncylindrical optimizers when the thresholds are separated. Exact one-sided derivative formulas identify nondifferentiability with the range of transverse energies among optimal states. Strict separation holds for all rectangular cross-sections and for sufficiently close smooth convex inner approximations of any rectangle, with no aspect-ratio restriction. These smooth examples exhibit both curvature-dependent small-volume concentration and a global symmetry transition.
Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
Niels Benedikter; Sascha Lill; Marcello Porta; Benjamin Schlein

We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $ρ^{-2/3}$ and $ρ^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.
Spatial Discretization Error for Quantum Chemistry Simulation

Nonrelativistic quantum chemistry is based on the Schrödinger equation in continuous, unbounded space. Computational approaches on classical and quantum computers often truncate the spatial domain and introduce a finite-dimensional basis, reducing the continuum problem to a finite-dimensional one. There is therefore a fundamental question: to what extent does this approximation capture the original continuum problem? In this work, we develop a general Sobolev-Galerkin framework for estimating spatial discretization errors in quantum simulation with unbounded Hamiltonians. We apply this framework to many-body Coulomb systems and establish both periodization and Galerkin error estimates for wave-function dynamics and ground-state energies. For dynamics, the finite-basis projection error of the exact wave function does not capture the full basis-discretization error: an additional dynamical projection error enters our bound at a different rate, and we introduce an inner-product argument to control this contribution. Interestingly, the spatial convergence rates for wave-function dynamics and ground-state energies differ quantitatively. For ground-state energies, we establish a sharp $M^{-1}$ convergence rate at fixed cell size, where $M$ is the number of one-particle basis functions. We also show that a uniform $M^{-1}$ convergence rate is impossible for the corresponding real-time wave-function error with general $H^2$ initial data. The analysis relies on many-body Sobolev estimates with explicit polynomial dependence on system size. Combining these estimates with state-of-the-art quantum algorithms, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first rigorous end-to-end complexity bounds for quantum simulation of molecular and electronic dynamics with all spatial errors explicitly controlled. The number of basis functions is determined directly from the continuum problem, without regularization.
Semi-classical Szegő kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension

In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $Π_{k,\leq kμ_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, kμ_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szegő projection $Π_k$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szegő projection $Π_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq kδ)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.
The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
Huagui Duan; Hui Liu; Wei Wang
Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.
Finite Symplectic Automorphism Groups of K3 Surfaces in Characteristic Seven

We classify all finite groups of order divisible by $7$ that admit a faithful symplectic action on a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic seven, together with the possible heights and Artin invariants. Combined with the known classification of tame actions, this gives the complete list of finite groups admitting such an action in characteristic seven.
Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems
Joscha Henheik; Marius Lemm; Tom Wessel

Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.
Lucas' Theorem modulo $p^n$ via Harmonic sums

Lucas' theorem states that for a prime $p$, integers $a,b\geq0$ and $0\leq r,s\leq p-1$, one has $\binom{pa+r}{pb+s}\equiv\binom{a}{b}\binom{r}{s}\bmod p$. Let $D(p^n)$ be the set of pairs $(r,s)$ with $s\leq r$ for which this congruence holds modulo $p^n$ for all $a,b\geq0$. Rowland characterized $D(p^2)$ in terms of harmonic sums and symmetries of Pascal's triangle. For $n<p$, we give a criterion for a point $(r,s)$ to lie in $D(p^n)$ in terms of generalized harmonic sums of order at most $n-1$. We show that $D(p^n)$ is invariant under the reflection $(r,s)\mapsto(r,r-s)$ and the rotation $(r,s)\mapsto(p-1-s,r-s)$, so that with every point it contains its full orbit under the dihedral group $D_3$. Applied to the vertices, our criterion gives a result of Jacobsthal-Ljunggren type modulo $p^n$. In particular, we recover Zhao's result $(0,0)\in D(p^4)$ if and only if $p$ is a Wolstenholme prime. We also study the centroid and the edge midpoints, whose membership in $D(p^3)$ and $D(p^4)$ is governed by Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Wolstenholme primes and super Wieferich primes. In particular, for $p=205129$ the centroid lies in $D(p^3)$, answering a question of Rowland.
Pre-Nichols algebras and generation of pointed Hopf algebras in positive characteristic

We study when a finite-dimensional pre-Nichols algebra $R$ of $V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\nmid\dim R$, is necessarily isomorphic to the Nichols algebra $\B(V)$. A trace identity gives a rigidity criterion involving the twist on minimal defining relations. Using integral forms and Hochschild cohomology, we establish uniform rigidity for Yetter--Drinfeld modules of bounded dimension over fixed finite abelian groups, and obtain related results for certain modules over nonabelian groups. For every finite group $G$ of odd order, outside finitely many characteristics depending only on $G$, every finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $H$ with $G(H)\simeq G$ and dimension prime to the characteristic is generated by group-like and skew-primitive elements. If $G$ is abelian, then, outside a possibly larger finite set of characteristics, every such $H$ is a Hopf $2$-cocycle deformation of its associated graded Hopf algebra.
An Exact Mass Threshold for Global Existence and Blow-up in Semilinear Anti-de Sitter Equations
Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento; Michael Reissig

We study the influence of the mass parameter on global existence and finite-time blow-up for the semilinear anti-de Sitter Klein--Gordon equation \[ ϕ_{tt}-e^{2t}Δϕ+nϕ_t+m^2ϕ=|ϕ|^p \qquad\text{in }[0,\infty)\times\R^d. \] After removing the damping term, we establish $L^2$ energy estimates for the resulting Klein--Gordon equation with constant coefficient in the potential. They imply global existence for arbitrary sufficiently small energy data, without spatial localization, whenever \( m^2>-\frac{d(2n+d)}{4} \quad\text{and}\quad p>1. \) In the remaining mass parameter interval above the structural threshold, an exact change to conformal time reduces the problem to a scale-invariant effective damped wave equation. Exponentially weighted energy estimates then extend global existence to \( -d(n+d)<m^2\le-\frac{d(2n+d)}4 \quad\text{for every } \quad p>1. \) In the complementary regime $m^2\le-d(n+d)$, we prove finite-time blow-up for every $p>1$ and for weak solutions with finite speed of propagation arising from nonnegative, nontrivial initial data. We further obtain lifespan estimates that are polynomial at the threshold and logarithmic below it. Thus, $m^2=-d(n+d)$ is the exact structural mass parameter threshold separating the global-existence and blow-up regimes.
Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays

Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $α<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in regressions involving general nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We demonstrate that the proposed methods---including IVX-based and related instrumental-variable procedures---facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes nearly and mildly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/α<d<2-1/α$, where $α\in(1,2]$. Our analysis is applicable to both parametric and kernel regression models. The finite-sample performance of the proposed methods is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study. Additionally, we provide an empirical application to the predictability of stock returns using long-memory heavy-tailed predictors.
Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
Tengfei Bai; Jingshi Xu; Jinlai Zhu

In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leqδ<1$, $0<μ,v\leq\infty$, $1\leqλ\leq2$, $r>n/μ$, and $N>2n/λ$, with $μ<\infty$ for the latter class. For $μ\geq1$, $(1-δ)r\geq n/μ$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.
Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$

We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}θ^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.
Local Approximation of $A$-Harmonic Functions and the Super-Localization Conjecture
Moritz Hauck; Chupeng Ma; Daniel Peterseim

We consider the local energy approximation of $A$-harmonic functions on concentric cubes with a fixed size ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, for bounded, symmetric, uniformly elliptic diffusion tensors~$A$. We give a short proof of the Kolmogorov $n$-width decay rate $\exp(-cn^{1/(d-1)})$ conjectured by Ma [Found.\ Comput.\ Math.\ 26 (2026), 1699--1758], where $n$ denotes the approximation dimension. We apply this result to numerical homogenization, improving local approximation estimates for multiscale spectral generalized finite element methods and proving the conjectured local super-localization rate of Hauck and Peterseim [Math.\ Comp.\ 92 (2023), 981--1003] for interior Cartesian patches.
The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients

A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose Kähler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be Kählerian (i.e., admitting a Kähler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant Kähler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence Kähler. We also describe the resulting Kähler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.
Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups

Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$. A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.
An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets

Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.
Generalized symmetric pairs, Lie superalgebras, Dirac operators and Kostant constants

In this paper, we present a geometric construction of contragredient Lie superalgebras, with the exceptions of $A(m,n)$ $(m,n>0)$ and $G(3)$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an order 4 automorphism $σ$, the eigenspace decomposition being $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)$. When $\mathfrak{g}(i)$ admits a $\mathfrak{g}(1)$-invariant symplectic structure, $(\mathfrak{g},σ)$ is called a \emph{generalized symmetric pair with symplectic subspace}. In this paper, we classify all such pairs and construct a natural Lie superalgebra structure on $L= L_{\bar{0}}+L_{\bar{1}}$ with $L_{\bar{0}}=\mathfrak{g}(1)$ and $L_{\bar{1}}=\mathfrak{g}(i)$. Furthermore, we investigate the constants arising from the squares of two distinct Dirac operators: $D$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}^{σ^2}+\mathfrak{g}^{-σ^2}$, and $D_s$ for $L=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)$. We prove that the constant $C$ in $D^2$ admits a remarkable factorization \[C=J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})\cdot\dim L_{\bar{1}}\cdot h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}},\] where $h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}}$ is the signed dual Coxeter number of $L$ and $J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})$ is a mapped Casimir constant of its even part. This formula reveals an unexpected unification of symmetric space geometry and Lie superalgebra invariants. Finally, we prove that the Kostant constant $\mathrm{K_s} = \left.Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}}\right|_{L_{\bar{1}}}=\frac{1}{2}$ is universal for all contragredient Lie superalgebras with non-degenerate Killing form, which implies that the constant $C_s$ in $D_s^2$ satisfies $C_s=\frac{1}{16}\dim L_{\bar{0}}$. We then establish a bijection between such superalgebras and solutions of the superadmissibility index equations $E_s^{I\!I} =\frac{1}{2}, E_s^I = \frac{1}{2}$, recovering the classification from an invariant-theoretic perspective.

We develop a nonlinear theory of complementary Cauchy elasticity in which the right Cauchy-Green strain is prescribed as a function of the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, without assuming constitutive invertibility or the existence of a complementary strain-energy function. We introduce the complementary stress-work 1-form and characterize the obstruction to complementary hyperelasticity through the failure of major symmetry of the tangent compliance tensor. For general implicit elasticity, we show that the simultaneous closure of the stress-work and complementary stress-work 1-forms is characterized by the Lagrangian structure of the constitutive manifold. Using the Darboux classification, we obtain local canonical representations of anisotropic and isotropic complementary Cauchy elastic solids, including explicit non-hyperelastic examples. We investigate kinematic and stress constraints, including applications to pentamode solids, and show that internally constrained constitutive relations are naturally formulated on equivalence classes of stresses modulo reactive stresses. We formulate the balance laws and thermodynamics covariantly and establish that covariance of the energy balance directly yields the balance of angular momentum in complementary Cauchy elasticity, unlike in conventional Cauchy elasticity. Finally, we linearize implicit, Cauchy, and complementary Cauchy elasticity about finitely deformed and prestressed configurations and show that nonlinear non-hyperelastic solids may possess hyperelastic linearized responses.
A counterexample to the geometric triangulation conjecture of Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio

Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct a triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.
LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction

The realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECC). Of particular interest are codes that combine a high encoding rate with sufficient distance. Existing algebraic constructions, such as lifted product (LP) codes, build a large quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code from a classical base matrix. In this work we introduce LiftDiff, a generative approach to the discovery of QECC. A discrete denoising diffusion model is trained to generate base matrices over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]$, which are then expanded into LP codes. The reverse diffusion process is guided by an energy function that evaluates quantum code properties, including girth, degree, sparsity and decoding performance, steering the sampler toward matrices that yield LP codes with favorable parameters. Our method discovers codes with parameters such as $[[169,13,11]]$, $[[143,15,9]]$, and $[[260,24,10]]$, including a $[[247,19,14]]$ code that achieves the highest ${kd^2}/{n}$ among the baselines. Moreover, several discovered codes outperform the Gross code across a broad range of the tested physical error rates under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise.
Condensation and Non-condensation in the Quasilinear 4-wave Kinetic Equation

We study finite-time condensation at zero frequency for the isotropic quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation in three dimensions. With Schrodinger dispersion and a product interaction coefficient with exponent $β\in(0,3/4]$, we construct global measure solutions $(g_t)_{t\geq0}$ for every nonnegative initial measure $g_0$ with finite wave action and energy. We then establish the sharp threshold $β=1/4$ for finite-time condensation of the constructed solutions. For $β\in[1/4,3/4]$, the constructed solutions satisfy $g_t(\{0\})=g_0(\{0\})$ for all $t\geq0$. For $β\in(0,1/4)$, every constructed solution with $(g_0)_{\mathrm{ac}}\neq0$ satisfies $\|g_t-\mathcal{N}_0δ_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq C\mathcal{N}_0(1+\mathcal{N}_0^2t)^{-(1-4β)/40}$ for all $t\geq0$, where $\mathcal{N}_0=g_0([0,\infty))$ and $C=C(β,g_0/\mathcal{N}_0)>0$. In particular, for every $ζ\in(0,1)$, there exists $T_ζ<\infty$ such that $g_t(\{0\})\geq(1-ζ)\mathcal{N}_0$ for all $t\geq T_ζ$.

For every $x\ge 0$, let $R^{x}=\{ R^{x}_{t}\} _{t\ge 0}$ be a three-dimensional Bessel process started at $x$. Given $x>0$, with the aid of Pitman's theorem, a path transformation $T_{x}$ under which the process $T_{x}(R^{y})$ is distributed as $R^{x}$ for any $y>0$ is constructed. In fact, we prove that, for every $x,y>0$, the two three-dimensional processes \begin{align*} \bigl( R^{x},T_{y}(R^{x}),\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x\bigr) && \text{and} && \bigl( T_{x}(R^{y}),R^{y},\mathcal{P}(-R^{y})+y\bigr) \end{align*} are identical in law, where $\mathcal{P}$ is Pitman's transformation. In the course of our exploration, it will be revealed that, for any $x>0$, the process $\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x$ has the same law as the standard three-dimensional Bessel process $R^{0}$, which is then applied to derive a disintegration formula for the law of $R^{x}$ in terms of Pitman's transformation. An application of the formula to three-dimensional Bessel bridges is also presented.
Crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs

Zarankiewicz's long standing conjecture states that the crossing number $cr(K_{m,n})$ of the complete bipartite graph is \[ Z(m,n):=\bigg\lfloor{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{m-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor. \] Using flag algebras, we show that $cr(K_{n,n}) \geq 0.96936 \cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. A closely related conjecture is Hill's conjecture stating that the crossing number $cr(K_{n})$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is \[ H(n):= \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor \] for all $n \geq 3$. This paper represents the state of knowledge before those publications and shows how far we can push the flag algebra method.

Over every nonzero commutative ring $R$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose finitely generated thick subcategories are alegbraic, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.

Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits

We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.
A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception

How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincaré-Miranda theorem.
Globally Optimal Estimation of Nested Logit Models

Nested logit is widely used in operational demand models, yet jointly estimating its utility coefficients and nest dissimilarity parameters requires nonconvex optimization. Standard estimation routines offer no certificate of global optimality, leaving a gap between globally optimizing decisions under nested-logit demand and reliably estimating that demand model. We develop, to our knowledge, the first globally convergent optimization framework with an explicit global-accuracy guarantee for joint nested-logit estimation. Our central complexity result confines all exponential dependence to the number of free nest dissimilarity parameters: computation is polynomial in the numbers of observations, alternatives, and utility coefficients. Consequently, under the stated compact-domain and relaxation-error conditions, fixing the number of nests yields an additive polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS). The framework exploits an exact exponential-cone formulation for fixed dissimilarities and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm that searches only over the free dissimilarities. Valid likelihood bounds provide an anytime certificate and finite termination at any prescribed additive average-log-likelihood tolerance. Across eight benchmark datasets and 240 estimation instances, the method certifies every reported solution and exposes inferior local estimates despite normal solver termination. These results establish a computational foundation for globally certified nested-logit estimation.
Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion

We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.
Schur-Positve Symmetric Functions from Products: Log-Majorization, Total-Positivity, and PSD Matrices

For a polynomial $F(t) = 1 + a_1 t + a_2 t^2 +\dots + a_d t^d$ with coefficients in a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $\mathcal{R}$, we consider Schur-positivity of the symmetric function $Ω_F(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{i \geq 1} F(x_i)$. Using work of Lindström and Gessel--Viennot, we give sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of directed networks. In the case when $F(t)$ is the multivariate independence polynomial of the incomparability graph $inc(P)$ of a natural unit interval order, we apply these ideas to give a new proof of Schur-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function $X_{inc(P)}(\mathbf{x})$. Additionally, we prove Schur-positivity of certain sums of chromatic symmetric functions, refining recent work of Amdeberhan--Shareshian--Stanley. In the case when $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{Q}[z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n]$, we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of symmetric function evaluations. In particular, we show for $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$, $s_λ(\mathbf{u}) \geq s_λ(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $λ$ if and only if $m_λ(\mathbf{u}) \geq m_λ(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $λ$, and these inequalities are equivalent to $\mathbf{u}$ log-majorizing $\mathbf{v}$. As an application for this result, we introduce the Kirchhoff symmetric function $K_G(\mathbf{x})$ of a loopless graph $G$ and show that it it always Schur-positive.
Saddle Codazzi tensor on spheres and hemisphere rigidity

Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 3$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. Our approach centers on saddle Codazzi tensors on round spheres, where the saddle condition requires the restriction to every tangent two-plane to have nonpositive determinant.
