The estimates extend to stable finite-energy Dirichlet $L^1$-weak solutions without an a priori local boundedness assumption, and an explicit logarithmic solution proves optimality in this class. Applications include global bounds in convex domains, bounded extremal solutions, and a Liouville theorem.
On the probability that a discrete IFR random variable exceeds its mean
Jianhang Ai; Vassilis Karagiannis; Ondřej Kuželka; Christos Pelekis

Let $X$ be an integer-valued random variable with $\mathbb{E}(|X|)<\infty$ whose survival probabilities $S_j=\mathbb{P}(X\ge j), j\in\mathbb{Z}$, form a log-concave sequence. Suppose that for some integer $m$ and some $γ\in (0, 1/2]$ it holds $\mathbb{E}(X)\ge m$ and $\mathbb{P}(X=m+1)\geγ\cdot\mathbb{P}(X=m)> 0$. It is shown that \[ \mathbb{P}(X \ge m+1) \,\ge\, \fracγ{1+2γ} \, , \] with the bound being best possible. As a consequence, it is shown that if $H \sim \text{Hyp}(n, i, k)$ is a hypergeometric random variable for which both $ik/n$ and $(n-i)(n-k)/n$ are at least $\log(4/3)$, then it holds $\mathbb{P}(H >\mathbb{E}(H)) \ge 1/4$ when $\mathbb{E}(H)$ is not an integer, and $\mathbb{P}(H >\mathbb{E}(H)) \ge 1/6$ when $\mathbb{E}(H)$ is an integer, both bounds being best possible.
Probabilistic large deviations approach to obstacle Hamilton-Jacobi equations

In this paper, we derive a non-classical variational representation of a viscosity solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation with obstacle, in which the Hamiltonian may take infinite values. We study a nonlinear selection-mutation model with an exponential-decay mutation kernel, using a probabilistic Feynman-Kac representation of a pure jump process. To handle the singular character of this process, we rely on a non-standard tool from large deviations theory, which allows us to establish a Varadhan-type lemma. This, in turn, yields the variational representation of the viscosity solution.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a semi-abelian category, $\mathcal{D}$ a Birkhoff subcategory of $\mathcal{C}$, and $I$ the associated reflector. For $C\in \mathcal{C}$, we establish an isomorphism between $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\check{C}(f,C))))$ (where $\mathrm{N}$ is the Moore normalization functor and $\check{C}(f,C)$ is a Cech resolution associated to $C$) and $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\mathbb{G}(C))))$ (where $\mathbb{G}(C)$ is the canonical $\mathbb{G}$-simplicial resolution of $C$ for $\mathbb{G}$ the comonad derived from an adjunction $F\colon \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{C}\dashv U\colon \mathcal{C}\to \mathcal{X}$ satisfying classical conditions introduced by Quillen). The former corresponds to the Hopf formula for the second homology object associated to $I$, while the latter represents the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$. Specifically, we show that both can be expressed by a single unified formula. Furthermore, we can also prove that, under certain assumptions, the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$ is naturally isomorphic to the first non-additive derived functor of $I$ (in the sense of Culot--Renaud--Van~der~Linden).
Planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
Zihao Geng; Zhiwen Wang; Wen-Jun Li; Xue-Ying Li; Qian-Qian Chen; Ji-Ming Guo

The problem posed by Hoffman, namely, to characterize graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most \(1\), was first studied by D.~M.~Cvetković in 1982 [\textit{Publ. Inst. Math. (Beograd)} \textbf{31} (1982), 15--20]. In this paper, we completely characterize all connected planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed $1$.
Numerical Analysis for a Nonlinear Coupled Thermoelastic System with Acoustic Boundary Conditions
Adriano A. Alcântara; Bruno A. Carmo; Juan B. Límaco; Carlos M. Guzmán

This paper presents the first $L^2$-norm error analysis for a nonlinear thermoelastic system with acoustic boundary conditions. The model involves three coupled variables: the acoustic potential $u$, the temperature $θ$, and the normal displacement to the boundary $δ$, with nonlinearities $|u|^d u$ in the domain and $g(\cdot,u')$ on the boundary, in addition to a nonlocal term $β(\int_Ωθdx)Δθ$ in the heat equation. We establish error estimates for the fully discrete problem, using the Crank-Nicolson method for time discretization and finite element method with basis of degree $r \geqslant 1$ for space discretization. We demonstrate that the domain-boundary coupling induces a half-power loss in the spatial convergence order for the variable $u$, and this effect propagates to the remaining variables due to the thermoelastic and boundary couplings, resulting in the final error estimate $\mathcal{O}(h^{r+\frac{1}{2}} + τ^2)$. A bootstrap argument is employed to ensure the uniform boundedness of $\|U_h^n\|_{L^\infty}$, which is essential for handling the nonlinearity. Numerical results using Lagrange finite element basis of degrees $ r = 1, 2, 3 $ (linear, quadratic, and cubic) corroborate the theoretical estimates and illustrate the transition from suboptimal to optimal convergence orders when the exact solution possesses additional $L^\infty$ regularity.
Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions II
Zheng-chao Han; Qinfeng Jiang; Hua-Yang Wang; Jingang Xiong; Lei Zhang

This is the second of two papers on isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation on manifolds with nonflat background metrics. In the first paper, we proved that, in dimensions $3\le n\le29$, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a radial model singular solution in the flat metric on the Euclidean space with origin as its singular point---a Fowler solution. In the present paper, we show that this dimension range is sharp. More precisely, for each $n\ge30$, we construct a smooth metric on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ and a positive solution of the corresponding Yamabe equation having an isolated singularity, near which the solution blows up along a sequence at a rate much faster than that of Fowler solutions. Moreover, the singular solution defines a complete conformal metric of constant positive scalar curvature and the metric agrees with the round metric to infinite order at the singular point.
A least-squares lower bound for capacity

We establish a least-squares lower bound for the logarithmic capacity of an arbitrary compact plane set, extending an inequality previously known for connected sets. The bound generalizes classical inequalities involving area and moment of inertia. It is sharp for disks, and asymptotically sharp for compact sets whose capacity coincides with that of their interior. We further show that asymptotic sharpness holds for general compact sets if we replace logarithmic capacity by minimal carrier capacity.
Density of length ratios on Teichmüller space

We study length ratios of simple closed geodesics on finite-type hyperbolic surfaces of positive genus. We allow cusps and fix the geodesic boundary lengths. Let $d$ be the dimension of the corresponding Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. We prove that for every positive vector $(r_0,\ldots,r_d)$, the set of surfaces carrying $d+1$ distinct essential interior simple closed geodesics with lengths proportional to this vector is dense in $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. In particular, one-holed tori with three distinct simple closed geodesics of equal length are dense. The proof uses high powers of Dehn twists, asymptotics of length differentials, and the Brouwer fixed-point theorem.

For a fixed nonempty finite set $L$ of positive integers and $k=\max L\ge2$, let $\binom{[n]}{L}=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}\binom{[n]}{\ell}$ denote the non-uniform hypergraph whose edge set consists of all $\ell$-subsets of $[n]$ for $\ell\in L$. A $1$-factor of a hypergraph $H$ is a collection of pairwise disjoint edges whose union is $V(H)$. We say $H$ is $1$-factorable if $E(H)$ can be partitioned into $1$-factors. In this paper, we study the 1-factorability of $\binom{[n]}{L}$. Earlier work of He, Huang, and Ma shows that, for all sufficiently large $n$, $1$-factorability can occur only in the residue classes $0$ and $-1$ modulo $k$: it always occurs in class $0$, whereas it occurs in class $-1$ only if $k-1\in L$. We determine exactly when $1$-factorability occurs in this exceptional class. More precisely, we define a finite gcd-peeling algorithm on $L\setminus\{k-1,k\}$ and prove that $\binom{[qk-1]}{L}$ is $1$-factorable if and only if the algorithm accepts. As a consequence, our result provides a criterion for the $1$-factorability of $\binom{[n]}{L}$ and confirms the conjecture posed by He, Huang, and Ma.
Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity

We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for Hölder continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.
Symmetry and Monotonicity for Subcritical Fractional Hartree Equations with Singular Sets of Zero Capacity
Guangze Gu; Aleks Jevnikar; Zhipeng Yang

We study positive weak singular solutions of the subcritical fractional Hartree equation \[ (-Δ)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^μ}d y \right)u^q \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(N>2s\), \(0<μ<N\), and \(Γ\subset\{x_1=0\}\) is compact with zero \((s,2)\)-capacity. For solutions with a nonremovable singular point on $Γ$, we prove hyperplane symmetry and strict transverse monotonicity under global Lebesgue integrability conditions. For $N\ge2$, we also prove these conclusions under upper bounds on $p$ and $q$, using only the integrability required for weak solutions. We also establish local regularity and construct solutions with logarithmic singularities along a line segment.
Model Theory of Products of Chains

We show that regarding the model-theoretic properties of distributive lattices isomorphic to finite products of linear orders there is a significant symmetry: if ${\mathbb X}_i$, $i<n$ are linear orders of size $>1$, ${\mathcal T}:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits (\prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X} _i)$ and ${\mathcal T}_i:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits ({\mathbb X}_i)$, for $i<n$, then ${\mathcal T}$ is finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small) iff ${\mathcal T}_i$, $i<n$, are finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small); the countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) model of ${\mathcal T}$, if it exists, is the product of countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) models of ${\mathcal T}_i$; further, we describe all models of ${\mathcal T}$: ${\mathbb Y} \models {\mathcal T}$ iff ${\mathbb Y}\cong \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb Y}_i$, where ${\mathbb Y} _i \models {\mathcal T}_i$, for $i<n$, and show that ${\mathbb E} \preccurlyeq \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X}_i$ iff ${\mathbb E} = \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb E}_i$, where ${\mathbb E}_i \preccurlyeq {\mathbb X}_i$, for $i<n$. ($I({\mathcal T},ω)\in \{ 1,{\mathfrak{c}}\}$ was proved in a previous paper.) In addition, for each $n\in {\mathbb N}$ the class ${\mathcal C}_n$ of distributive lattices isomorphic to a direct product of $n$ linear orders of size $>1$ is first order definable.

Inspired by the two-parameter continuity-path approach of Chen and Xu, we employ a modified continuity path to characterize the solvability of the Hessian quotient equation for Kähler metrics with Poincaré-type singularities along a divisor D, allowing simple normal crossings and self-intersections.
Spectra of Multivariate Vandermonde Matrices and Min-max Error Bounds for the High-dimensional Super-resolution Problem

We study multivariate rectangular Vandermonde matrices $U_N$ whose rows are indexed by the grid $G_N=\{-N,\ldots,N\}^d, $ and whose columns correspond to irregularly spaced points on the unit $d$-dimensional torus. Motivated by the problem of super-resolution (recovery of spike trains from low frequency noisy measurements), we consider configurations in which the points form several clusters, with points within each cluster separated by at most $h$ and distinct clusters are well-separated. We show that the column subspaces associated with different clusters are nearly orthogonal, i.e. for $N \rightarrow \infty, Nh \ll 1$, the minimal principal angle between any such pair is at least $ {π\over 2} - \frac{C_1}{N} - C_2Nh - \frac{C_3}{\sqrt{N}}, $ for some constants $C_1,C_2,C_3$ independent of $N$ and $h$. This near-orthogonality enables the spectral analysis of such $U_N$ to be reduced to the analysis of each individual cluster. As a consequence, we derive sharp scaling for all singular values of $U_N$, revealing how the geometry of clustered points controls the conditioning of the high-dimensional super-resolution problems. Then we establish min-max error bounds for the recovery of clustered point sources, requiring only an upper bound on the largest cluster size and no knowledge of the geometry within the clusters. These bounds coincide with the optimal rates known in the one-dimensional setting. Furthermore, when the clustered points are in generic position (i.e. do not lie on a low-dimensional algebraic variety) our results indicate that super-resolution in high dimensions is more stable than in one dimension.
On the Proportion of Time that a Conventional Confidence Interval Covers

The concept of confidence sequences, or `anytime confidence intervals,' has attracted significant interest in recent years. This motivates the question of how well conventional confidence intervals behave when similarly evaluated. In particular, we study the probability distribution of the proportion of time a conventional confidence interval procedure covers the population mean, when the total time $n$ spent sampling is large. We establish an invariance principle for the limiting distribution as $n$ tends to infinity and show that the limit random variable $Z(1)$ can be expressed as a functional of Brownian motion. The random variable $Z(1)$ exhibits a scale invariance property that enables the derivation of a partial differential equation (PDE) for the density of $Z(1)$ jointly with the Brownian motion at $t=1$, namely $B(1)$. We show that this density can also be computed as the stationary distribution of a two-dimensional singular diffusion, one component of which is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We then derive an approximating Markov chain that allows us to numerically solve the PDE. This density has a number of interesting features that provide various insights into the time-averaged coverage proportion problem.
Inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic identities,series and products for Lucas sequences

In 1936 Lehmer observed that the inverse tangents of the reciprocals of the odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers add up exactly to a quarter of $π$. Many formulas of the same kind have been found since, each with its own proof: for the inverse tangent and for the inverse hyperbolic tangent, for sums and for differences, for the Fibonacci numbers and for the Lucas numbers. We show that these are not different results but one and the same computation, seen through three signs. A single two-term identity, valid for the generalized Fibonacci sequence and its companion Lucas sequence of any parameter, contains them all. From it follow, with short telescoping proofs, infinitely many series for $π$ whose speed of convergence can be chosen at will, series whose sums are multiples of the logarithm of the golden ratio and of its analogues, and infinite and finite products with closed values. The Fibonacci and Lucas cases are listed in full; the classical formulas of Lehmer, of Hoggatt and Ruggles, of Melham and Shannon and of Melham appear among them, and the Pell cases, among them those of Mahon and Horadam, the Jacobsthal cases, where the logarithm of the golden ratio is replaced by that of $2$, the Mersenne numbers and the Chebyshev polynomials follow by substitution.
Derived equivalences and isogenies of supersingular abelian varieties
An Jiang; Zhiyuan Li; Ziwei Lu

We study (twisted) Fourier-Mukai partners of supersingular abelian varieties. We give a simple proof that any two supersingular abelian varieties of the same dimension at least two are derived isogenous, answering a question raised by Li, Lu, and Tang and generalizing the result of Li and Zou. Moreover, in every dimension greater than two, we construct derived-equivalent supersingular abelian varieties whose corresponding positive powers are never isomorphic. We also give conditions under which derived equivalence between two supersingular principally polarized abelian varieties implies that their underlying abelian varieties are isomorphic. In particular, this implication holds in dimensions at most three.
Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
Tshifhiwa Murovhi; Mensah Folly-Gbetoula; Kwassi Anani

A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.
The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$

We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.
Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces

We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.
Void probabilities for perturbed lattices under mixing

We study void probabilities for stationary perturbed lattices with possibly dependent perturbations. Our main result gives a general upper bound in terms of two ingredients: the number of lattice sites having a uniformly positive probability of hitting the observation set, and the $α$-mixing rate of the perturbation field. For unions of lattice cubes, this yields explicit bounds without moment or regularity assumptions on the marginal distribution of the perturbations. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative estimates for growing bounded Borel sets with non-empty interior, including stretched-exponential decay under exponential mixing and polynomial decay under polynomial mixing.
Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps

Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.
Optimal degree bounds for sum-of-squares representations
Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer; Sander Gribling; Didier Henrion; Milan Korda; Poornendu Kumar; Victor Magron; Lucas Slot; Luis Felipe Vargas; Juan Vera

The moment-sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy provides a sequence of bounds on the minimum of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set, i.e., a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by finitely many polynomial constraints. We establish optimal bounds on the error of the SOS hierarchy in the following settings: 1. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module: the error of the Putinar-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^4/k^2)$ in the worst case. 2. If the constraints define a compact semialgebraic set: the error of the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^2/k^2)$ in the worst case. 3. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module and satisfy linear independence constraint qualification conditions (LICQ): the error of the hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ(1/k^{4})$ in the worst case. Here, the upper bound holds already for the Putinar-based hierarchy, while the lower bound holds even against the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy. Equivalently, these give best-possible effective versions of Putinar's and Schmüdgen's Positivstellensätze for these settings (in terms of their dependence on $k$).
The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
Siyuan Fu; Stephen S. -T. Yau; Huaiqing Zuo
This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.
Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays

We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.
Random Tournaments Are Asymptotically Almost Surely Link-irregular

Bastien and Khormali (2025) conjectured that a nontrivial link-irregular tournament with $n$ vertices exists if and only if $n \ge 6$. Their work establishes the conjecture for $n \le 100$. We present a probabilistic argument for the existence of link-irregular tournaments with $n$ vertices when $n \ge 9$ to resolve the conjecture. In fact, we show that a random tournament is asymptotically almost surely link-irregular.
Signed FK percolation in Ising spin glasses
Alberto Gandolfi; Charles Newman; Danile Stein

We introduce signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) percolation for the +/-J random-interaction Ising model to characterize nonzero uniform magnetization density and two-replica overlap within the class of Gibbs distributions whose infinite-volume Edwards-Sokal (ES)/FK representation has at most one infinite FK cluster almost surely. The construction refines ordinary FK connectivity by retaining the parity of coupling products along open paths. Using the infinite-volume ES representation and its DLR equations, we study pairs of companion objects and the compatible spin assignments on them. In one replica, companions are defined by positive-parity FK connections. For extremal states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of companion densities along the chosen van Hove sequence, nonzero limiting expected magnetization density is equivalent to density distinguishability of the companions of the infinite FK cluster. For two independent replicas, companions are defined by FK connections coherent in parity. For products of extremal one-replica states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of the companion densities along the chosen sequence, density distinguishability of the companions is equivalent to nonzero limiting expected mutual overlap. For two independent replicas drawn from the same extremal state, this specializes to the Edwards-Anderson self-overlap.

We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.
Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
Lapin K. S.; Lapin S. V

In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.
Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual

For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_σ$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $σ(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_σ$ is $σ$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_σ$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_σ$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.
Human Exposition of Claude's 2/3 Theorem on the zeros of zeta

We expose Claude's proof that $N_0(T)\ge 0.6725 N(T)$ where $N(T)$ is the number of zeros of zeta satisfying $0<\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}ρ\le T$, and $N_0(T)$ the number of those zeros that are simple and on the critical line. Unconditionally it was only known that $N_0(T)\ge 0.4166 N(T)$. This proof is simpler than the previous ones and takes a different approach.
Length-convexity and domination for Hitchin representations

Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. For any $n\geq 3$, let $\text{Hit}_n(S)$ be the Hitchin component and let $\text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ be the subset of representations that take values in $\mathrm{PSp}_{2m}(\mathbb{R})$ if $n=2m$ and $\mathrm{PSO}(m,m+1)$ if $n=2m+1$. In this note we prove that for any Hitchin representation $ρ\in \text{Hit}_n(S)$ there is $j \in \text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ such that $ρ$ dominates $j$ in the Hilbert length spectrum; this confirms a conjecture of Lee-Zhang and, independently, Tholozan who had proved this for $n=3$. The key step is establishing a convexity of the Hilbert length function in the Bonahon-Dreyer parametrization of $\text{Hit}_n(S)$; this uses a result from the recent work of Barman-Gupta. We also prove these convexity and domination results for translation length functions and their spectra.
Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
Iva Bačić; Carsten Hartmann; Philipp C. Böttcher; David Gross; Andrea Benigni; Dirk Witthaut

Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.
Strong generation of the chiral algebra of $\mathcal N=4$~$SU(N)$ super Yang--Mills theory

The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic--odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.
Local quadratic convergence of iterated correlation matrices: bounds and counterexamples

Kruskal's unpublished manuscript on CONCOR gives a local argument for convergence of successive correlations to a prescribed two-class sign pattern. We identify a failure in its stated one-step estimate and establish a replacement bound for correlation matrices in arbitrary dimension. A geometric estimate for sign-aligned centered rows yields an explicit sufficient neighbourhood of convergence and a quadratic error bound. We construct invariant families of correlation matrices with an exact scalar recurrence in every dimension at least three. These families yield counterexamples to the original estimate in every dimension at least four. The failure persists on relatively open sets of positive-definite correlation matrices. In dimensions divisible by four, an explicitly solvable subfamily provides counterexamples arbitrarily close to the prescribed fixed point and attains the asymptotic coefficient in the new bound. Quadratic order is attained by the constructed families in every dimension at least three. These counterexamples concern the quantitative estimate, not the convergence conclusion: all the exhibited trajectories converge to their prescribed sign patterns.
The fractional Calderón problem on finite Cayley graphs

We study a Calderón-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.
Complex Representatives, Similarity Invariants, and Iterates in $\bf{U(1,1;\mathbb{H})}$
Bingzhe Hou; Cailing Yao; Jiaxing He

We study the similarity classes of matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ and the iterates of their associated quaternionic Möbius transformations. Building on the known elliptic case, we show that every parabolic or loxodromic element of $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ is similar, via a matrix in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$, to a complex matrix. Explicit complex representatives and matrices realizing these similarities are constructed for the different types. We then introduce the invariants $\operatorname{Tr}(T), Δ(T), η(T), κ(T)$, and prove that they form a complete system of similarity invariants for matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$. Finally, using the complex representation of quaternionic matrices and Chebyshev polynomials, we derive a fourth-order recurrence for a real sequence $(q_n)$ satisfying $Δ(T^n)=q_n^2Δ(T)$. Together with recurrence relations for the relevant matrix entries, this identity yields a complete classification of the quaternionic Möbius transformation associated with $T^n$, including the degenerate cases in which $Δ(T^n)=0$.
Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem

We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]
Short proof that Vopěnka's Principle is symmetrically stable

We show that Vopěnka's Principle is stable under symmetric extensions. Recently, de Groot and Woloszyn [1] proved this fact. We found the proof of this theorem unnecessarily complicated. In this short note we prove the same statement. We direct the reader to [3] for an exposition on symmetric extensions.
Energy-minimized interpolatory B-spline lofting for sequences of closed contours

B-spline lofting through closed cross-sections is common in reverse engineering, but interpolating each section on its own knot vector can produce an unnecessarily large control net. We construct a common-knot method for closed section curves of odd and even degree by minimizing the strain energy of each section subject to its interpolation constraints. Feasibility for closed section data and uniqueness of the resulting saddle-point solution require full row rank of the periodic collocation matrices, a property that a previously proposed periodic Schoenberg-Whitney window condition does not always guarantee. We establish the exact parity distinction: the condition is sufficient at odd point counts but admits singular configurations at every admissible even point count. For the odd and even degrees used here, the natural and shifting anchor knots are nonsingular; at odd point counts the window condition certifies the selected candidate, whereas at even point counts a rank test with an anchor fallback is applied. The lofting method therefore retains a nonsingular square subsystem for each section and uses nestedness to transfer full row rank to the rectangular common-knot system. Across six closed-contour models the common-knot method uses 83-98% fewer control points than traditional interpolating lofting, with section energies no larger than those of a previous knot-selection method within numerical precision.
Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories

We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion, and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.
Rapid convergence of Langevin AIS for multimodal distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$

We study annealed importance sampling (AIS) driven by the overdamped Langevin diffusion, targeting a multimodal Gibbs measure $π_\varepsilon \propto e^{-U/\varepsilon}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ at low temperature $\varepsilon$. For a potential $U$ with nondegenerate critical points, finitely many wells of comparable mass, and at least quadratic growth at infinity, we show that AIS with a harmonically spaced temperature schedule produces a weighted empirical measure that approximates $π_\varepsilon$ to accuracy $δ$ at a total cost of order $\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-2}$, up to logarithmic factors, and the exponents do not depend on the dimension. This is an exponential improvement over plain Langevin Monte Carlo, whose relaxation time obeys the Arrhenius law. The assumptions cover, in particular, the potentials of Gaussian mixtures, as long as their critical points are nondegenerate and their wells carry comparable mass. The analysis extends that of arXiv:2604.17526 [math.PR] from the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ to the noncompact state space $\mathbb{R}^d$. The two new ingredients are a weighted $L^\infty$ bound on the eigenfunctions of the Langevin generator, obtained by combining Agmon estimates at infinity with a local maximum principle near the critical points, and a Weyl-type eigenvalue count derived from the Cwikel-Lieb-Rozenblum and Lieb-Thirring inequalities. For potentials with more than two wells the eigenfunction bound requires an additional argument, which we give by constructing a perturbation of $U$ that renders every saddle an effective local maximum.
Discrete Phase-Shift Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces using Uniform Reference Directions
Pavithra P.; Manoj Kumar Panda; Chandramani Singh

Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) enable programmable control of the wireless propagation environment through adjustable reflecting elements. A fundamental challenge in RIS-assisted communications is the optimization of discrete phase shifts to maximize the received signal power. While recently developed algorithms can obtain optimal solutions with linear complexity, their computational cost may still be excessive in applications requiring large-scale simulations, real-time adaptation, or repeated optimization over numerous channel realizations. This paper proposes a low-complexity discrete phase-shift optimization algorithm based on multiple reference directions within the feasible optimality sector. By evaluating candidate phase configurations generated from uniformly distributed reference directions, the proposed method systematically improves upon existing approximation approaches that rely on a fixed set of reference directions. The number of reference directions serves as a design parameter that enables a controllable trade-off between computational complexity and optimality. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves substantial computational speedups while maintaining a small optimality gap relative to the optimal solution. The results further show that increasing the number of reference directions progressively reduces the optimality gap, providing flexible operating points that can be tailored to application-specific complexity and performance requirements.
Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals

The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the Gârleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.
Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions

In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $α$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.
Special identities of nonsymmetric bicommutative operations in associative algebra with an operator

Let $A$ be an associative non-unital algebra with a linear operator $S$ satisfying \[aS(S(b)c)=S(aS(b))c,\] and define $a\prec b=aS(b)$ and $a\succ b=S(a)b$. We determine the special identities of these two operations. If $K_n$ is the arity-$n$ kernel of the corresponding operad morphism and $D_n$ is the space of consequences of smaller-arity kernel elements, then for every $n\geq8$ the quotient $K_n/D_n$ has dimension $n-2$. A basis is given by the classes of $F_{n-2}$, $ρF_{n-2}$, $G_{n-3}$, $ρG_{n-3}$, $J_{n-4}$, $ρJ_{n-4}$ and $H_{p,n-p-1}$, $4\leq p\leq n-5$. The upper bound is proved by a direct reduction of singleton sectors, using pure normalization, rigid boundary contraction and the four-singleton corner. The lower bound is obtained from coefficient functionals and a corner projection. In particular, new independent special identities occur in every arity $n\geq8$, and the operadic kernel is not finitely generated.
Unique Factorization of Power Series Rings over Q-UFDs of Dimension at Most 3

Let $R$ be a Noetherian unique factorization domain containing $\mathbb Q$, with $\dim R\leq3$. We prove that $R[[t]]$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if two conditions hold: every two-generated parameter ideal $q$ in every height-two localization satisfies $\overline{q^2}\subseteq q$, and every height-three localization has depth three. No excellence or completion hypothesis is imposed. The main local result is that $A[[t]]$ is not a UFD whenever $A$ is a local $\mathbb Q$-UFD of dimension at least three and depth two. We also prove that the UFD property of $R[[t]]$ passes to every coefficient localization in dimension at most three, give an all-dimensional criterion when the completions of the maximal localizations satisfy Serre's condition $(S_2)$, and obtain an arbitrary-characteristic criterion for excellent UFDs of dimension at most three.
Equivariant Moment Maps and the Ricci Cocycle in Weighted Fujiki--Donaldson Theory

Let $(M,ω)$ be a closed connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$,. We discuss weighted Fujiki--Donaldson theory with respect to the measure $dν=e^hω^n/n! $ for an arbitrary smooth real-valued function $h$ on $M$. We prove that the group generated by the flows of Hamiltonians that Poisson-commute with $h$ always admits an equivariant moment map for its action on the full space of $ω$-compatible almost complex structures. The moment map takes values in the continuous dual of the Lie algebra. Its density is expressed in terms of the Hermitian scalar curvature, a local weight correction, and an $L^\infty$ function $r_h^0$ constructed from the long-time average of the polar determinant phase. The function $r_h^0$ can be regarded as a Ruelle-type asymptotic density incorporating phase comparison via a connection. The key step in the proof is to represent the Ricci cocycle as the coboundary of a continuous cochain constructed from $r_h^0$. We also consider the action of the exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on a connected component of the space of almost complex structures inducing the given orientation on a closed connected oriented manifold of real dimension $2n$. In contrast to the weighted Hamiltonian setting, we prove that, for $n>1$, this action admits an equivariant moment map if and only if the real first Chern class vanishes.
Comment on "The polarization hierarchy for polynomial optimization over convex bodies, with applications to nonnegative matrix rank"

We revisit the feasibility and convergence claims for the polarization hierarchy of Plávala, Ligthart and Gross [Linear Algebra Appl.\ 723 (2025) 15--32]. Counterexamples show that the stated assumption is insufficient for the feasibility characterization and for convergence of the hierarchy with the polarization constraint. We establish corrected results under a stronger algebraic condition and supply a missing compactness argument.
A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics

For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.
Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles

We study nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with finite-sum objectives and fully first-order oracles. We propose Sampled Implicit Corrections for Bilevel Optimization (SICBO), which combines a penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for the lower-level variables. Under componentwise lower strong convexity, SICBO finds a point $x$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\|\nablaΦ(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$ within $\tilde{O}(N+\sqrt{N}κ^{7/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient calls, where $N$ is the total number of components and $κ$ is the normalized lower-level condition number. The bound achieves square-root finite-sum dependence using only gradients and preserves the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number exponent for smooth problems. Our improvement follows from a curvature-dependent bound for nonlinear correction errors, which permits epochs of length $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{N/κ})$ with batches of size $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{Nκ})$. A single-level reduction shows that the dependence on $N$ and $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed $κ$.
Extension of surjective isometries between unit spheres of $\ell^p$-direct sums

We study surjective isometries between the unit spheres of Banach spaces of the form $A\oplus_p B$, where $A$ is nonzero and strictly convex, $1<p<\infty$, and every unit vector of $B\neq\{0\}$ has at least two distinct unit vectors at distance $2$. For two direct sums $A_i\oplus_{p_i}B_i$, $i=1,2$, satisfying these hypotheses, we prove that every surjective isometry $$Δ:S_{A_1\oplus_{p_1}B_1}\to S_{A_2\oplus_{p_2} B_2}$$ between their unit spheres forces equality of the direct-sum exponents $p_i$ and extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry $$\widetildeΔ:A_1\oplus_p B_1\to A_2\oplus_p B_2$$ preserving the corresponding components, where $p:=p_1=p_2$. The proof identifies the component unit spheres through diametral sets and distance formulas, and then constructs isometries between the component unit balls. As a principal application, we obtain extension and representation results for absolutely continuous functions equipped with norms combining evaluation at a fixed point and the $L^1$-norm of the derivative. We also discuss Lipschitz and differentiable function spaces, distinguishing the consequences of our theorem from those already covered by existing extension results. Endpoint conclusions are derived separately, including the Mazur-Ulam property for the real absolutely continuous space with the sum norm.
Analysis and approximation for inverse potential problem of space-dependent variable-exponent sub-diffusion in heterogeneous medium
Zhiyuan Li; Chunlong Sun; Xiangcheng Zheng

Anomalous transport in complex heterogeneous medium is often characterized by non-Markovian memory effects and spatially varying trapping properties. From the point of view of continuous-time random walks, such heterogeneity can be described by a position-dependent heavy-tailed waiting-time density $q(t \mid x)\sim C(x)t^{-1-α(x)}$, where $0<α(x)<1$ is the local anomalous exponent. This microscopic interpretation naturally leads to the sub-diffusion with a space-dependent variable exponent $α(x)$. Compared with constant-exponent models, the variable-exponent fractional operators generally do not commute with the spatial Laplacian, which makes both the forward and inverse analysis substantially more delicate. This paper investigates the inverse problem of recovering a spatially dependent radiative or potential coefficient in variable-exponent sub-diffusion from terminal observation data. We formulate the inverse problem as a nonlinear fixed-point equation and prove that the associated fixed-point operator is monotone such that the fixed-point iteration converges decreasingly to the unique solution. We further establish a Lipschitz-type conditional stability estimate for the terminal observation map, which also implies uniqueness of the inverse problem for sufficiently large terminal time. For numerical reconstruction, we develop a fully discrete finite element scheme and derive an error estimate for the inverse problem. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the method, even in the presence of noisy data.
Skew-Symmetric Formulations and Energy-Stable Schemes for Compressible Reactive Flow Equations

This paper develops skew-symmetric formulations and energy stable finite difference schemes for the reactive Euler and reactive Navier--Stokes equations. By introducing suitable transformed variables, we rewrite the governing equations into skew-symmetric forms and obtain continuous energy estimates by standard integration-by-parts arguments. The proposed formulations extend the skew-symmetric framework for compressible flow equations to reactive systems, where the chemical energy and the species equation must be incorporated into the transformed variables. Based on these formulations, we construct semi-discrete schemes with summation-by-parts (SBP) operators. The convective terms are discretized by the non-dissipative part of linear upwind SBP operators, while a nonlinear SBP--WENO operator is used only to supply artificial dissipation near discontinuities. For periodic boundary conditions, the resulting schemes satisfy semi-discrete energy estimates consistent with the continuous analysis. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions validate the designed order of accuracy and demonstrate stable performance for problems with shocks, viscous layers, detonation-type waves, and complex wave interactions.
Multicolor Ramsey numbers of unbalanced double stars

For integers $n\ge m\ge1$, let $S(n,m)$ be the double star obtained by joining the centers of $K_{1,n}$ and $K_{1,m}$. Ruotolo and Song proved the upper bound $r(S(n,m);k)\le kn+m+2$ under the condition $(n+1)\lceil\frac{n+1}{k-1}\rceil >m((k-1)n+m)$, as well as the matching lower bound for odd $k$. Zhao, Mao and Zhou proved the matching lower bound for even $k$ and even $n$. We establish the remaining lower bound for even $k\ge6$ and odd $n$ through a new edge-coloring construction. Combining these results, we obtain $r(S(n,m);k)=kn+m+2$ for all integers $k\ge5$ and $n\ge m\ge1$ satisfying $(n+1)\lceil\frac{n+1}{k-1}\rceil >m((k-1)n+m)$. We also determine the four-color Ramsey number for $m\ge2$ and odd $n\ge15m$, showing that $r(S(n,m);4)=4n+m+1$.
Local energy and vertex deletion for $A_α$-matrices

We study the change in the trace norm and the centred energy of the $A_α$-matrix of a graph under vertex deletion. A pinching argument proves that the trace norm is nondecreasing under passage from an induced subgraph to the original graph, and gives a lower bound in terms of the edges induced by the deleted vertices. Exact perturbation spectra yield sharp upper bounds for deleting a vertex or an independent set of vertices with a common neighbourhood. For $0<α<1/2$, equality in these upper bounds is characterized by star and complete bipartite components, respectively. For the centred energy, we derive explicit deletion bounds and classify all connected equality graphs for $0\leα<1$: the extremal graphs are stars and complete bipartite graphs for single-vertex and independent-twin deletion, respectively. We also characterize equality in the general-set trace-norm lower bound and prove strictness of the total centred-energy inequality for connected nonregular graphs when $0<α<1$. Examples show that centred local energy can be negative and that the degree deviation term cannot be omitted in general.
Curvature Effects on Boundary Accumulation of Self-Propelled Particles: A Fokker-Planck Approach
Jingyi Fu; Jinqi Liu; Benoit Perthame; Min Tang

It is well known that self-propelled particles tend to accumulate near boundaries. Although the influence of boundary geometry on this accumulation has been extensively studied using individual-based models, a population-level PDE description becomes desirable when a large number of particles are involved. In this work, we investigate boundary accumulation of self-propelled particles confined in two-dimensional circular and annular domains. We develop Fokker--Planck models that qualitatively reproduce the behavior observed in individual-based simulations. The main contribution is the formulation of appropriate evolution equations for particles accumulated at the boundary, incorporating transitions between the interior free-swimming state and the boundary-contact state. Starting from a general spatial two-dimensional model, we simplify the associated boundary conditions by assuming radial symmetry and then design an exponentially weighted difference scheme that preserves the total mass of the coupled system. Because transitions between different particle states induce singular behavior near the boundary, establishing discrete mass conservation is nontrivial. In particular, the velocity space must be divided into two subdomains, with the resulting discontinuity treated explicitly. Stochastic simulations and numerical experiments are performed both to validate the proposed models and to investigate the effects of geometric and dynamical parameters on boundary accumulation.
The Siemons--Wagner property and Bradley's conjecture

A transitive permutation group $G\le\Sym(\Pcal)$ is said to have the Siemons--Wagner property $\star_3$ if some three-point subset has a $G$-orbit longer than the orbit of every four-point subset containing it. In this paper we develop a structural theory of three-point orbits of finite $2$-transitive groups (orbit-length hierarchies, pointwise and setwise stabilizers, and their geometric realisations, including the unital and the ovoid), and we use it to completely settle Bradley's conjecture: a finite primitive group of degree at least $8$ satisfying $\star_3$ is isomorphic to $\PSL(2,7)$ or $\PGL(2,7)$.
The Segal-Bargmann Transform in Neural Partial Differential Equations
Jie Xu; Julio Castrillón-Candás; Mark Kon; Qinxun Bai

We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order $ L^{-\frac{1}{2}} $, where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control $ \sup_{x}\lvert\hat{u}_{NO} - u_{truth}\rvert $ for solutions of PDEs $ \mathcal{L}u = f $ which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.
The Neumann problem for stochastic partial differential equations

In this paper, we study the Neumann problem for second-order stochastic partial differential equations in the half space. The coefficients are random and merely measurable in time. We develop a class of weighted function spaces for this problem, and establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity results. In contrast to the Dirichlet problem, the Neumann problem admits solutions with improved boundary regularity under suitable assumptions on the coefficients and data.
Riemannian Submersion whose Total Manifold admits an Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
Sonali Jaiswal; Akhilesh Yadav; S. S. Shukla

In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.
Kennett L. Dela Rosa; Eloise P. Misa

The zero-trace index $t(A)$ of a square complex matrix $A$ is introduced. It is defined as the largest integer $k$ such that $A$ admits a $k \times k$ compression with trace zero. This concept is analogous to the zero-dilation index $d(A)$ and is closely related to the $k$-numerical range. The $k$-numerical range is characterized as an intersection of half-planes, which is used to derive a formula for $t(A)$ that reduces its computation to the Hermitian case. Conditions for $t(A) = d(A)$ are also established, and matrices satisfying $t(A) = n - 1$ are characterized. Finally, the zero-trace index is determined for several classes of matrices.

A coloring of the edges of a complete graph with $r$ colors is balanced if the edges among any $r+1$ vertices use all $r$ colors. Erdős and Gyárfás (1999) conjectured that for all $r\ge3$ the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ has no balanced $r$-coloring. They proved the conjecture for $r=3$ and $r=4$. We prove the conjecture for $r=5$, the first new case settled in over two decades. There is no balanced $5$-coloring of $K_{26}$, and since $K_{25}$ has one, $K_{25}$ is the largest complete graph admitting a balanced $5$-coloring. We design a reduce--dispatch--enumerate workflow, where every machine step produces an artifact that can be independently checked. First, we use a machine-checked (Lean 4) proof to reduce the conjecture to a single extremal statement about the color class with the fewest edges: no graph on $26$ vertices has between $55$ and $65$ edges while every $6$ of its vertices span between $1$ and $11$ edges. We then search on the sparse class instead of its dense complement, which makes enumeration up to isomorphism feasible. With classical stability theorems for $K_6$-free graphs, we dispatch the five near-extremal edge counts analytically. For the exhaustive enumeration on the remaining six edge counts, we design efficient encodings with SAT modulo symmetries and parallel cube-and-conquer. We also certify all eleven edge counts: each of the $12{,}296$ subproblems carries a clausal refutation checked by the independent verifier drat-trim, and all $273{,}503{,}938$ symmetry-breaking clauses are also validated against the vertex permutations that justify them.
Mohammad Afzali; Hassan Ashtiani; Adam Smith

We study differentially private black-box evaluation of arbitrary high-dimensional functions. Given a dataset $S$ and query access to a function $f$---whose sensitivity may be unknown or unbounded---the goal is to privately output an approximation to $f(S)$. The black-box evaluator can only query the value of $f$ over a down neighborhood of $S$ (i.e., those subsets of $S$ that are obtained by removing a bounded number of elements from $S$). We design generic black-box evaluators for both pure and approximate differential privacy through a reduction to high-dimensional private quasi-concave optimization (QCO). Our black-box evaluator enjoys a geometric notion of utility. Consider the vectors obtained by applying $f$ on sets in a down neighborhood of $S$. With high probability, the evaluator's output is guaranteed to be in the convex hull of these vectors. Our work generalizes the result of Linder et al. [LRSS25] for real-valued function evaluation to high dimensions. It also recovers the private center-point guarantees of Beimel et al. [BMNS19], with an explicit additive approximation to maximum Tukey depth. We also apply our evaluators to user-level quasi-concave and convex optimization, showing how they can improve upon the sample-and-aggregate baseline of Nissim et al. [NRS07] by replacing the multiplicative data overhead with an additive overhead. Finally, we show that our formulation of high dimensional black-box evaluation and high dimensional private QCO are equivalent up to a factor of the dimension: the hardest private evaluation instances already arise from the cases that $f$ is a (non-private) quasi-concave optimizer.
A frequency localized maximum principle and its applications to time fractional equations with rough coefficients

We establish a frequency localized maximum principle for parabolic second-order partial differential equations with the Caputo time fractional derivative $\partial_t^α$ of order $α\in(0,1)$. The leading coefficients are uniformly elliptic, measurable in time, and independent of space. We construct suitable equivalent norms on frequency localized subspaces of $L_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for which a frequency localized maximum principle holds. The corresponding result may fail in the usual $L_\infty$ norm even for the classical heat equation. As an application, we prove existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates in Sobolev-Zygmund spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in time for equations with spatially variable coefficients and zero initial data. The coefficients are strongly measurable in time with values in a Hölder-Zygmund space of positive order and uniformly bounded in this space.

Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).
A Gauge-Invariant Finite Element Method for the Time-Dependent Ginzburg--Landau Equations
Huadong Gao; Yuhui Huang; Wen Xie

It is well known that the Ginzburg--Landau equations are gauge invariant. The most popular gauge choice in practical simulations is the temporal gauge, also known as the zero electric potential gauge. However, the commonly used Nédélec approximations may produce spurious giant vortices on domains with re-entrant corners. To address this issue while retaining the Nédélec approximation, we propose a finite element scheme that preserves the gauge invariance of the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations at the discrete level. Under the temporal gauge, the method employs lowest-order Nédélec edge elements for the magnetic potential and continuous piecewise-linear elements for the order parameter on triangular and tetrahedral meshes, and yields a linear, decoupled formulation that requires only the solution of linear systems at each time step. We prove that the scheme is gauge invariant, preserves a discrete maximum bound principle for the order parameter, $\|ψ_h^n\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\le 1$, and satisfies a discrete energy law under mild step-size and mesh conditions. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties. In particular, on domains with re-entrant corners, the scheme computes the correct physical solution, whereas conventional temporal-gauge discretizations with Nédélec elements produce an unphysical solution.
The Lattice of Coalition Logics between MCL and CL: Coatoms and Compact Meets

For a fixed finite set $N$ of at least two agents, we investigate the lattice $L_N$ of coalition logics between minimal coalition logic (MCL) and classical coalition logic (CL), with extensions required to be structural. This lattice is order-dual to an interval in the subvariety lattice of Boolean coalition algebras. The eight basic extensions obtained by imposing seriality, independence of agents, and determinism form a Boolean cube under inclusion, but not a sublattice of $L_N$. Our main results concern coatoms and compact meets. First, finite critical coalition algebras, realized as complex algebras of finite general concurrent games, yield three infinite families of pairwise distinct coatoms containing seriality, distinguished by failures of independence, determinism, or both. An explicit splitting characterizes the unique coatom omitting seriality. Second, the meet of two basic extensions is compact if and only if the extensions are comparable. For incomparable pairs, no axiomatization of the meet can use formulas of uniformly bounded modal depth, even with infinitely many axioms. Consequently, $L_N$ and three natural principal intervals are non-coherent algebraic lattices. These results reveal lattice-theoretic phenomena beyond the inclusion order of the eight basic extensions.
end point estimates for the bilinear circular averaging operator

We prove that the bilinear circular averaging operator is bounded from $L^1(\mathbb{R}) \times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$. The corresponding strong estimate fails, even when the inputs are nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported. We also construct nonnegative $f,g \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ for which the average does not belong to $L^{1/2}(\mathbb{R})$. The weak estimate is proved by a dyadic decomposition of the inputs and a summation over interval pairs near each quadratic fold.
Smooth Quasi--Einstein Lifts of Locally Embeddable Three-Dimensional CR Manifolds

We prove a $C^\infty$ analogue of the real-analytic quasi--Einstein lifting theorem of Hill, Lewandowski and Nurowski \cite[Theorem~2.5]{HLN2008}. Every smooth, locally CR-embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex three-dimensional CR manifold admits, for each real cosmological constant, a local smooth Lorentzian quasi--Einstein lift whose null congruence is geodesic, shearfree and twisting and whose Weyl tensor has Petrov type~$\mathrm{II}$ or $\mathrm{D}$. The result extends local lifting beyond the Sasakian setting of the global constructions in \cite{GSS2020} and the local results in \cite{GGS2026}. The proof establishes smooth local solvability of the reduced semilinear contact equation by combining an $L^\infty$ contraction with subelliptic regularity.
A Crawling Metric on the Space of Subtrees of a Tree
Thu-Le Tran; Cao Minh Quang; Nguyen Chi Tam; Kien Trung Nguyen

We propose a crawling metric on the space of subtrees of a tree. The symmetric difference cannot tell whether two disjoint subtrees are close or far; we halve it and add the gap between them. The result is a metric, one half is the smallest factor, and the tree embeds canonically. The metric equals the least cost of crawling between subtrees by growing and shrinking without jumping. With simultaneous growth and shrinkage, subtrees of fixed length form a geodesic space.
A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
Liang Ding; Jin Wang; Jinrong Wang; Zhifu Xie

While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.
Claus Koestler; Liam McQuay; Alexandru Nica

We consider a notion of $ω$-circular $*$-distribution $μ_ω$, defined in terms of a parameter $ω\in \mathbb{C}$ with $| ω|=1$. This $*$-distribution appears as limit law in an algebraic central limit theorem (CLT) for $ω$-commuting unitaries, and interpolates between the Fermionic setting (at $ω= -1$) and the Bosonic one (at $ω= 1$). On a combinatorial level, $μ_ω$ is described in terms of pair-partitions of sets $\{1, ... ,2n\}$, where one has a total order among the $n$ pairs of the partition and where every pair is assigned a direction, to the effect that one can define the sign of a crossing between two pairs. The main goal of the paper is to study a significant subspace, with "Fock space" flavour, of the $L^2$-space associated to a natural multi-variate version of $μ_ω$. The inner product on this subspace is defined by a sesquilinear form $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ on non-commutative polynomials. We explicitly describe $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ in terms of some tractable non-negative definite functions on symmetric groups, and we prove that it is non-degenerate if and only if $ω$ is not a root of unity.
A proof of the strong Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture

A family of nonempty sets is $r$-cover-free if no member is contained in the union of at most $r$ other members. Let $T(r)$ denote the least $n$ for which there is an $r$-cover-free family on $n$ points with more than $n$ members. In this paper, we prove that $T(r)\ge(r+1)^2$ for every integer $r\ge1$, confirming the strong form of the Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture. In particular, $T(r)=(r+1)^2$ whenever $r+1$ is a prime power.
Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning
Zhaiming Shen; Alexander Cloninger; Rongjie Lai; Wenjing Liao

Transformers have emerged as a dominant architecture in modern machine learning, with in-context learning (ICL) enabling models to adapt to new tasks by conditioning on prompts, without any parameter updates. To understand the attention mechanism in transformer blocks, a growing line of theoretical work interprets ICL through the lens of classical statistical estimators. Recent works have established a connection between the attention mechanism and kernel methods, while the kernel function is usually assumed to be fixed. In practice, the query and key matrices in the attention mechanism are trained, which allows the attention mechanism to serve as an adaptive kernel method. In this work, we demonstrate that transformers can act as adaptive anisotropic kernel learners. Specifically, we study ICL for low-rank linear and multi-index nonlinear regressions, and conduct numerical simulations to show that the learned attention scores closely resemble the oracle kernels for these function classes. We then develop a general framework to analyze the generalization error of ICL by connecting transformers to the oracle kernel estimator for each function class. Our theory gives an explicit and constructive implementation of the oracle kernel estimators for these function classes using a wide and shallow transformer architecture, illustrating how the prediction is carried out by the interaction between the query token and the context tokens. Our work complements existing studies by providing numerical and theoretical evidence of how the attention mechanism adapts to anisotropic kernels in both linear and nonlinear settings.
Dynamic Programming for Value-at-risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
Xian Chen; Erick Delage; Weikai Wang

Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.
Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
Takayuki Hibi; Seyed Amin Seyed Fakhari

A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.
Low-Bit Distributed Constrained Optimization with Application to Optimal Scheduling and Allocation

This paper proposes a distributed resource allocation algorithm in which each agent communicates only the sign of its local cost gradient, a single bit per directed link per iteration. The algorithm is based on Laplacian-gradient dynamics and preserves the equality (demand) constraint at every iterate, guaranteeing anytime feasibility irrespective of termination time.
