First, we provide a complete Lyapunov-based convergence analysis for the fixed-step-size regime: the iterates are shown to enter, in at most O(1/\varepsilon^2) iterations, a neighborhood of the optimizer whose radius scales as O(τ) in the decision variable and O(τ^2) in the cost residual, where $τ$ is the step-size. Crucially, the step-size bound is a time-invariant network constant (depending only on the graph Laplacian spectrum and the cost curvature bounds), so no adaptive tuning is required. Second, we characterize the invariant set under B-connected, weight-balanced digraphs, strictly weaker than the all-time connectivity and doubly-stochastic weights assumed in most prior work, and show that any odd, sign-preserving nonlinearity yields the same invariant-set and descent structure, with the single-bit protocol being the extreme communication-minimizing instance of a broader nonlinear class. Third, we address local box constraints via smooth penalty relaxation and quantify explicitly how the penalty weight interacts with the step-size bound and the optimality gap. Simulations on economic dispatch (1000 generators) and CPU scheduling (500 servers) demonstrate that the single-bit protocol achieves 5-60 times reduction in total communication cost relative to multi-bit baselines, at the price of a tunable and explicitly bounded optimality gap. A diminishing step-size schedule is shown empirically to eliminate this gap; its formal convergence analysis is identified as an open problem.
Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus

We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $β$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $β$ whose interiors are disjoint from $β$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $β$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $β$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|β| ζ(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $β$, the constants are continuous at the points where $β$ lies in a non-periodic direction.
Local Ore Conditions for Rainbow Pancyclicity and Vertex-Pancyclicity in Graph Systems

We investigate rainbow pancyclicity and vertex-pancyclicity of graph systems satisfying a local Ore-type degree condition. All graphs in the system share the same vertex set. We prove that if each graph is 2-connected and satisfies our local Ore condition, then the graph system is either rainbow pancyclic and vertex-pancyclic for cycles of length from 4 to n, or all graphs are identical balanced complete bipartite graphs on an even vertex set. A stronger degree threshold ensures full rainbow vertex-pancyclicity. All thresholds we obtain are tight. Our proofs rely on cycle extension techniques and neighborhood separation arguments.
A note on the rectangular Schoenberg-Whitney theorem for clamped B-splines

Wang et al.(Computer-Aided Design 40 (2008) 999-1008) proposed a knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices. We identify an incorrect inequality in their Appendix proof, which invalidates the argument as written, and make explicit the endpoint and multiplicity conventions on which the criterion depends. The defect lies in the proof, not in the underlying result, which is valid under suitably stated hypotheses; in the lofting construction of Wang et al. these hypotheses are implicitly satisfied, so the lofted curves are unaffected. We state the corrected result and give a new proof, independent of the disputed argument, for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities. In our proof, sufficiency follows from inclusion of spline spaces and knot insertion; necessity selects independent columns and builds the reduced knot vector from them. The proof uses no recursive column-selection construction.
Weakly uniform computable categoricity and function composition

We introduce the definition of a weakly $X$-uniformly $Y$-computably categorical structure, relativizing a definition of Kudinov (1996), and show that this relativized notion is closely related to the 2-dimensional complexity of the pairs of partial functions $(f,g)$ with the property that the composition $g\circ f$ simulates convergent $\emptyset'$-oracle computations. We develop a general theory for computing via composition and use it to prove results about the surprisingly complex weakly uniform categoricity spectrum of the structure $(ω,S)$ where $S(n)=n+1$. Namely, that $(ω,S)$ is w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for some $X\not\geq_T\emptyset'$ and $Y<_T\emptyset'$, but $(ω,S)$ is not w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for any $X<_T\emptyset'$ and $Y\not\geq_T\emptyset'$. We also construct a computably categorical structure that is not w.$\emptyset'$.u.c.c., but is w.$X$.u.c.c. for a set $X$ that is $\leq_T$-incomparable with $\emptyset'$.
Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization

This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.
Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality

We give a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than $1.77987164$. The proof provides a complete interval-arithmetic realization of Ren's five-variable construction. A finite Fourier calculation encloses every scalar coefficient through degree $403$; a fourth-derivative estimate on the entire unit circle bounds the remaining coefficient sum by $10^{-4}$. Exact rational arithmetic then certifies the final inequality. We include the transfer to all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions, the analytic quadrature errors, the rational parameters, and source code for checking and regenerating the certificate.
Asymptotic Normality of the Hill Estimator in Linear Preferential Attachment

We prove asymptotic normality of the Hill estimator based on the largest $k_n$ degrees in a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph with $n$ vertices. Each new vertex sends a fixed number $m\ge1$ of edges sequentially to older vertices, with attachment weight $d+δ$ and fixed $δ>-m$. Let $α=m/(2m+δ)$. For every deterministic sequence $k_n\to\infty$ satisfying $\sqrt{k_n}(k_n/n)^α\to0$, the estimator, centered at $α$ and multiplied by $\sqrt{k_n}$, converges to a centered normal law with an explicit variance strictly smaller than $α^2$. The reduction relative to the Hill variance for independent observations separates into contributions from the different degree laws at different birth times and from competition for new edges. The contribution from competition is $1/m$ times that from different birth times. Representations using Gamma and beta functions give a consistent standard error and a studentized normal limit. The proof uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparisons with independent pure-birth processes, while retaining the integer degrees and their ties.
A Recursive Construction of Perfect $K^n\times K^n$ Arrays over $K$ Roots of Unity

We give a uniform, explicit and elementary recursive construction of two-dimensional arrays with perfect (ideal) periodic autocorrelation over a \emph{fixed} alphabet of $K$ roots of unity and \emph{unbounded} size: for every integer $K\ge2$ and every $n\ge1$ a perfect $K^n\times K^n$ array whose entries are $K$-th roots of unity, given by a nested sum of floor terms. The construction works with \emph{twisted} (quasi-perfect) arrays indexed by a type $v\in\Z_K^2$, of which ordinary perfect arrays are the type $v=0$ members. For $K=2$ the types are Jedwab's generalised perfect binary arrays and the recursion specialises to the doubling constructions of Jedwab--Mitchell and Wild; for prime $K$ the arrays are the relative difference sets whose existence in abelian $p$-groups was settled by Ma and Schmidt; and the bare existence of perfect $K^n\times K^n$ arrays over $K$ roots of unity follows, for every $K$, from recent constructions of group-invariant Butson Hadamard matrices. The contribution of this note is therefore not existence but the calculus: types with arbitrary entries in $\Z_K^2$; three spectral lemmas (a twisted periodic extension of a type-$v$ array has a flat spectrum supported on one coset of $K\Z^2$; interleaving arrays whose spectra are flat on disjoint cosets gives a perfect array; and a shear of the index plane with a floor-function carry permutes types through the action of $SL_2(\Z_K)$ on $\Z_K^2$, whose orbits are the classes $\gcd(v_1,v_2,K)=g$); a one-directional lift that produces every type at side $KM$ from every type at side $M$ for arbitrary $K$; and the resulting closed index function, which is the recursive form of the floor-function arrays of \cite{Blake2017}.
Coactions of weak multiplier Hopf algebras

In this article, we investigate the notion of a coaction for a weak multiplier Hopf algebra. We show that there is a duality for actions and coactions of weak algebraic quantum groups. Then we obtain the well known Blattner-Montgomery duality theorem for weak algebraic quantum groups in the framework of dual pairs. We form a Morita context when the weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a two-sided faithful integral and show that the coaction is Galois if and only if the map in the Morita context is surjective. As an application, we obtain the result that a grading by any groupoid $G$ can be considered as a $\mathrm{C}G$-comodule algebra. We also construct a Morita context connecting the smash product $A\# \mathrm{C}(G)$ and the coinvariant subalgebra $A^{\mathrm{C}(G)}$. Finally we construct an isomorphism between $(R\# \mathrm{C}(G))\# \mathrm{C}G$ and $R\otimes (\mathrm{C}(G)\# \mathrm{C}G)$ when $R$ is graded by $G$.
Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
Li Cai; Haoran Liu; Mingyu Yang; Wenyan Yang

We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Plücker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Plücker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.
The Geometry of Informativeness: A Bregman-Centroid Diagnostic for Partial Pooling in Multisite Trials

Two multisite trials can have the same informativeness yet differ in how reliably individual site effects can be estimated. We show that the informativeness index averages site-specific reliabilities on the logit scale and is a Bregman centroid under Bernoulli-Kullback-Leibler divergence. This explains the geometric mean of sampling variances and yields a measure of profile dispersion. Under stated conditions, we relate profile dispersion to estimation error and show when balanced allocation maximizes informativeness at fixed total enrollment. Simulations show that estimator performance depends on the reliability profile and whether the target is individual effects, ranks, or their distribution. An online credit recovery trial illustrates the diagnostics and their conditional posterior uncertainty. We recommend reporting informativeness with arithmetic mean reliability and profile dispersion. The accompanying R package poolinfo provides tools for computing the diagnostics, posterior summaries, and design calculations.
On the annular overdetermined problems with linear and power nonlinearities in $\mathbb{R}^2$
Jun Wang; Fei Xu; Yong Zhang

In this paper, we study two classes of partially overdetermined elliptic problems on planar annular domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a fixed inner circle and a free outer boundary. The Dirichlet values are prescribed to be $1$ and $0$ on the inner and outer boundaries, respectively, while the squared normal derivative is constant on the outer boundary. For the linear law $Δu=-μu$, we establish local bifurcation under a Dirichlet nonresonance condition. For the power law $Δu=u-u^p$ with $p>1$, we take the mean outer radius as the bifurcation parameter and construct large positive radial solutions on thin annuli. The limiting profile solves $-V''=V^p$ on an interval, and the principal mixed Dirichlet--Neumann eigenvalue of its linearization determines a constant $κ_p>0$. For every fixed inner radius $λ>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $K$, we obtain a critical radius $R_K=λ+λκ_p/K+o(K^{-1})$ and a smooth local curve of positive solutions with noncircular, even, $2π/K$-periodic outer boundaries. The proof combines shape derivatives, spectral estimates, and the Crandall--Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem.

We prove that four periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribe a family of isosceles trapezoids for every angle $θ\in(0,π)$, whose similarity types are determined by the signed areas between the quotients of the curves in the infinite cylinder. In the smooth case, the problem is identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, while the continuous case follows by a convergence argument.
Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients

Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.
Spherical-Design Oracles for Zeroth-Order Optimisation: Deterministic, Variance-Free Gradient Estimation
Amir Ali Farzin; Yuen-Man Pun; Philipp Braun; Iman Shames

In this work, we develop a zeroth-order (ZO) method that estimates the gradient with minimal bias and variance. Instead of the random directions often used in the ZO literature, we consider central differences with directions given by a fixed spherical $t$-design, a finite point set that integrates every polynomial of degree at most $t$ exactly. The oracle is deterministic and thus does not induce any variance.We also propose a general finite difference method in the higher-order-smoothness regime and show the bias of both finite difference methods. We then show the convergence of the proposed ZO method via the input-to-state stability concept. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed method over the existing random ZO methods.
Pfaffian Positivity for Convex Kernels and Optimal Matching Bounds

We show that for all positive, nonincreasing, convex functions $f : (0, \infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and for any collection of $n$ points $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1 < x_2 < \ldots < x_n$ and $n$ even, the Pfaffian of the skew matrix defined by $f(x_j - x_i)$ above the diagonal is positive. More generally, we establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for Pfaffians arising from interval decompositions, which also yields quantitative lower bounds for singly and doubly bordered Pfaffians. Choosing $f(r) = r^{-2}$ proves the three nonvanishing assertions in the conjecture of Albouy and Moeckel. Further, we show that the rainbow bound (the product over the nested matching $\{1,n\}, \{2,n-1\}, \ldots \{n/2, n/2 + 1\}$) is the unique single-matching product that bounds $\mathrm{Pf}(A_f(x))$ below uniformly over $x$ and $f$ positive, nonincreasing, convex.
Tactix: Towards a Programmable Strategy Interface for Flexible SAT Solving
Haoze Wu; André Schidler; Armin Biere; Nina Narodytska

Modern SAT solvers combine a rich repertoire of proof rules with sophisticated strategies that determine when and how to apply them. Often, the internal implementations are tightly coupled to particular strategies, making it inconvenient to define new strategies without changing solver internals. We present Tactix, a proof-producing sequential CDCL solver that incorporates a wide range of techniques in state-of-the-art solvers with a clean separation of proof rules from solving strategies. This separation enables a public interface through which users can invoke particular techniques, observe their effects, and program a wide range of solving strategies. The default strategy of Tactix is programmable over this interface and outperforms state-of-the-art solvers on benchmarks from the 2024--2026 SAT Competitions. We also use the interface to develop novel strategies tailored to challenging benchmarks from two application domains, which led to performance gains over strong baselines. We intend Tactix to serve as an infrastructure for designing and evaluating novel solving strategies. Finally, we also present a self-study of the AI-assisted development process behind Tactix.
Tetrahedral points and classification of Almgren-minimizing sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$

We prove that a two-dimensional Almgren-minimizing set in three dimensions which is sufficiently close in Hausdorff distance to a tetrahedral cone contains an interior tetrahedral point. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative regularity near tetrahedral cones and we complete the classification of entire Almgren-minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.
Benign Overfitting Property of the Minimum $\ell_q$ -norm Interpolant Estimator in Regression Problem via Feature Space Decomposition
Radosław Adamczak; Guillaume Lecué; Zong Shang; Marta Strzelecka

This paper establishes high-probability, non-asymptotic upper bounds for the population excess risk of minimum $\ell_q$-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression, valid for all $1<q<\infty$ under three scenarios: convex concentration, mild moment assumptions and log-concavity. Consequently, we derive sufficient conditions for these estimators to exhibit benign overfitting. Our analysis hinges on a Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) framework, which naturally highlights the self-regularizing properties of minimum norm interpolants as well as the role of alignment between the signal and the features for benign overfitting. From a technical perspective, our approach circumvents the traditionally used Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) by instead leveraging the Dvoretzky-Milman theorem. We emphasize that the FSD method has the potential to refine standard uniform convergence approaches. Furthermore, the isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem established herein -- proven under the three scenarios mentioned above -- for the $\ell_q$-norm is of independent mathematical interest.
Pillai's equation between k-generalized Pell numbers and Tribonacci numbers
Cherif B. Deme; Kancou D. Fall; Bernadette Faye

For an integer $k\ge2$, let $(P_n^{(k)})_{n\ge0}$ be the $k$-generalized Pell sequence and $(T_m)_{m\ge1}$ the Tribonacci sequence. We determine, for every $k\ge2$, all integers $c$ having at least two representations $c=P_n^{(k)}-T_m$ with $m\ge2$. The starting point is an identity of Kılıç: $P_n^{(k)}=F_{2n+1}$ for $0\le n\le k$. In the range $n\le k$ the problem therefore becomes, for all $k$ at once, Pillai's equation between odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers and Tribonacci numbers, which has exactly six solutions. In the range $n>k$ we solve the problem for $k=2$ and $k=3$ using the exact heights of the Binet coefficients; for $k\ge4$ we prove a bound for $n$ polynomial in $k$. We also use the fact that $P_n^{(k)}$ is extremely close to $F_{2n+1}$ when $k$ is large to show that $k\le414$, and treat the remaining values one by one. For $k\ge4$ there are, besides the solutions common to all $k$, exactly four further solutions, for $k=4$, $5$ and $9$. The proofs combine Matveev's theorem with the reduction method of Dujella and Pethő.

We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index $q\ge 5$. Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.
João Marcos R. do Carmo; Marcos S. Ferreira

In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =ϕ_{a,θ}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $ϕ_{a,θ}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.
The prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_{11}$- and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups
Logan Abounader; Austin Bell; April Beun; Elvis Cabrera; Dakota Nobuyuki Goto; Thomas Michael Keller

We study prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_n$-solvable groups, focusing on the cases $\mathcal{A}_{11}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$. These provide the first classifications of $T$-solvable groups for which $|π(T)|>4$. We develop structural and representation-theoretic tools for analyzing the possible prime graph complements and use them to obtain complete characterizations for both $\mathcal{A}_{11}$-solvable and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups. The methods introduced also provide a framework for studying analogous classification problems for larger alternating groups.
Julián A. Fresán-Figueroa; Ilán A. Goldfeder; Aldo Lozano-Piña

A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices in $S$ is joined by a geodesic whose internal vertices do not belong to $S$. We define a reconfiguration graph whose vertices are the mutual-visibility sets of $G$. Two configurations are adjacent if one is obtained from the other by adding or removing one vertex or by sliding one token along an edge of $G$. The subgraphs induced by configurations of a fixed cardinality are called layers. The spanning subgraph formed by token-addition and token-removal edges is a daisy cube. We study the effects of token-sliding edges on distances and connectivity to this skeleton. For a connected host of order $n\ge3$, the vertex connectivity of the reconfiguration graph lies between $3$ and $n$, and both bounds are attained. We determine several parameters of $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{M}}(K_n)$ and describe the behavior of the model for disconnected hosts and for isometric or convex subgraphs. We also give a component-based criterion for mobile mutual visibility. For complete bipartite graphs, we use a description of feasible configurations to determine connectivity and distance bounds for fixed-cardinality layers. For trees, we show that every component of a layer of cardinality at least three is isomorphic to a Cartesian product of subtrees, obtaining exact metric formulas and characterizing the connected layers. Finally, we prove that every layer of a cycle is connected.
Computing Multi-Slot First-Price Pacing Equilibria at Scale via Entropic Smoothing
Yuchen Xie; Shenyinying Tu; Yuan Gao; Yi Zhang; Deepak Kumar

Pacing equilibria describe how budget-constrained advertisers clear an ad market, but computing one at production scale is hard when every request fills several slots: the allocation jumps whenever two campaigns' scores cross. We consider the first-price pacing equilibrium (FPPE) of auctions with $K$ homogeneous slots and unit-demand campaigns, whose Eisenberg-Gale dual reduces, via a TopK identity, to a convex program over bids. Regularizing each request's allocation with the binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy gives a smooth, strictly convex dual whose gradient is exactly spend minus budget and whose evaluation splits into independent one-dimensional threshold solves, one per request. The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard one at an explicit $O(\sqrt{T})$ rate, and a duality gap certifies how far any bids are from the hard equilibrium. We implement an efficient multi-GPU solver and test it on a production ad workload. We use it to compute an equilibrium price anchor: each campaign's hindsight equilibrium cost per key result.
Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
Xingtang Dong; Zipeng Wang; Kehe Zhu

We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_φ$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $φ$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_φ: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_φ: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_φ$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_φ$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.

Let $R = \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{14}]$, let $π= 4 + \sqrt{14}$, and let $\mathfrak{p} = (2,\sqrt{14}) = πR$ be the prime ideal above $2$. Cavallar and Lemmermeyer studied the multiplicative weighted norms $ϕ_{t}(x) = |N(x)|(t/2)^{v_π(x)}$ and asked for which weights $t$ they are Euclidean functions on $R$. We show that the set of these weights, the Euclidean window of $\mathfrak{p}$, is $(\sqrt{5},T]$, where $T$ is the algebraic number \[ T = \sqrt{\frac{8}{104051\sqrt{2} - 55617\sqrt{7}}} = 2.2468286690\ldots = \sqrt{5} + 0.0107606915\ldots. \] Thus the window is nonempty but not open. We also obtain the integer-valued completely multiplicative Euclidean function $2^{v_π(x)}|N(x)|^{6}$ on $R$.
Lifting Safety Through Reduced-Order Model Architectures: An Invariant Manifold Approach
Massimiliano de Sa; Aaron D. Ames

Reduced-order model architectures are often used to decompose complex safety-critical control design tasks into tractable subproblems. In this paradigm, one must ask: when does the safety of a reduced-order model lift to safety of the full system? Taking an invariant manifold perspective, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of smooth, regular lifts of compact safe sets from reduced-order models. Our characterization relies only on asymptotic stability of an embedding of a reduced-order safe set, without additional robustness or rate conditions. We apply these results to study control barrier functions in reduced-order model architectures and lifts of safe sets through cascades. Further, we use our conditions to obtain topological obstructions to the tracking of safe, kinematic reduced-order models for mechanical systems. We conclude by using these obstructions to inform safe hierarchical control design for an underactuated satellite on SE(3).

Let $χ$ be the quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor $N$ associated with a given real quadratic field $k$ and let $X_χ(N)$ be the double covering of $X_0(N)$ associated with $χ$. In this note, we study a modular unit $f$ on the curve $X_χ(N)$. We prove that the transform of $f$ by the Fricke involution $\mathscr{w}_N$ is the level $N$ analogue of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction introduced by Lee and Park. Furthermore, if $N$ is a positive prime discriminant, then $f$ is Ligozat's modular unit, which is known from Mazur's work on the Eisenstein ideal. We extend Ligozat's construction to any positive fundamental discriminant $N$.
PICKLES: Covariance-Preconditioned Kinetic Langevin Ensemble Sampler
Hong Ye Tan; Stanley Osher; Yifan Chen

We propose a covariance-preconditioned kinetic Langevin ensemble sampler named PICKLES. This is a kinetic analogue of the affine invariant interacting Langevin dynamics (ALDI). PICKLES uses a rectangular covariance square root as a preconditioner to avoid computing matrix inverses or square roots, leading to position and momentum variables of different dimensions. Theoretically, the continuous-time dynamics are ergodic under mild regularity and growth conditions on the potential, assuming $N>d+1$ particles and a full-rank initial ensemble. We discretize PICKLES using BAOAB or OBABO splitting, with the latter convenient for Metropolization. For Gaussian targets at stationarity, we demonstrate that Metropolized PICKLES achieves an integration step size scaling of $d^{-1/4}$ to achieve fixed acceptance probabilities, as the ensemble size and dimension increase at a fixed ratio. This matches the scaling of single particle Metropolized Hamiltonian and kinetic samplers. Numerical experiments compare sampling efficiency and estimation error with non-preconditioned, overdamped, and single-chain counterparts, demonstrating improved efficiency per gradient evaluation. On a Dark Energy Survey Year 1 3x2pt cosmology benchmark, we obtain competitive effective sample size per gradient evaluation compared to a densely preconditioned No-U-Turn Sampler.
Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform
Sho Sonoda; Luca Galimberti; Yuanchao Xu; Isao Ishikawa; Masahiro Ikeda

Neural networks whose inputs are functions, as in operator learning, are usually shown to be universal by existence arguments, either by reduction to finite-dimensional networks or by Stone--Weierstrass-type density; these prove that approximants exist but say little about how the parameters depend on the target. We take a constructive route. We extend the ridgelet transform, an integral transform related to the Fourier, Radon, and wavelet transforms, to continuous maps on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, replacing the Lebesgue measure that is unavailable in infinite dimensions by Gaussian weights with a homogeneous mixture on the direction space. The resulting transform has a Plancherel identity and reconstruction formulas incorporating the frame operator, the correction induced by the weights, and it assigns to each target an explicit coefficient measure, one for every admissible analysis filter. From these representations we obtain uniform approximation on compact sets for all continuous non-polynomial activations of polynomial growth, including ReLU, and, by Monte Carlo sampling of the coefficient, finite-width networks with a dimension-free $O(N^{-1/2})$ error in the width $N$ for globally Lipschitz activations and coefficients with finite variation and second moments. Explicit examples include Gaussian targets and neural-operator layers. A companion Lean~4 formalization provides machine-checked proofs, with its correspondence to the manuscript documented at https://shosonoda.github.io/lean-operator-ridgelet/ .
The Heesch number in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is unbounded

The Heesch number of a figure is the largest number of times that the figure can be surrounded by layers of its congruent copies. Heesch's problem asks whether finite Heesch numbers are bounded. We show that in the three-dimensional Euclidean space, and thus also in higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces, they are not: for every positive integer $h$, we construct a shape whose Heesch number is finite and at least $h$. The construction is explicit, and it starts from a four-point set of integers that does not tile the line, but packs long intervals.
Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov--Hausdorff Class

Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov-Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, which is an extended pseudometric. We prove that every nonempty extended metric space is isometrically embeddable into $\mathfrak{GH}$. More precisely, for every nonempty extended metric space $X$, the embedding can be chosen so that all image points are represented by metrics on a common underlying set of cardinality $\max\{\mathrm{dens}\,X,\aleph_0\}$, where $\mathrm{dens}\,X$ denotes the density character of $X$. To establish this result, for every nonempty set $I$, we realize the space of all real-valued functions on $I$, equipped with the uniform extended metric, as a family of metrics on a fixed underlying set. Under this realization, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance agrees with the uniform extended distance between functions, including when this distance is infinite, and each resulting metric space is complete, uniformly discrete, and unbounded, with cardinality $\max\{|I|,\aleph_0\}$. When $I$ is countable, the representing spaces can also be chosen proper and of bounded geometry. We also show that, for every infinite cardinal $κ$, there are exactly $2^κ$ clouds represented by metric spaces of cardinality at most $κ$, and that $2^κ$ of their cardinality-restricted parts are isometrically universal for all metric spaces of density character at most $κ$. Furthermore, every sphere of positive radius centered at a point of the constructed copies of $\ell^\infty(κ)$ in the zero-distance quotients admits isometric embeddings of all metric spaces of density character at most $κ$ and diameter at most twice the radius.
Build Your Own Neural Network From Scratch
Samantha Donner; Ethan Geary; Peter March; Mathew Umano

These notes are based on our reading of Michael Nielsen's online book neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com. They represent our effort to elaborate his exposition of neural networks and to provide supporting mathematical detail. Our goal is to provide self-contained instructions for building a basic neural network in the form of pseudocode, so that an interested reader can build a network from scratch and know why it works. No prior knowledge of neural networks or of Python is assumed. Some familiarity with linear algebra, calculus, and probability is helpful but we explain the relevant mathematics in a set of appendices designed to be accessible to newcomers.
Global well-posedness and orbital stability of the Gross--Pitaevskii branch in a coupled defocusing Schrödinger system
Michał Kowalczyk; Jarosław Mederski; Isidora Miranda

We consider a one-dimensional coupled defocusing Schrödinger system with a nonzero background in its first component and finite mass in its second component. We prove global well-posedness in the full energy space, together with conservation of energy, bright mass, and total untwisted momentum. For all nonnegative coupling coefficients, every subsonic Gross--Pitaevskii soliton with vanishing second component is orbitally stable against perturbations of both components, including the zero-speed black soliton. At nonzero speed the proof uses a fixed energy--momentum functional augmented by the conserved bright mass. At zero speed it uses weighted coercivity and a local real lift of the momentum. We also identify the sharp threshold for positivity of the unaugmented bright energy and explain why this threshold is not a necessary condition for orbital stability.
Dimension Thresholds for Relative-Error Representations of Finite Metrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces
Nikita Muravya; Aleksandr Bespalov; Anna Vozianova

A finite metric space with $N$ points admits an exact representation in a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension at most $N-1$. We study the minimum dimension required for relative-error approximation of squared distances. Our main result gives an upper bound for arbitrary metrics in terms of local distance ratios: for $4/5<\varepsilon<1$, dimension $O((N/k)\log N+kρ_k^4\log N/(\varepsilon-4/5)^2)$ suffices, where $ρ_k$ is the largest ratio, over all points, between the distance to the $k$th closest point (counting the point itself) and the nearest-neighbour distance. The proof combines a low-rank landmark approximation with a sparse correction controlled by its factorization norm. For metrics with distances in $[1,Φ]$, where $Φ\ge5$ is fixed, the worst-case dimension is $Θ(N)$ for $0<\varepsilon<4/5$, lies between $Ω(\sqrt N)$ and $O(\sqrt N\log N)$ for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, and is $Θ(\log N)$ for $\varepsilon>(Φ^2-1)/(Φ^2+1)$. For $Φ>5$, an intermediate range remains without matching bounds. Sign-pattern counting yields the $Ω(\sqrt N)$ lower bound for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, while Hadamard matrices give explicit linear lower bounds for $\varepsilon<4/5$ via a known approximate-rank estimate. We also construct configurations with null squared intervals whose minimum representation dimension remains $N-1$ for every $\varepsilon<1$. Finally, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<3/5$, we show that the quadratic dependence on the parameter $C$ in the dimension bound derived from Deng et al.'s pseudo-Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is necessary up to a logarithmic factor.
Sharp Gromov Hyperbolicity Constants for Cartesian Products of Finitely Many Trees
Junior Michel; Anier Soria Lorente; Jean Marie-Vilaire

Let $X=T_1\times\cdots\times T_k$, $k\ge2$, be a Cartesian product of finite nontrivial trees with unit edges, and write $d_i=\diam T_i$, $S=\sum_id_i$ and $M=\max_id_i$. We prove that the thin-triangle hyperbolicity constant of the geodesic realization of $X$ is \[ \Rips(X)=\min\Bigl\{\frac S2,\ S-M+\frac12\Bigr\}, \] and that the four-point hyperbolicity constant of its vertex metric is the value \[ \mathcal{P}(d_1,\dots,d_k) = \max_{E\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}} \min\left\{ \sum_{i\in E} d_i,\, \sum_{i\notin E} d_i \right\}. \] of the best two-way partition of the diameters. Both constants therefore depend only on the diameter vector, and their difference is governed by the partition imbalance $η$ of that vector: it equals $η/2$ when $M\le S-M$ and $1/2$ otherwise. In particular the two constants coincide if and only if the diameters admit a perfect partition, and their difference is unbounded. For $k\ge3$ the first formula exhibits a many-factor balancing phenomenon: several short factors can collectively balance the longest one and force the universal bound $\frac12\diam X$ to be attained. The proofs are self-contained and rest on an exact distance formula for the geodesic realization of $X$. For the $\ell_1$-product of the factors, i.e.\ the $\ell_1$-metric on the associated cube complex, we obtain $\Rips=\min\{S/2,S-M\}$, which identifies the half-unit above as a pure $1$-skeleton effect, and we show that the four-point formula holds for $\ell_1$-products of arbitrary $0$-hyperbolic metric spaces, in particular for weighted trees and $\R$-trees. We also treat products with unbounded factors and record algorithmic consequences.
An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps

The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory. The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
Codimension of Brill-Noether Loci on Abelian Surfaces and the First Segre Invariant

Let $X$ be an abelian surface of Picard rank 1 with ample generator $H$. We show that, for a Mukai vector $\mathbf{v}=(r,mH,χ)$ with $r,m\geq 1$ and $χ\leq 0$, the first Brill-Noether loci $\{E \;|\; H^0(E)\neq 0\}$ in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$ is nonempty of the expected codimension $1-χ$. As an application, we study the rank 1 Segre invariant on these abelian surfaces. Specifically, for $\mathbf{v}$ a Mukai vector of a $μ$-stable sheaf of $\mathrm{rank}\geq 2$, we compute the Segre invariant of the general sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$, and we determine the numbers which arise as the Segre invariant of a sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$.
Rinat Kashaev; Vladimir Mangazeev; Marcos Marino

Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.
Nonradial Finite-Time Blow-up for the Mass-Critical Inhomogeneous Biharmonic NLS
Ngoc Uyen Cong Nguyen; Van Duong Dinh

We consider the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=Δ^2u-|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{8-2b}{N}}u, \quad 0<b<\min\{4,N/2\}. \] We prove that every $H^2(\mathbb R^N)$ solution with negative energy blows up in finite time, both forward and backward. No radial symmetry or finite-variance assumption is required. In particular, this rules out the global grow-up scenario in the previously known negative-energy blow-up alternative and establishes finite-time blow-up in the genuinely nonradial setting. The proof relies on a new localized virial argument exploiting the spatial inhomogeneity to control the localization errors.
Pilot-Projected Nonlinear Self-Interference Estimation with Simultaneous Uplink Training

This paper considers nonlinear digital self-interference (SI) cancellation and uplink-channel estimation for single-antenna in-band full-duplex radios when a desired uplink pilot is present during SI training. In this setting, a rich nonlinear SI dictionary can absorb part of the structured pilot response, while its large and correlated set of basis functions can make reliable SI estimation difficult, particularly with limited training. During SI-coefficient estimation, we treat the unknown uplink channel as a nuisance parameter and eliminate it to obtain an equivalent reduced SI estimation problem on the orthogonal complement of the pilot convolution subspace. Since the projected nonlinear dictionary can remain ill conditioned, we develop two complementary full-dictionary estimators: a pilot-projected ridge estimator with Bayesian-information-criterion tuning (PP-RidgeBIC), which uses global ridge shrinkage, and a pilot-projected group-sparse Bayesian estimator (PP-GSBE), which learns branch-dependent Bayesian shrinkage from the data. These estimators offer two complementary operating points: PP-RidgeBIC favors computational efficiency, whereas PP-GSBE provides greater adaptivity to heterogeneous nonlinear SI components. Simulations show substantial gains in SI cancellation and uplink reception over non-projected and hard-selection alternatives; notably, PP-GSBE suppresses the residual SI below the noise floor with moderate training and consistently provides the strongest performance under nonlinear model mismatch.
Orientation Diversity Provably Increases the Angular-Domain Rank of 3D MIMO Arrays

Movable and rotatable-antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but the supporting theory is largely position-only. We prove that element orientation is an effective spatial resource in its own right, complementary to position. For collinear or coplanar arrays, the angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes of the scattering directions, for every common element orientation and pattern. Orientation-diverse elements with sufficiently rich analytic patterns restore the maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw. A closed-form correlation expression, strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, quantifies the gain within the scalar-pattern model, and Monte Carlo simulations corroborate the exact-rank and capacity behavior.
Variational mean curvatures for general $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ domains

The notion of variational mean curvature (VMC) arises from Massari's variational approach to hypersurfaces of prescribed mean curvature and expresses a minimizing property for Massari's functional. Here, we complement the theory of VMCs with a new sharp relation between hypersurface regularity and VMC integrability. In fact, our main result asserts that every bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ boundary, $0<α<1$, has a global VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for every $p<\frac{1+α}{1-α}$. In addition, we underpin sharpness of this conclusion by constructing examples of bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ boundary which do not admit a VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any $p>\frac{1+α}{1-α}$. Our proofs are based on Barozzi's level-set construction of global VMCs and determine integrability of these VMCs by geometric investigation of their superlevel sets and of related unions of balls.
On the kissing number of hyperbolic surfaces with a small systole

Parlier proved that there exists a constant $U>0$ such that for any hyperbolic surface $S$ of genus $g$ with systole $\ell$ the following holds: \[ Kiss(S)\leq U \frac {e^\ell}\ell g \] where $Kiss(S)$ is the maximum number of homotopically distinct systoles in $S$ (Kissing number). We show that there exists a constant $V>0$ and a sequence $S_n$ of hyperbolic homogeneous surfaces of genus $g_n\to \infty$ with a bounded systole such that \[ Kiss(S_n)\geq Vg_n \] for all $n\geq 1$. This shows that Parlier's theorem is sharp for a fixed systole length. Our proof uses Bruhat--Tits buildings of type $\tilde A_2$ and Hamiltonian surfaces.
Almost-optimal bulk regularity conditions in the CLT for G$β$E

We consider linear statistics $\sum_{k=1}^N f(x_k)$ of a Gaussian $\b$-ensemble. Following the work of \cite{LaSo22}, which was concerned only with Wigner matrices, we extend their results for general $\b$. In particular, we show that the CLT holds for any $f \in H^{1/2 + \e}$. The novel input which was not used in \cite{LaSo22} is the Helffer-Sjöstrand representation for the covariance, first appearing the random matrix context in \cite{ErYa15}, coupled with characteristic flow estimates for DBM, first appearing in \cite{Bo22}.
A Kleene-inspired sequent system for a minimal logic of evidence and truth

This paper investigates the proof theory of the logic of evidence and truth LETFm, with the aim of obtaining a sequent calculus consisting only of logical rules, suitable for a simple bottom-up decision procedure. We begin with G1f, a sequent system containing structural rules, which makes explicit the main difficulties in obtaining a fully logical and decidable calculus for LETFm. We then introduce G3f, a G3-style system obtained from by applying Kleene's trick, which absorbs contraction into the logical rules by adding the principal formula of the rule to its premises.
Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems

Residual-trained neural surrogates carry no error guarantee, a limitation for free-boundary problems such as phase change and contact. We derive guaranteed error bounds for neural approximations of parabolic obstacle problems in first-order state--flux--multiplier form. The main result bounds the flux error of the network and the energy error of its feasible projection $\max\{v,g\}$ by the constitutive residual, the initial mismatch, the complementarity defect, and the PDE residual weighted by $c_F^2/α$, without the coercivity and norm-equivalence constants of the first-order formulation. It extends the Apushkinskaya--Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers and a flux bound. A penetration-consistency result shows that neural triples with arbitrarily small bound exist. Outward-rounded cellwise Taylor-model enclosures turn the bound into a finite computation valid on any adaptive partition. The flux and gradient errors of the projected output are certified below $0.27$ and $0.33$ of the solution scale for a one-dimensional Stefan problem and, after adaptive refinement, below one half for all three trained networks on a two-dimensional expanding disk. On an expanding ellipse the gradient bound stays above one half; substitution diagnostics trace the floor of the trained networks to the projected state near the free boundary, and the remaining gap to enclosure overhead. Without a closed-form solution, a validated lower bound replaces the solution norm; there the enclosure is nearly exact, but the trained networks have errors above the solution scale and no useful accuracy is certified. The bounds control a state--flux norm, not the multiplier or the free-boundary location.
Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes

We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.
Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds

Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
Certifiably Correct Fréchet Means in Orbit Spaaces
Dustin G. Mixon; Tom Needham; Nathan Willey

We study Fréchet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series
Finiteness of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds
We show that for any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, there are only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows on $M$ up to orbit equivalence.
Optimal dimension growth rates in the high dimensional Central Limit Theorems

We investigate the optimal dimension growth rates for the high-dimensional Central Limit Theorem (CLT) over half spaces, Euclidean balls and Borel convex sets, under the existence of fourth moments. It has been observed in the literature that $d=o(n^c)$ with $0< c\leq 1/2$ is sufficient for the CLT to hold over Euclidean balls. As a consequence, the CLT over half spaces should ideally hold under similar dimension growth rates. In case of Borel convex sets, however $d= o(n^{c})$ with $0< c\leq 2/5$ is generally sufficient. The most recent results for CLT over Euclidean balls and Borel convex sets with respective rates $d= o(\sqrt{n})$ and $d= o(n^{2/5})$ is due to Fang and Koike (2024) and under the existence of fourth moments. In this paper, we investigate whether these sufficient growth rates of $d$ with respect to $n$ are also necessary. Thus, our results completely characterize the sharpness of dimension growth rates under existence of fourth moments across half-spaces, Euclidean balls, and Borel convex sets.
T-embeddings as stationary measures on T-graphs
Mikhail Basok; Benoit Laslier; Marianna Russkikh

In this paper, we investigate the relation between t-embeddings and T-graphs associated with the same weighted planar bipartite graph. We prove that, given such a T-graph, the corresponding t-embeddings are classified by positive stationary measures on this T-graph and describe a reconstruction procedure of the t-embedding given such a measure. As an application, we develop an approach for constructing t-embeddings of arbitrary sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.
Recovering Dirichlet coefficients from even samples

In this work, we determine the exact case error for recovering a Dirichlet coefficient from finitely many positive even samples with bounded additive errors. For sequences with a bounded tail and an unrestricted initial block, a polynomial estimator is minimax among all recovery maps. Its tail and noise constants admit explicit product formulas. We prove a sharp tail asymptotic on the index scale K^(3/2) and give a terminating procedure for selecting the sample count from a computable error bound.
Representing Information on DNA using Patterns Induced by Enzymatic Labeling
Daniella Bar-Lev; Eitan Yaakobi; Zohar Yakhini; Tuvi Etzion

Enzymatic DNA labeling is a powerful tool with applications in biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, medical science, and genomic research. This paper contributes to the evolving field of DNA-based data storage by presenting a formal framework for modeling DNA labeling in strings, specifically tailored for data storage purposes. Our approach involves a known DNA molecule as a template for labeling, employing patterns induced by a set of designed labels to represent information. One hypothetical implementation can use CRISPR-Cas9 and gRNA reagents for labeling. Various aspects of the general labeling channel, including fixed-length labels, are explored, and upper bounds on the maximum size of the corresponding codes are given. The study includes the development of an efficient encoder-decoder pair that is proven to be optimal in terms of maximum code size under specific conditions. The codewords for this framework are codesets, i.e., each codeword is a collection of a few labels. Of special interest are codes whose codesets contain fixed-length labels. Their construction and analysis are tied to de Bruijn sequences and constrained coding.
A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets

In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding infinite-dimensional Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for strong solutions and asymptotic replication results for mild solutions through Yosida approximations. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. Finite-dimensional noise truncations and Yosida approximations are employed to establish approximate and asymptotic approximate completeness results. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.
Margin Certificates for Voting Classifiers under Mixing Dependence
Adria Binte Habib; Ibne Farabi Shihab

Margin bounds explain why weighted votes generalize after training error vanishes, but dependent observations require concentration arguments that keep the dependence model and failure budget explicit. We study stationary mixing streams without treating dependence as a formal substitution of an "effective sample size." For a finite base class, we combine independent-block Rademacher theory for stationary $β$-mixing processes with a clipped margin loss to obtain an explicit uniform voting-margin certificate, whose dependence penalty is set by the number of approximately independent blocks and the coupling budget $4(μ-1)β(a)$. A black-box transfer theorem shows that any i.i.d. voting-margin guarantee remains valid on a regularly spaced subsequence, with only an additive $β$-mixing failure probability. For votes fixed independently of a stationary finite-state reversible Markov stream, spectral concentration gives the cleaner $\sqrt{t_{rel}/n}$ rate, and a sticky-refresh construction shows this exponent is unavoidable. The constant is statistic-specific: the effective sample size is $n/τ_{int}(g)$, with $τ_{int}(g) \le 2t_{rel}-1$. When the dependence scale is unknown, a batch-means Student-t interval is valid up to an explicit remainder vanishing in the number of batches, with width governed by $τ_{int}(g)$ rather than the worst-case $t_{rel}$. Experiments show: the learned-vote certificate is nonvacuous once the block count is large; a two-timescale construction gives a batch-means interval 8.1x narrower than the worst-case interval at nominal coverage (0.945); block-bootstrap and batch-means intervals undercover under strong dependence while the certificate stays valid; and on real, ordered UCI HAR sensor data the dependence-agnostic certificate reaches 0.95 coverage where naive intervals reach only 0.38.
On condensations of $C_p(X)$ spaces onto Banach spaces with the weak topology

We show that for a broad class of spaces $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the pointwise topology maps bijectively onto any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with the weak topology. We prove that the inverse $φ^{-1}$ of any continuous bijection $φ: C_p(X)\to (E,w)$, where $X$ is an arbitrary infinite Tychonoff space and $(E,w)$ is an arbitrary normed space with the weak topology, is everywhere discontinuous. This generalizes a recent result of Kania--Kąkol and solves a problem raised by Kąkol, Leiderman and Michalak by providing a complete classification of function spaces $C_p(X)$ that are homeomorphic to Banach spaces with the weak topology.
Explicit Criteria for Finite-Time Identification in Sparse Primal--Dual Dynamics

We study when selected coordinates become and remain zero in a finite-dimensional sparse-regression primal--dual flow and its exact full resolvent iteration. Invariant balls centered at \((0,z)\), with \(z\) strictly dual feasible, give computable deadlines without rank assumptions or optimizer knowledge. The certificates may be available at initialization. We determine the smallest invariant radius for the continuous flow within this family. For a prescribed positive feasibility margin, center selection is convex and admits an exact finite conic formulation. We bound the coordinate margins for all centers in this family and give a normalized correlated example attaining the bound. A composite Bregman Lyapunov estimate proves rank-free convergence without primal uniqueness and finite identification under strict dual margins. Under restricted injectivity, the discrete gap-based deadlines multiplied by the step size tend to the continuous bound for fixed data, observed state, and certificate parameters. Numerical experiments assess certificate timing. A noisy weak-form oscillator regression illustrates the difference between fitted and physical support.
A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fréchet Means on Real Grassmannians
Bipayan Banerjee; Imon Banerjee; Swagatam Das

Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fréchet mean is their standard sample mean [11,9,15,23]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fréchet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [18]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $δ$ of the mean has volume $O(δ)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fréchet Hessian vanishes.
Reusable QUBO-Derived Block-Schur Inverse Factors for Fixed-Operator Finite-Difference PDE Solvers
Arash Fath Lipaei; Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu; Özlem Salehi; Selin Aslan

Many simulations of partial differential equations require the repeated solution of linear systems whose matrix remains fixed while the righthand side changes. We present a hybrid offline online framework for this setting. The discretized operator is organized into small coupled blocks and reduced through block Schur complements. Instead of expressing the complete PDE solution as one large binary optimization problem, quadratic unconstrained binary optimization is used only to construct reusable local inverse factors. These factors are computed during an offline stage, decoded and stored, and then reused in an ordinary classical block solve for subsequent righthand sides. The optimizer facing problem size is governed by the local block size and chosen numerical precision, rather than by the dimension of the full spatial grid. We develop the mathematical formulation, analyze the accuracy and resource requirements of the binary representation, and examine the method on representative finite difference PDE problems, including execution of the local optimization stage on quantum optimization hardware. The resulting architecture provides a reusable interface between conventional numerical linear algebra and QUBO based quantum optimization.
$L^p$-regularity for fourth-order Schrödinger operators with unbounded or degenerate coefficients
Federica Gregorio; Chiara Spina; Cristian Tacelli

We prove that operators of the form $A=-Δ^{2}-V(x)$, with $|D V(x)|\leq γV(x)^\frac{5}{4}+ C_γ$ for some $γ$ small enough and $C_γ$ positive constant, generate analytic semigroups in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for $1\leq p<\infty$ and in $C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Moreover, we characterize the maximal domain of such operators.
Translation-Invariant Pure States with Exotic Half-Chain Factors

We construct translation-invariant pure quasifree fermionic states on the one-dimensional lattice whose half-chain von Neumann algebras are hyperfinite factors of type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ or $\mathrm{III}_λ$ for any $0<λ\leq 1$. Via the Jordan-Wigner-Araki transformation, these yield translation-invariant pure spin-chain states with the same half-chain factors, demonstrating that such factors need not be of type I or III. Each state is the unique ground state of a gapless, translation-invariant parent Hamiltonian with superpolynomially decaying interactions. For any fixed factor type, the interval entanglement entropy can exhibit widely varying growth rates, from arbitrarily slow divergence to nearly power-law growth, showing that entropy scaling does not determine the factor type. In contrast, we prove that gauge-invariant quadratic Hamiltonians with finitely many flavours and exponentially decaying hopping exhibit a dichotomy: their ground states either satisfy an area law with a type I half-chain factor, or have logarithmic entropy growth with a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. The counterexample was discovered with AI assistance.
Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory

We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories. Temporal age and state-space displacement enter a nonlinear hereditary force admitting an exact, trajectory-dependent velocity representation. A common velocity-history phase space contains both resting and uniformly translating solutions. We establish global velocity arrest under a uniform geometric memory-gain bound and obtain exact translating-speed balance laws from the full radial imprint. The response slope yields a positive longitudinal exponent on rising-speed branches, while a complementary contraction criterion gives local exponential attraction to selected descending branches in the scalar velocity dynamics, in fading-memory topology. Our principal result is a constructive geometric non-identifiability theorem: two systems with identical nonlinear force operators on an open neighborhood of rest can exhibit sharply different complete-motion behavior at the same subcritical gain. In the first, every admissible trajectory with bounded velocity prehistory comes to rest exponentially; in the second, locally attracting rest coexists with a locally attracting translating branch and an additional spectrally unstable translating branch. The infinite-memory case exhibits exponentially flat force differences, with all finite-order equilibrium derivatives agreeing despite the possibility of distinct global translating families. The framework also yields classical Volterra kernels and distributed-derivative transfer functions by linearization.
Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
Nate Harman; Rylan Rosas; Charles Troutman III; Chris Wu

We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.
Energy of signed graphs and the vertex cover number
Aniruddha Samanta; Deepshikha; Kinkar Chandra Das

The energy $\mathcal{E}(Γ)$ of a signed graph $Γ=(G,σ)$ is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix $A(Γ)$. In this article, we prove that $\mathcal{E}(Γ)\geq 2τ(G)$, where $τ(G)$ is the vertex cover number of $G$. The case of unsigned graphs, a 1980s conjecture proved only recently, is a special case of this result. Moreover, we completely characterize the equality case: equality holds if and only if every connected component of $Γ$ is switching equivalent to an \emph{additive rook graph} $\Rook_N(a,b)$. This graph is constructed on an $N\times N$ board with $a_i+b_j$ vertices on square $(i,j)$. Two vertices are joined by a positive edge if they share only a row, and by a negative edge if they share only a column. As consequences, we obtain a balanced/antibalanced trichotomy for the extremal signed graphs and deduce the characterization of the extremal unsigned graphs. Finally, an example shows that the bound does not extend to the Hermitian adjacency matrices of mixed graphs or to complex unit gain graphs.
Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System

We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.
The Kemeny-Braess Paradox in Random Graphs
Manuel Bodirsky; Lorenzo Ciardo; Mihyun Kang

In 2016, Kirkland and Zeng initiated the mathematical treatment of Braess paradox for random walks on graphs using Kemeny's constant as the measure of travel time. We study this phenomenon for the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$. An edge in a connected graph is called Kemeny-Braess if its deletion preserves connectedness and decreases Kemeny's constant, while a nonedge is Kemeny-Braess if its insertion increases Kemeny's constant. Let $\bar d=(n-1)p$ be the expected degree of $G\sim G(n,p)$, and assume that $\bar d-\log n\to\infty$, so that $G$ is connected with high probability. We determine the sharp asymptotic thresholds for the existence of both types of paradoxical behaviour. With $C^*=1/(1-\log 2)$, the threshold for Kemeny-Braess edges is $\bar d=C^*\log n$, whereas the threshold for Kemeny-Braess nonedges is $\bar d=2C^*\log n$. Hence, as the expected degree $\bar d$ increases, the connected regime exhibits three phases: first Kemeny-Braess paradox occurs for both edges and nonedges, then only for nonedges, and finally it disappears. In particular, in the dense regime, with high probability $G$ has no Kemeny-Braess edges or nonedges. This contrasts sharply with the spectral gap of the normalised Laplacian, for which Braess' paradox persists at constant edge density. Our proof combines a spectral-moment expansion of Kemeny's constant with uniform edge-perturbation estimates. Near the thresholds, the sign of the perturbation is governed by the endpoint degrees, and binomial large deviations yield the constant $C^*$ and the factor of two between the two thresholds.
Axisymmetric Navier--Stokes with Swirl: Regularity and Blow-Up Constraints

For smooth finite-energy axisymmetric Navier--Stokes solutions with swirl, we give a continuation criterion in terms of the signed cumulative work of the actual post-cut source-generated meridional current, with quartic viscous dissipation counted once. In the stated strong Sobolev class the criterion is necessary and sufficient and requires neither a global circulation bound nor spatial moments. We also prove cumulative inward-compression criteria, collect quantitative necessary conditions at a first singular time, and give a complete-history mixed-residual test for noncontinuation. Auxiliary results quantify quartic dissipation, energy-funded source bounds, and causal source--receiver identities. An explicit smooth whole-space datum has positive newborn source production.
Arithmetic Constraints on Charges of Symmetric Monopoles

For Euclidean BPS monopoles with gauge group $SU(N)$, maximal symmetry breaking, and sufficiently generic spectral data, we produce necessary congruence relations that their magnetic charges must satisfy when $N \geq 3$. As such, a monopole as above with given charges can have certain subgroups of $SO(3)$ ruled out as possible groups of symmetries. In particular, the axially symmetric case may only admit non-trivial magnetic charges in the non-generic setting.
Invariants of big classes from asymptotic total Betti numbers

We introduce and study a new numerical invariant of big line bundles on normal complex projective varieties, defined in terms of the total Betti number of hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of the line bundle. We prove that this invariant is birational and provides an upper bound for the volume of the line bundle. When the big line bundle admits a rational Zariski decomposition, we show that the invariant coincides with the volume. In particular, this holds when the line bundle is ample or is defined on a projective surface. We also investigate the analogous problem in the real algebraic setting, proving the existence of real algebraic hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of a big line bundle whose real vanishing loci have arbitrarily large total Betti numbers.
Hamel-based TVG Stronger than the Usual Topology on R

For every nonzero rational-valued additive functional on the real line, we construct a Hausdorff nondiscrete topological vector group topology strictly finer than the usual topology. We prove that two such topologies coincide exactly when their coefficient functionals differ by a nonzero real rescaling; every other pair is incomparable. The family contains as many distinct topologies as there are subsets of the real line. Their supremum is still nondiscrete and strictly finer than every individual member. We also prove failure of first countability and existence of maximal nondiscrete extensions.
Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves

Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and González-Sánchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\leσ(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $σ(A)$; the reverse inequality $σ(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$.
