The reflection is defined by a one-sided reflection problem on $(-\infty,1]$ in which the regulator is convolved with a memory kernel. Given a càdlàg input $ρ$ and a kernel $K$ with $K(0)=1$, we seek a pair $(\hatρ,η)$ such that $\hatρ=ρ-\int_0^\cdot K(\cdot-u)\,dη(u)$ takes values in $(-\infty,1]$, $η$ is nondecreasing, and $η$ increases only when $\hatρ=1$. We refer to this problem as the Volterra-Skorokhod problem. We show existence and uniqueness of the solution and that the solution map is Lipschitz continuous in the uniform norm and nonanticipating. It therefore applies to stochastic inputs path by path. Unlike the classical Skorokhod map, this map is not monotone. For nonincreasing kernels, however, the regulator is the smallest admissible one and monotone in the input. In the queue, this orders the cumulative fluid losses under ordered arrival rates. Furthermore, since arrivals enter the queue through the reflection kernel, the regulator is a thinning of the arrivals.
On strongly coherent confidence envelopes for the false discoveries
Romain Périer; Gilles Blanchard; Guillermo Durand

Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.
Computing Fréchet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds

Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fréchet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fréchet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $Ξ_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Schützenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.
Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2

This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.
Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
Alexander Chervov; Ilia Gaiur; Sergey Galkin; Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk; Volodya Rubtsov; Shamil Shakirov

We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.
Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains

In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.
Deterministic Bounds on Accuracy and Stability of Metric-Space Regression and Classification
Nina Maria Gottschling; Jakob Gawlikowski; Michele Caprio

Data-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data. While best-fit machine learning methods can accommodate such noise through uncertainty estimates, they are prone to overfitting and it is challenging to quantify ambiguity of the relation between inputs and targets. We introduce a geometric framework that quantifies this ambiguity through the average kernel size, computed with data-dependent, i.e. model-independent, feasible sets derived from worst-case input and target noise. The framework provides computable, deterministic, non-asymptotic bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy for a finite, constructed dataset, independent of the predictive model class, and applies to regression and classification with pseudo-metric input spaces and metric target spaces. The ambiguity of the input-target relation implies three consequences: an empirical error floor, an accuracy-stability trade-off, and, under standard probabilistic assumptions, a strictly positive distribution-training error gap when training below the accuracy bounds. Under standard Borel assumptions for Euclidean norms, the distributional analogue of the average kernel size is related to Bayes risk as it reduces to the optimal distribution root-mean-squared error times the square root of two. Experiments spanning tabular regression, image regression and classification datasets yield nontrivial bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy on a constructed dataset, alongside descriptive comparisons with model performance on the original datasets. The bounds provide a computable, model-independent reference scale on the constructed dataset and comparisons with model performance on the original dataset are descriptive.
Geometric rigidity principles for $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures

We study generalized Young measures generated by $\mathscr{A}$-free measures, $\mathscr{A}$ a constant-rank operator, in a compactification of the value space adapted to an energy. Given an $\mathscr{A}$-quasiconvex integrand $G$ of linear growth with coercive recession function $G^\infty$, the unit sphere at infinity is replaced by the indicatrix $\mathbb{S}_G=\{G^\infty=1\}$, which need be neither convex nor symmetric. The two compactifications are equivalent, but in the adapted one the equality cases of the Jensen inequalities characterizing $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures become statements of convex geometry about $\mathbb{S}_G$. We prove the characterization in this setting, with a new streamlined proof of the inhomogenization step based on a dyadic martingale argument. We then show that if $\mathscr{A}$-free measures $μ_j\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}μ$ and their $G$-energies converge, then at $|μ^s|$-almost every point the concentration-angle measure is supported on the smallest exposed face of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$ containing the $G$-polar of $μ^s$; in particular, it never charges the set where $G^\infty$ differs from its convex envelope, which, by the automatic convexity of Kirchheim and Kristensen, does not meet the wave cone. The concentration on the singular part of $μ$ is elementary for every such sequence if and only if each point of the wave cone on $\mathbb{S}_G$ is an extreme point of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$, as for the Euclidean norm underlying Reshetnyak's continuity theorem; on flat faces of $\mathbb{S}_G$, rigidity degrades from a point to a face. Finally, we prove a transfer principle for the convergence of energies of $\mathrm{BV}$ maps under Dirichlet boundary conditions.
Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of all planar graphs

A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no such colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a planar graph on $25$ vertices that needs four colours. Further, we give critical planar graphs on $25$ vertices with $52$ and with $51$ edges, an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.
The transition between order to disorder in the Seppäläinen-Johansson model

We study the Seppäläinen-Johansson model of first-passage percolation along a region of the plane where it moves from an ordered to a disordered phase, represented by a 2nd order discontinuity in its limit shape function. The fluctuations in this transition region are of order one, and we determine that certain limiting statistics are described by Fredholm determinants and are closely related to the largest eigenvalue of the GUE.
Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
Petros Galanopoulos; Alejandro Mahillo; Jesus Oliva-Maza; Aristomenis G. Siskakis
We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_μ$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $μ$ on $(0,1]$.
Local Projected Controllability of Nonlocal Continuity Equations
Elena Goncharova; Nikolay Pogodaev; Maxim Staritsyn

We formulate and study the problem of local projected controllability (LPC) for characteristic solutions of controlled nonlocal continuity (transport) equations on the space of probability measures over a separable Banach space. The task is motivated in particular by self-interacting models in machine learning, whose action can be represented as controlled dynamics of the probability distribution over input data, while the actual output is given by a finite-dimensional vector of features extracted from the terminal distribution by a possibly nonlinear observation map. Given a fixed finite family of velocity fields which may depend on the transported measure, we ask whether the reachable values of the observable vector fill a neighborhood of its reference value. Our approach is to lift the transport equation in the space of measures to an ordinary differential equation on a Banach space of maps. This representation makes it possible to employ the machinery of Lie brackets developed for Banach manifolds, while the resulting sufficient condition for LPC can be formulated directly on the space of measures.
A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
Shankar Balasubramanian; Margarita Davydova; Ting-Chun Lin; Ryan Thorngren

We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.
An improved randomized algorithm for finding sinks of Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations of the binary hypercube

Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations (AUSOs) of the binary hypercube form an elegant abstraction of various optimization problems, ranging from linear programs whose feasibility region is a combinatorial hypercube, to 2-player turn-based stochastic games (2TBSGs) in which one of the players has two actions from each one of its states. The currently fastest known randomized algorithm for finding the sink of such AUSOs is the Random-Facet algorithm of Kalai (STOC 1992), and of Matoušek, Sharir and Welzl (SoCG 1992), adapted to the binary hypercube by Gärtner (RSA 2002). The expected number of vertex queries made by the algorithm is at most $e^{2\sqrt{n}}$, where $n$ is the dimension of the cube. We design an improved randomized sink-finding algorithm that performs an expected number of only $e^{\sqrt{(2+o(1))n}}$ queries. This is the first improved bound for the problem in over two decades. The improved algorithm is obtained by adapting improved versions of the Random-Facet algorithm for solving general linear programs, and LP-type problems, developed by Kalai (STOC 1992), Gärtner (FOCS 1992), and by Hansen and Zwick (STOC 2015). The improved bound is not implied by these much more general algorithms. A key feature of the improved algorithm and its analysis is its simplicity. The structure of binary AUSOs enables a simpler description and a much simpler analysis of the adapted algorithm. In particular, the recurrence relations bounding the complexity of the algorithm depend on only one variable, and not two, and they can be solved using fairly straightforward techniques.
Avas Banerjee; Michał Kijaczko; Vivek Sahu

We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.
Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic
Elena I. Bunina; Winston Lee; Alexei Miasnikov; Kyrylo Muliarchyk

For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finitely presented group $G_p$ and elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ such that $ab=1$, $ac=0$, and $c\ne0$. Thus $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$, and the group algebra over every field of characteristic $p$, fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of $c$, so the proof does not require torsion-freeness.
Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials

On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.
A new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds

We give a new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds, following the work of Balogh-Krisátly. Our proof extends also to equality cases of the strong Brunn-Minkowski inequality, introduced by Magnabosco-Portinale-Rossi.
No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition

Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nuñez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.
Asymptotic dimension of graphs excluding an induced or fat minor
Robert Hickingbotham; Freddie Illingworth; Piotr Micek; Bartosz Walczak

Asymptotic dimension is a large-scale invariant of metric spaces that was introduced by Gromov (1993). A major open problem in coarse graph theory asks whether, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs excluding $H$ as a fat minor has bounded asymptotic dimension. A weaker conjecture asserts the same conclusion for graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor. We substantially expand the range of graphs $H$ for which these conjectures are known to hold. Specifically, we prove bounded asymptotic dimension for the following classes of graphs: graphs excluding a fixed planar graph as a fat minor; and graphs excluding a fixed string graph as an induced minor. All of our results also hold for the stronger notion of Assouad--Nagata dimension, a refinement of asymptotic dimension. These results have a number of applications, two of which we mention here. First they imply that an induced minor-closed class is $χ$-bounded if and only if it does not contain some Burling graph. Second they imply that, in graph classes excluding a fixed planar graph as an induced minor, treewidth is polynomial in maximum degree.
Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
Wern Juin Gabriel Ong; Gabriel Ribeiro

We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $κ$ for which they are $κ$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
Generating functions of hypermaps and m-constellations with two alternating boundaries

We study the enumeration of planar hypermaps with several alternating boundaries. We first derive a peeling recursion with an arbitrary number of alternating boundaries and, in the two- boundary case, translate it into a functional equation for the corresponding generating function. Our main result is an explicit solution of this equation for m-constellations. In particular, we obtain a rational expression for the genus-zero two-point function, or cylinder generating function, with two alternating boundaries.
Admissible solutions of the Euler equations
Alexey Cheskidov; Zirong Zeng; Deng Zhang

In this paper, we prove the existence of an extensive class of initial data--characterized by intermittency dimension and roughness--for which the d-dimensional Euler equations (d \ge 2) admit a decreasing energy channel with infinitely many admissible solutions arising from the same initial data. This class includes initial data in C^{1-κ}(\mathbb{T}^d) and W^{1,p}(\mathbb{T}^d) for any 0 < κ< 1 and 2 < p < \infty, thereby demonstrating the sharpness of the Lions and Yudovich uniqueness principles. Our proof is based on a new backward convex integration scheme employing approximate Λ-Euler equations to reduce the initial error and on uncovering a quantitative relationship between regularity, energy, and intermittency.
Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
Kaumudibikash Goswami; Archana Barvar; Manabendra Nath Bera

Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.
Well-posedness of 2D stochastic parabolic-parabolic Keller-Segel system with logistic source
Erika Hausenblas; Boris Jidjou Moghomye; Paul Andre Razafimandimby

We consider a stochastic, fully parabolic Keller-Segel system with multiplicative noise in non-divergence form and a logistic source in a two-dimensional bounded domain, subject to random initial data. We construct a global-in-time, non-negative martingale solution by means of a suitable regularisation procedure, combined with Banach fixed-point arguments, a localisation procedure, and a stochastic compactness method. We further establish pathwise uniqueness and uniqueness in law for martingale solutions, and prove the existence of a unique global-in-time, non-negative weak solution without imposing any smallness condition on the initial data.
Threshold and Below-Threshold Dynamics for the Energy-Critical NLS: The Higher-Kinetic-Energy Regime
Zuyu Ma; Changxing Miao; Kai Yang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Jiqiang Zheng

We study the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation below and at the ground-state energy, focusing on solutions in the upper energy cone, characterized by \[ E(u)\le E(W),\qquad \|\nabla u\|_{L_x^2}>\|\nabla W\|_{L_x^2}, \] where \(W\) is the ground state. Unlike the lower cone, where compactness of critical solutions plays a central role in understanding the dynamics, such compactness is generally unavailable on the upper branch. Consequently, previous results have often required additional assumptions, such as finite mass or finite variance. In this paper, we remove the finite-mass assumption in the radial setting and give a complete characterization of the upper-cone dynamics in the natural energy space \(\dot H^1_{\mathrm{rad}}\), resolving an open problem posed by Duyckaerts and Merle\cite{DM08}. In particular, this establishes finite-time blow-up of the special threshold solution \(W^+\) in the negative time direction in dimensions \(d=3,4\). For non-radial data in dimensions \(d\ge5\), we show that {for solutions in the interior of the upper cone, the limit superior of their $\dot H^1$-norm satisfies an explicit lower bound as time approaches each endpoint of the maximal lifespan,} while forward-global solutions on the upper threshold sheet that remain below this level must coincide with \(W^+\) modulo symmetries. We also obtain a complete classification of upper-threshold dynamics for finite-variance data in all dimensions \(d\ge3\).
BOLT: Multi-Bottleneck Bound-Guided Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource-Coupled Transport
Ziheng Zhang; Wei Zhang; Yunyi Zhao; Zuming Liu; Wei Zhou; Boon Ping Gan

Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Across five zero-shot 50- and 80-module production batches, BOLT outperforms the best dispatching-rule pair on four and the penalty policy on the three with long moves. In the three-vehicle 80-module batch, its mean makespan is 13.0% below the best pair and 4.2% below an hour-budget constraint-programming solver whose proven gap averages 34%. BOLT decides in 2.3-5.9 ms per event on one processor core and re-plans a disruption in seconds.
GPU-Accelerated Robust MA--RIS Pre-Optimization for Communication and Target Illumination
Tran Le Dung; Ho Viet Duc Luong

Movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer strong spatial control for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), but repeatedly adapting MA positions and RIS phases to each channel realization can be impractical. This letter develops a GPU-accelerated robust pre-optimization framework that jointly selects slow-timescale MA geometry and RIS phases and returns a reusable Pareto set balancing expected worst-user rate and transmit-side worst-target illumination. The illumination objective measures directional transmitted power rather than complete echo-detection or parameter-estimation performance. The proposed Regime-Aware Multiobjective Pre-optimization (RAMP) preserves regime-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross-regime mating using Pareto-survival feedback, and constructs a worst-regime robust archive. Numerical results demonstrate competitive robust Pareto quality against the considered evolutionary baselines while avoiding online physical re-optimization.
A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes

We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.
Strict monotonicity of weighted inhomogeneous percolation thresholds under covering maps
Jing Liu; Kainan Xiang; Lang Zou

We study Bernoulli bond percolation under weak covering maps for a class of weighted inhomogeneous product measures such that each edge $e$ carries a positive weight $w(e)$ and is open at intensity $λ\geq 0$ with probability $1-\exp(-λw(e))$. We prove a strict monotonicity of the weighted critical intensities $λ_c$ in the covering compatibility setting under bounded degree, uniform ellipticity, tame fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. While for the weighted uniform connection thresholds $λ_{\mathrm{conn}}$, we establish their strict monotonicity for non-injective weak covering maps under bounded degree, covering compatibility, uniform ellipticity, bounded-fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. Moreover, we verify a general-profile theorem on strict monotonicities of the two thresholds $λ_c$ and $λ_{\mathrm{conn}}$ respectively under explicit compact-interval finite-energy, derivative bounds and aforementioned geometric conditions.
Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients

The $W^{1,p}$ estimate for uniformly elliptic operators of divergence form with VMO coefficients is classical. In particular, this provides $W^{1,p}$ estimates for elliptic operators with coefficients in $W^{1,n}$. However, this theory does not yield constants in the estimates controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the rate of decay for the mean oscillation. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems whose coefficients lie in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, have an $L^\infty$-bounded spatially symmetric part, and satisfy an integral ellipticity condition. The constant in the estimate is controlled by the corresponding norms of coefficients and the ellipticity constant.
Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D

We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.
The rank problem for metric spaces

We construct a complete, second countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank. This answers a well-known question posed by Fokina, Friedman, K{ö}rwien and Nies, and shows that the known upper bound $ω_1$ on the rank, proved by Doucha, is sharp. Further, a Baire category based variant of the rank of metric spaces is developed, and this is used to give new proofs of the known rank bounds based only on standard methods of descriptive set theory.
On exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients

Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\leq1}$ be multiplicative, and suppose that $α$ has a rational approximation $a/q$ with $|α-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$ and $q\leq x/((\log x)^2(\log\log x)^3)$. We prove that $\left|\sum_{n\leq x}f(n)e(nα)\right|\leq \left(\frac4{\sqrt6}+o(1)\right)\frac{x}{\sqrt q} +O\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$, whereas complete multiplicativity improves $4/\sqrt6$ to $1$. Both constants are optimal. In particular, this confirms a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients motivated by the work of Montgomery and Vaughan (1977). We also obtain logarithmically weighted estimates and give counterexamples to related conjectures.
Polynomial Maximal Surfaces in H^{2,2} and Spherical Polygons

We study the moduli space of complete maximal surfaces in pseudo-hyperbolic space $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ with polygonal asymptotic boundary a lightlike $(n+4)$-gon in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, up to the action of $\mathsf{SO}_0(2,3)$. Importantly, this space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ is disconnected for $n\geq 2$. We introduce a \emph{turning invariant} $Θ$ that classifies the components in terms of the geometry of the boundary polygons in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, which is related to \emph{spherical polygons} in $\mathbb{S}^2$. We provide a geometric parametrization of the moduli space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ via holomorphic data, namely a pair of polynomials $α$, $β$. These polynomials appear in relation to certain components of the complexified second fundamental form of the corresponding surface. We then relate the holomorphic data $α,β$ with the turning invariant $Θ$. This leads to characterizations of the \emph{Hitchin component} of polygonal maximal surfaces studied by Tamburelli-Wolf.
Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
Duong Dinh; Troy Figiel; Joerg Teschner

On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

We analyze the behavior of systems of algebraic differential equations when considered as systems of difference-differential equations, with special emphasis on systems which define minimal sets relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCF}$ of differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ distinguished commuting derivations. We show that if $p$ is a minimal type relative to $\operatorname{DCF}$ defined by a system of algebraic partial differential equations and inequations and the forking geometry on $p$ is trivial (also called ``disintegrated''), then $p$ remains minimal when regarded as a partial type relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCFA}$ of difference-differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ commuting derivations in the sense that every completion has $\operatorname{SU}$-rank one. We illustrate this theorem by describing in detail the possible difference-differential equations consistent with differential equations of the form $y' = y^3 + a_2 y^2 + a_1 y + a_0$ where $a_0$, $a_1$, and $a_2$ are differential constants.
Classical Capacity of Single-Mode Bosonic Gaussian Channels
Gerardo Adesso; Ludovico Lami; Vittorio Giovannetti

The classical capacity of a noisy optical channel is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted reliably, given a constraint on the mean input energy. For the ubiquitous bosonic Gaussian channels, which include standard models of loss and noise in fibre and free-space optical links, determining this rate requires addressing whether entanglement between channel uses or non-Gaussian signals can outperform Gaussian encodings. More precisely, the question is whether the energy-constrained Holevo information is additive across arbitrarily many channel uses and coincides with its Gaussian counterpart. We answer these fundamental questions in the affirmative for every single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel at every input energy. Namely, we prove that independently prepared Gaussian states with Gaussian-distributed random displacements achieve the capacity, including in the low-energy regime where squeezing the signals competes with encoding information in their displacement. Our proof connects an entanglement inequality to a sharp, additive lower bound on output entropy. We then characterise communication above capacity: under a strict total photon-number cutoff, the probability of correct decoding decreases exponentially with the number of channel uses, and we derive explicit bounds on the decay exponent. When only the mean photon number is constrained, a simple energy-rescaling formula determines exactly the entire asymptotic rate--error trade-off: the capacity at mean photon number $N$ and allowed average decoding error $ε$ equals the vanishing-error capacity at mean photon number $N/(1-ε)$. Together, these results identify the ultimate limits of classical communication for some of the most fundamental models of optical communication.

We classify $h$-cobordisms between compact simply-connected $4$-manifolds with boundary in both the smooth and topological categories. This extends a result of Kreck, which proved the corresponding result for closed manifolds. As an application, we recover the injectivity portion of Orson-Powell's computation of the mapping class group for simply-connected topological $4$-manifolds with boundary.
When Fresh Information Is Not Enough: Age-of-Actuation-Optimal Scheduling for Energy-Harvesting Actuators
Ali Nikkhah; Anthony Ephremides; Nikolaos Pappas

We study transmission scheduling in an energy-harvesting actuation system where an actuation requires both a received update and available energy. While age of information (AoI) measures information freshness, age of actuation (AoA) measures the time elapsed since the latest completed actuation. The transmitter observes the receiver's AoA and battery state and decides whether to transmit a fresh update in each slot. We formulate average-AoA minimization as a Markov decision process and establish an AoA-threshold property for an optimal policy. We also derive the average AoA in closed form under the AoI-optimal policy, which is always-transmit. Numerical results show that AoA-aware scheduling can improve actuation freshness while reducing the number of transmissions, although information freshness may deteriorate. The two policies coincide for some pairs of channel success and energy-arrival probabilities. For a one-unit battery, the transmission rate under the AoA-optimal policy can vary nonmonotonically with the energy-arrival probability.
Chih-Hung Liu; Aaron Sidford; Ta-Wei Tu

In this paper we consider the problem of computing a positive diagonal scaling of a $d \times d$ symmetric $M$-matrix so that all row and column sums are $1$. We provide a poly-logarithmic iteration algorithm that solves this problem to high accuracy, where the cost of each iteration is dominated by the cost of solving a Laplacian system. This improves upon the recent $\tilde{O}(d^{1/3})$ iteration bound of [Vladu STOC 2025] and yields a randomized algorithm for the problem that runs in near-linear time and poly-logarithmic parallel depth.
An Induced Subgraph Paradigm for Strongly Regular Graph Constructions

How many disjoint copies of some graph $H$ can appear in an induced subgraph of a strongly regular graph? We give upper and lower bounds that depend on the number of vertices in their boundary. This generalizes a result of Lou-Murin which bounds the independence number of a (hitherto still elusive) strongly regular graph with parameters $(99,14,1,2)$. The equality cases suggest alternative structural approaches for potential constructions of such a graph. We show, using computer searches, that one cannot impose certain additional natural conditions for some of the cases.
Automorphic Dirac Operators and an Analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator on $Γ\backslash \mathfrak{H}$

In the 2010's Bombieri and Garrett showed that the discrete spectrum, if any, of a self-adjoint extension of a restriction of the hyperbolic Laplacian on the upper half plane is $s(s-1)$ where $ζ_{\mathbb{Q}(i)}(s) = 0$. However, they also showed that at most 94% of the zeros of zeta can participate in this spectrum. In an effort to obtain a larger discrete spectrum, Sands in 2020 characterized an automorphic Hamiltonian that is an analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator for the modular curve. The motivation for this is that the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator is a discretized version of the Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}$. In describing this operator, it is necessary to understand automorphic Dirac operators and the growth of the potential. Here, we explain several noteworthy features of automorphic Dirac operators, prove that Sands' Hamiltonian has a purely discrete spectrum using an explicit presentation of Kronecker's limit formula, and use the operator to give a characterization of an automorphic Schwartz space.
Extending Donaldson's HyperKähler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
Christian El Emam; Filippo Mazzoli; Nicholas Rungi; Andrea Seppi; Andrea Tamburelli

We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperKähler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperKähler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-Kähler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.
Causal Fingerprints Reveal Hidden Mechanisms in Partially-Observed Dynamical Systems
Zhang Jiang; Marios Andreou; Nan Chen

In partially-observed dynamical systems, distinct hidden mechanisms can produce similar observable summary statistics while explaining individual events differently. We introduce causal fingerprints: realization-dependent patterns that track how information about a hidden state is revealed through subsequent evolution. Within a prescribed dynamical model, we compare the filtering posterior, based on observations up to a given time, with the smoothing posterior, obtained after adding an expanding window of future observations. We quantify this retrospective information gain using Kullback-Leibler divergence and track its evolution as the future window of observational data expands. The fingerprint reveals both the strength and temporal reach of hidden influence, which can vary across events and their stages. Because the observed trajectory is held fixed while hidden-state inference depends on the candidate model, fingerprints reveal how competing dynamical mechanisms explain the same observations even when selected statistics agree. In linear Gaussian systems, we derive a characteristic fingerprint timescale for the temporal reach of hidden influence. Calibrated surrogates matching the observable mean, variance, and decorrelation time can still produce distinct fingerprints when feedback memory, hidden-noise memory, or hidden forcing timescales are misrepresented. Nonlinear examples reveal mechanism-dependent signatures for extreme bursts, oscillatory variability, and regime switching, including multiplicative instability versus additive forcing, deterministic nonlinear feedback versus state-dependent multiplicative noise, and intrinsic bistability versus hidden double-well forcing. Causal fingerprints therefore provide a time- and event-resolved diagnostic for asking not only whether a model reproduces observed statistics, but how its hidden dynamics explain individual events.
Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics

We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.
Tensor-generating line bundles on toric varieties
Daigo Ito; Michael R. Zeng; Xiangru Zeng

A line bundle is $\otimes$-generating if its powers generate the derived category of perfect complexes. Refining the derived Nakai--Moishezon criterion of Ito--Olander, we characterize $\otimes$-generating line bundles on proper toric varieties by a combinatorial criterion on the fan, leading to the notion of $\otimes$-generating fans characterizing $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Furthermore, we prove an analogue of Kleiman's criterion of ampleness for $\otimes$-generation. As applications, we provide several examples including: (i) smooth proper fourfolds with no $\otimes$-generating line bundle, by showing that products of two or more positive-dimensional proper toric varieties admit a $\otimes$-generating line bundle only when they are projective, (ii) families of smooth non-projective proper threefolds with $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Finally, we study subvarieties obstructing $\otimes$-generation of canonical bundles and implications to autoequivalences of derived categories.

Given a joint distribution $P_{XY}$ on a finite alphabet, the information bottleneck method seeks a representation $T$ of $X$ that is as informative as possible about $Y$ while compressing $X$, where $T$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $X$. We show that computing the optimal value $\mathrm{IB}(P_{XY},R) = \sup_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \le R \}$ of the information bottleneck problem, as well as its Lagrangian relaxation $L_β(P_{XY}) = \sup_T \big[I(Y;T) - βI(X;T)\big]$, is NP-hard. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither $\mathrm{IB}(P_{XY},R)$ nor $L_β(P_{XY})$ can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-3/2}$.
Uniform Intersection Numbers and Subgroup-Based Generating Graphs of Groups

The uniform intersection number of a finite group $G$, denoted by $ui(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the intersection of any $k$ distinct maximal subgroups of $G$ is equal to its Frattini subgroup. We determine the uniform intersection number of dicyclic, dihedral, and quasi-dihedral groups. We then investigate the uniform intersection number through the subgroup-based generating graph $\mathcal{G}(G)$ of a finite group $G$. We characterize the finite groups $G$ for which both the intersection number and the uniform intersection number are equal to two, and show that this condition is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}(G)$ being complete multipartite. We also classify finite groups in terms of the diameter, girth, and perfectness of $\mathcal{G}(G)$. Finally, we show that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $n=p_1^{r}p_2^{r}$, where $r\geq 2$ and $p_1$ and $p_2$ are distinct primes.
Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
Ismail Cosandal; Sennur Ulukus; Nail Akar

In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.
Real-Arithmetic Sketched Eigensolvers for Symmetric Matrices

In this work, we develop sketched variants of subspace iteration and TraceMIN, called sSI and sTraceMIN, for real symmetric eigenvalue problems by combining basis whitening with the sketched Rayleigh-Ritz (sRR) procedure. The nonsymmetric projected matrix in sRR may have nonreal eigenpairs, leading to complex arithmetic and additional computational costs. We overcome this difficulty using a real Schur formulation of sRR that keeps the iterations in real arithmetic. We further develop procedures for characteristic subspace selection and convergence monitoring within this formulation. On the theoretical side, we discuss suitable subspace embedding assumptions for sketched eigensolvers that use a fixed sketching matrix throughout the iterations. Under a mild embedding assumption, we establish local convergence results for sSI and sTraceMIN. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime savings of up to 39% for sSI and 21% for sTraceMIN relative to their standard counterparts on the test problems.
Global well-posedness of the periodic Majda-Biello systems in the resonant case

We study the Cauchy problem for the following Majda-Biello system in the resonant case $α\in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$ on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}$. \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} u_{t} + u_{xxx} & = & - v v_x, v_{t} + αv_{xxx} & = & - (uv)_{x}, (u,v)|_{t=0} & = & (u_0,v_0), \end{array} \right. \quad x \in \mathbb{T}, \, t \in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, the initial data $u_0$ and $v_0$ live in the Sobolev space $H^{s}(\mathbb{T})$ and $u_0$ has zero mean over $\mathbb{T}$. We establish the optimal global well-posedness for the above system when $s\geq \min\{1, s_α+\}$, where $s_α$ is a constant depending only on $α$, and $s_α= \frac12$ for almost every $α\in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$. These indices match the sharp ones in the local theory obtained by Oh (Int. Math. Res. Not., 18:3516-3556, 2009). The main novelty of our proof is to introduce a third modified energy in the I-method by performing a partial correction to the second modified energy around the resonant region. This partial correction avoids the singularity in the full correction, and therefore makes it possible to pointwise bound the quintilinear multipliers arising in the time derivative of the third modified energy. Another feature in our proof is the combination of the Diophantine approximation theory with the sparsity of nearly resonant frequency pairs on the periodic lattice to obtain the key quadrilinear and quintilinear estimates, leading to an almost conservation law sufficient for the global iteration.
The ReLU Matrix Decomposition: NP-Hardness, Ill-Posedness, and ReLU-Rank
Giovanni Seraghiti; Arnaud Vandaele; Nicolas Gillis

The ReLU Matrix Decomposition (RMD) approximates a sparse, nonnegative m-by-n matrix X by max(0, WH), where W is an m-by-r matrix, H is an r-by-n matrix, and r is the rank of the decomposition. The most common formulation, referred to as Fro-RMD, minimizes the Frobenius norm of X - max(0, WH) over W and H. We prove that Fro-RMD is NP-hard, even for binary matrices and r = 1; to the best of our knowledge, this is the first complexity result for RMD. We also show that Fro-RMD is ill-posed, in the sense that its infimum may not be attained. We then turn to exact RMD, that is, X = max(0, WH), and define the ReLU-rank of X as the smallest r for which such a decomposition exists. We interpret exact RMDs geometrically as configurations of points and hyperplanes in an r-dimensional space, associated with the rows of W and the columns of H, respectively. Building on this interpretation, we derive upper bounds on the ReLU-rank of diagonal, block-diagonal, and block-sparse matrices and, under an additional structural assumption, improve the best known bound for block-diagonal matrices. Finally, we propose two formulations of exact RMD as feasibility problems: a nonconvex quadratically constrained program, which can be tackled by global solvers such as Gurobi, and a formulation based on the latent model of Saul, (``A nonlinear matrix decomposition for mining the zeros of sparse data', SIMODS, 2022), which we tackle using alternating projections for which we establish local convergence together with asymptotic convergence rates. We compare these two approaches on some numerical examples.
Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
Amir Hashemi; Rozhin Sadr; Werner M. Seiler

Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity underlying these invariants in terms of $β$-maximal position and strong stability. In particular, we show that $β$-maximal position suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required generic positions and for computing these invariants.
Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems
Ivan Kaygorodov; Cándido Mart\'ın González; Antonio Viruel

Evolution algebras, introduced by J. P. Tian as an algebraic model of non- Mendelian inheritance, are commutative algebras with a basis whose distinct elements multiply to zero. The first part of the paper surveys the theory: low-dimensional classifica- tions, structure theory, nilpotency, automorphisms and derivations, directed graphs and random walks, infinite-dimensional and dynamical aspects, and embedding theorems. The second part is a unified list of fifty open questions and eleven new conjectures, each accompanied by the available evidence; two of the conjectures and one of the questions are settled here. We also prove several new observations, most of them formally verified in the proof assistant Lean (see Section 2.1.11): every finite group is the automorphism group of a simple evolution algebra over every field, and | Aut(A)|/ dim A takes every positive ratio- nal value on simple evolution algebras over every field; infinitude of the automorphism group of nilpotent algebras, the possible numbers of idempotents of real perfect evolution algebras, a Galois-theoretic criterion for the existence of idempotents in dimension two, the average number of idempotents over finite fields, and a perfect evolution algebra whose automorphism group is a non-split extension.
An infinite completely normal basis theorem

Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $φ:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $φ^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.
Geometric Graph Representations via Compact SAT Encodings
L. Sunil Chandran; Rishikesh Gajjala; Suraj Kumar Sahoo; Aatman Supkar

We present compact SAT encodings and certifying exact solvers for boxicity and cubicity. The boxicity of a graph is the minimum dimension in which it is the intersection graph of axis-aligned boxes; cubicity is defined analogously using unit cubes. Grid-based formulations face a geometric discretization bottleneck, growing rapidly with the target dimension. We avoid this bottleneck by encoding the total order of interval endpoints in each coordinate. For an $n$-vertex graph and target dimension $d$, our boxicity encoding uses $O(n^2d)$ variables and $O(n^3d)$ clauses, both linear in $d$. Requiring the left- and right-endpoint orders to agree yields a cubicity encoding of the same asymptotic size. Satisfying models are decoded into independently checked geometric representations, while unsatisfiable instances used as lower-bound evidence carry mechanically verified DRAT certificates. In a controlled evaluation with 186 trials per encoding on standard and structured graph families, the order encoding solves 96.8% of trials, compared with 71.0% for the known grid formulation, and reduces mean PAR-2 time from 178.21 to 21.70 seconds. The pipeline also certifies exact values for several named graphs. We turn one such value into a reusable obstruction by proving that every Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ with $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$ contains an induced Desargues graph. The resulting lower bound, together with an explicit three-dimensional representation of $K(7,3)$, establishes $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(7,3))=3$. This disproves the conjecture of Caoduro and Sebo that $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(n,k))=n-k$ for all $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$.
Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
Shiyuan Zhang; Xuheng Li; Qiwei Di; Quanquan Gu

Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.
Transference theory for the trilinear restriction estimate and an application to the quadratic NLS in 3D
Ioan Bejenaru; Vitor Borges; Tiklung Chan

In this article we develop a theory for effectively transferring trilinear restriction estimates for the Schrödinger equation to functions in a more general resolution space adapted to the Schrödinger equation. As an application we provide a global theory for the quadratic NLS in three spatial dimensions in the critical Sobolev space $\dot{H}^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
Classes of integrable metrics on Banach spaces

We introduce a large new class of (weak) metrics on the Hardy space that have infinite families of conservation laws in involution. The construction of the metrics and the integrals involve the Hankel operator and a field of Nijehuis operators. The commutativity of the integrals is based on the notion of the coupling transform, which allows us to recursively construct new classes of metrics and integrals. We characterize the spectrum of the Nijenhuis operators. The paper establishes a connection between a rich class of completely integrable geodesic flows appearing in the finite dimensional Riemannian geometry and a new class of integrable systems in Banach spaces.
Design of a Family of Rate-Adaptive LDPC Convolutional Codes with Short Constraint Length
Massimo Battaglioni; Edoardo Carnevali; Franco Chiaraluce; Marco Baldi; Giovanni Cancellieri

This paper studies the design of some high-rate, adaptive, low-density parity-check (LDPC) convolutional codes with short constraint length, based on interleaved parity-check polynomials. Starting from some known results regarding the selection of polynomials that yield codes free of short cycles in the associated Tanner graphs, we propose some new constructions based on Golomb rulers, along with relaxed variants that do not strictly satisfy the Golomb ruler condition, but retain similar structural properties. The result is a family of rate-adaptive code constructions with code rates of the form $R=(n_0-1)/n_0$. Conditions for the absence of length-4 cycles are derived, together with upper bounds on the free distance that are met in all considered examples.
Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
Alessandro Carlotto; Yangyang Li; Zhihan Wang

We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.
Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
Enrico Da Ronche; Matteo Longo; Stefano Vigni; Francesco Zerman

Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.
A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
Guozheng Cheng; Xiang Fang; Menghan Li; Hongdou Qu; Chengbo Xiao

We give a quantitative planar form of a multiscale argument for Falconer's distance problem. For every $0<η<1$, we obtain a positive lower bound for the Lebesgue measure of the distance set of a compact subset of the unit ball supporting a probability measure with $ν(B(x,r))\le 2r^{1+η}$. The bound depends only on $η$. For a compact set of diameter $D$ carrying a probability measure with $μ(B(x,r))\le A(r/D)^{1+\varepsilon}$, localization gives $|ΔE|\ge c_{\varepsilon,p}DA^{-p}$ for every fixed $p>1/\varepsilon$. In particular, compact planar sets of Hausdorff dimension greater than one have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure. The proof develops the multiscale method of the September 2026 manuscript of OpenAI, using one sequence of restricted distance measures for both the mass and Fourier estimates. A reconstruction lemma combines summable total-variation errors with summable squared Fourier norms. No endpoint or sharpness assertion is made.
Logical isomorphism and logical limit laws for small permutation classes and regular languages

In this paper we show that for each small permutation class $\mathcal{F}$ there exists a regular language $L_\mathcal{F}$ such that the monadic second-order TOTO logic on $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to classical monadic second-order logic on $L_\mathcal{F}$. Thanks to the fact that regular languages are closed under monadic second-order restrictions this shows that many subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ have a well-behaved structure. In particular, this allows us to show that random permutations from any small permutation class satisfies convergence laws for both first-order logic and monadic second-order logic. In the latter case, the law is modular. Our proofs introduce a way of using the automaton description of regular languages to prove properties of generating functions which may be of independent interest. Potential applications include first-order limit laws for random words in some regular languages.
Gradient-Hessian Query Tradeoffs: Matching Lower Bounds in Logarithmic Dimension
Wendao Wu; Haihan Zhang; Chenheng Zhang; Yanyi Li; Chunyuan Zheng; Cong Fang; Haoxuan Li; Zhouchen Lin

We establish matching lower bounds for the tradeoff between gradient and Hessian queries in nonconvex optimization with Lipschitz Hessian. In normalized units, the initial objective gap is at most $T$, the Hessian Lipschitz constant is at most one, and the target gradient norm is one. For sufficiently large $T$, dimension $d \ge C\log(2+T)$, and a prescribed Hessian budget $h \ge 1$ with $h+1 \le aT$, every randomized algorithm requires $Ω(\min\{Td^{1/3}, T^{3/2}/\sqrt{h+1}\})$ ordinary queries. An ordinary query returns the value and gradient; a Hessian query returns the complete second jet and is charged only to its own budget. Both budgets are worst-case caps. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary real points, and no Hessian-norm bound is imposed. The hard input law consists of fixed, globally $C^3$, coercive functions. The construction combines sequential readouts of a continuous random matrix with localized completion blocks and reliability dimensions that vary across hierarchy levels. Premature disclosures are charged by their expected task cost, while every oracle reply remains the exact jet of the presampled objective. This yields a logarithmic dimension threshold and a depth-independent third-derivative bound. Together with a translation of the NALEN upper bound of Chen, Liu, Luo, and Zhang, the result determines the query tradeoff up to absolute constants throughout the stated range.
Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction

The paradigm of a simple unstable theory in the sense of Shelah is the theory of the random graph, the Fraïssé limit of the finite graphs. Quantum error correction has a paradigm of its own, and we show that it is the counterpart of the random graph: the Pauli group on countably many qubits, taken modulo phases and with commutation as its relation, is the Fraïssé limit of the finite alternating spaces over the two-element field, and its form computes the syndromes of stabilizer codes. Seen through this correspondence, simplicity theory turns out to be a theory of error correction. Clifford encoding circuits implement the homogeneity of the Pauli group, forking recognizes the logical errors, and the independence theorem of Kim and Pillay is the gluing of syndromes. The two paradigms look alike as first-order structures, and they part company only when observables enter. Each defines a bipartite observable, and we prove that, once preparations are mixed, both acquire the tree property of the second kind in real-valued logic. They reach it by different roads, however, and we show that the probes decide which. The probes of the Pauli observable are the Pauli channels; for them the indicator of each syndrome sector is the difference of the responses of two uniform mixtures, and actual mixtures already witness the tree. The probes of the Rado observable see only marginals; conditions given by actual mixtures remain compatible on disjoint blocks, and the tree must be sought among idealized preparations.
Series of Fano quiver moduli from extended Dynkin quivers

Associated to small extended Dynkin quivers, we construct series of Fano varieties of fixed Picard rank at most five and arbitrary even dimension, which admit a very explicit description of their geometry. For example, they all admit a flat morphism to a projective space, whose general fiber is a product of projective lines. We also give a closed formula for all Betti numbers, and interpret this formula in terms of an action of a cohomological Hall algebra on the cohomology of all the varieties in a series.

Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are multipartite entangled quantum states that play a central role in quantum information theory, with applications in quantum communication, cryptography, and distributed quantum computing. A major experimental goal is to create high-dimensional GHZ states using multiple entangled parties. Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger discovered a surprising bridge between these quantum-optical experiments and graph theory: certain photonic experiments can be represented by edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs, and the dimension of the produced GHZ state equals the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings. This led Krenn and Gu to conjecture that every GHZ graph with more than four vertices has dimension at most $2$. A counterexample would give a new high-dimensional multipartite GHZ construction, while a proof would clarify fundamental resource limitations in quantum optics. It is known that the conjecture holds for graphs of vertex connectivity at most $2$ [MFCS 2024], and that simple GHZ graphs with $n>4$ vertices have dimension less than $n/\sqrt{2}$ [Quantum 2024]. However, no general upper bound depending only on vertex connectivity was known. We prove that every simple connected GHZ graph $G$ with at least four vertices has dimension at most $2^{κ(G)-1}+\binom{κ(G)}{2}$, where $κ(G)$ is the vertex connectivity of $G$. We also prove new bounds in terms of edge connectivity and maximum degree.
The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations

This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.
Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM-Based Text Scoring
Wonjeong Jo; Gyuwan Kim; Ming Shan Hee

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in computational social science to assign scalar scores to social and psychological constructs. However, studies use different rating scales, and whether their scores remain comparable across scale designs is understudied. To address this gap, we define and systematically investigate scale sensitivity, the variation in LLM-generated scores caused by rating scale design. We distinguish numerical sensitivity, changes in normalized scores, from semantic sensitivity, changes in score interpretation. To assess both, our experimental design crosses 2 formats (continuous vs. ordinal), 4 ranges (3, 5, 11, and 21 points), and 2 signs (signed vs. unsigned) across 3 tasks (political leaning, sentiment, and toxicity), 2 prompting strategies (zero-shot and rubric-based), and 5 LLMs. We find that changing one design element shifts normalized scores by about 0.10 on average and changes the category of roughly 20% of texts. Sensitivity is greatest for toxicity, the only unipolar construct examined. Also, rubric-based prompting does not reduce sensitivity compared with zero-shot prompting. We provide practical guidance for designing more reliable LLM-based text scoring and highlight the need for robustness checks across alternative scales.
Tiexin Guo; Xiaohuan Mu; Pasqualetto Enrico; Qiang Tu; Guang Yang

To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-Šmulian theorems.
Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems

I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.
Per-State Signatures and Mean Time-to-Failure: An Algorithm for Systems With Simultaneous Failures

We present an algorithm that computes the structural signature and the mean time-to-failure (MTTF) of a monotone binary system at every one of its states, rather than only at the state in which all components work. It makes no assumption on the structure function and evaluates it exactly once per state, as many times as needed for the signature of the complete system alone, so computing the MTTF everywhere costs only a factor polynomial in the number of components over computing it once. As a by-product, it identifies all minimal path sets. We assume exchangeable component failure times whose survivor count is a continuous-time Markov chain.
