We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.
Von Neumann Type Inequalities for NC Operator Balls

We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $Ω=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $Ω(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $Ω(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{Ω,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(Ω(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\inΩ(n)$, with $C_{Ω,n}=(2ρ_ΩK_Ω)^{n-1}$; here $K_Ω$ is the Gleason constant and $ρ_Ω$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $Ω(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $ρ_Ω=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_Ω)^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.
On Partial Optimality in QUBO via Quadratic Posiform Autarkies

Partially optimal assignments (also called persistencies) allow combinatorial optimization problems to be reduced by fixing a subset of variables to values consistent with at least one optimal solution. For the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, such assignments can be computed efficiently via autarkies of quadratic posiforms. However, the largest autarky domain and thus the number of fixed variables can depend on the specific posiform representation. We show that every quadratic posiform with the greatest possible constant term (the roof-dual bound) yields the largest autarky domain obtainable from any quadratic posiform. By computing such a roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiform and a corresponding autarky with largest domain in polynomial time, one can therefore attain the maximum partial optimality obtainable by quadratic posiform autarkies in polynomial time. This justifies the computation of roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiforms and corresponding autarkies in popular polynomial-time algorithms and establishes that finding additional partial optimality in QUBO requires going beyond autarkies of quadratic posiforms.
Envelope Cubic Regularized Newton Method for Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
Qihao Zhou; Lesi Chen; Luo Luo; Chengchang Liu

We study nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problem $\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ in which the objective has $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian and condition number $κ$. We propose envelope cubic regularized Newton method (ECRN) which applies a refined inexact cubic regularized Newton method to the envelope of the primal function $Φ(\cdot) : = \max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\cdot,\mathbf{y})$. We show that ECRN finds approximate second-order stationary points of $Φ(\cdot)$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrtρ\,κ^{3/4}\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ second-order oracles, improving the condition number dependence $\mathcal{O}(κ^{2})$ achieved by the best known second-order methods. Our improvement comes from the key observation that the Hessian Lipschitz parameter of the envelope is $\mathcal{O}(ρκ^{3/2})$, which is sharper than the order of $\mathcal{O}(ρκ^{3})$ for the function $Φ(\cdot)$. We also conduct a lower bound on second-order methods to show that our complexity is optimal up to a logarithmic factor.
Weak (1,1) Shur multipliers and the Hörmander--Mikhlin--Schur theorem

Let $S_m$ be the Schur multiplier with symbol $m$. We characterize the boundedness of $S_m:\mathcal S^1\to\mathcal S^{1,\infty}$ by approximation of weighted columns in a common finite-dimensional subspace. If $W(m)$ is the weak $(1,1)$ bound and $\fD(m)$ is the column approximation constant, then $\tfrac12W(m)\le\fD(m)\le2W(m)$. These estimates hold uniformly under amplification. We also prove the Hörmander--Mikhlin--Schur weak $(1,1)$ estimate in every Euclidean dimension under the usual integer-order condition. The proof combines Cuculescu's projections, adjacent dyadic grids and tensor polynomial interpolation on a binary block decomposition.
Generation by lazy and invertible cellular automata over the Klein four-group
Edgar Alcalá-Arroyo; Alonso Castillo-Ramirez; Haobo Ma; Wenlin Zhang

Let $G=C_2\times C_2$ and $A=\{0,1\}$. We characterize the submonoid of $\text{CA}(G;A)$ generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata. A cellular automaton belongs to this submonoid if and only if, whenever it maps the two free $G$-orbits onto the same free orbit, it maps both constant configurations and some two-point orbit to the same constant. The proof gives a factorization using elementary orbit collapses and three two-cell lazy maps. The criterion yields the cardinality $59\,712$ and identifies the maps missed by a weaker constant-separation invariant. Adjoining one idempotent generates the full monoid, and the generated submonoid is contained in exactly one maximal proper submonoid, of cardinality $65\,024$. The submonoid generated by lazy maps alone has $4\,007$ elements, and for both generating sets the maximum shortest-word length is six. The criterion and the cardinalities $59\,712$ and $4\,007$ are formally verified in Lean.
Xiaohong Cai; Ruze Zhang; Laigang Guo; Raymond W. Yeung

We study cache-aided linear computation in distributed systems where each source generates and stores its own data. An external receiver requests a linear combination of these data, and the sources use information cached before the request is known to reduce the communication needed to recover the requested result. In our model, each of the $N$ sources stores its own independent file over a finite field and has an additional cache of normalized size $M$. The receiver must recover any requested linear combination with zero error from the messages sent by the sources over separate noiseless links. We establish a lower bound on the worst-case communication rate over any finite field by analyzing several requests under the same cache placement. This bound determines the optimal rate when no additional cache is available. For binary files, we propose parity-aided placement (PAP), a coded-placement scheme that combines cached parities with uncoded symbols. For every $N\geq3$, we characterize its communication rate for each request and optimize its placement parameters to obtain a closed-form worst-case rate. The resulting achievable rate meets the lower bound for $0\leq M\leq1/(2N-1)$ and $M\geq(N-1)/N$, establishing the optimal memory--rate tradeoff in these two ranges.
Antoine Abram; Florent Hivert; James D. Mitchell; Jean-Christophe Novelli; Maria Tsalakou

In this paper we describe the quotients of several plactic-like monoids by the least congruences containing the relations $a^{σ(a)} = a$ for $σ(a) \geq 2$ for every generator $a$. The starting point of this paper is the recent paper of Reutenauer and the first author about the stylic monoid. This monoid is the quotient of the plactic monoid by the relations $a^2 = a$ for every generator $a$. The plactic-like monoids considered here are the plactic monoid itself, the Chinese monoid, the hypoplactic monoid, the sylvester monoid, the metasylvester and hyposylvester monoids. In each case we describe a set of normal forms and the idempotents. We obtain formulae for their cardinalities and we describe their isomorphism types.
S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms

Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.
Quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical Schrödinger map flow
Jacek Jendrej; Jitao Xu; Xu Yuan; Lifeng Zhao

We study the Cauchy problem for the energy-critical Schrödinger map into the 2-sphere: \[ \partial_{t}u = u\timesΔu, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{1+2}, \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{S}^2 \] for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. Given any integer $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate \[ λ(t)\sim \frac{\left(T-t\right)^L}{\left|\log(T-t)\right|^{\frac{2L}{2L-1}}} \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow T. \] Our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by Rapha{ë}l and Schweyer~[Anal. PDE 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. However, its adaptation to a Schrödinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-Virial-Morawetz Lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.
Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers

For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$ Φ_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $Φ_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$ N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N). $$

We study the finite basis problem for flat semirings of the form $S(W)$, where $W$ is a nonempty set of nonempty words, possibly infinite. We prove that $S(W)$ is finitely based if and only if the strict interior of every word in $W$ is linear; here the strict interior of a word is obtained by deleting its first and last letters. This completely resolves an open problem raised by Jackson et al.~(J. Algebra 611: 211--245, 2022).
The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings

For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.
Jump limits of continuous multiscale diffusions: Homogenization under heavy-tailed activity bursts

We show that purely continuous microscopic diffusions can homogenize to a Markov process with genuine jumps. Consider a multiscale diffusion with time-dependent generator $\mathcal{L}_{0}+r_{t}^ε\mathcal{L}_{1}$ driven by a regenerative random environment. When the integrated activity over a regeneration cycle has a regularly varying tail of index $β\in(0,1)$, the cumulative operational clock converges to a $β$-stable subordinator, compressing finite activity-driven diffusion into vanishingly short physical time intervals. To overcome the noncommutativity of $\mathcal{L}_0$ and $\mathcal{L}_1$, we develop an extended-time parametrization paired with Khasminskii-type time discretization, establishing finite-dimensional convergence and strong semigroup convergence on $C_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ toward a jump process with nonlocal generator $\overline{\mathcal{L}}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-κ(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$. Under uniform ellipticity of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$, the fractional power $(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$ is identified as a $2β$-stable-like nonlocal operator. We also clarify physical-time path-topology obstructions and apply the framework to Poisson resetting pulses, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, and multiscale stochastic volatility.

Our previous work established the mapping cone Chern character on the even-degree side, using the powers of the mapping cone curvature associated with the given mapping cone connection. In this paper, we carry out the odd-degree version using a trivial mapping cone connection and an automorphism on a trivial complex vector bundle. This version is based on the related odd-degree transgression.
Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces

Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
LLCT: Learnable Linear Canonical Transform Family with Stability for Visual Feature Processing
Zunwei Fu; Zhen Wang; Dachun Yang; Shuhui Yang

Visual structures are often characterized by directional geometry, local oscillation, and spatial--frequency coupling. To overcome the limitations of conventional spatial convolutions mainly operating on fixed Euclidean coordinates, this article develops the learnable linear canonical transform (LLCT) framework that learns parameters within the linear canonical transform (LCT) family. The framework treats the LCT family as parameterized analytical views spanning spatial, Fourier, and intermediate linear canonical representations. The framework has the following two complementary modes. The Linear Canonical Riesz Transform (LCRT) mode combines learned linear canonical coordinates with regularized Riesz-type directional responses at sites chosen for geometric and local-structural refinement. The learnable LCT mode provides the integrated responses for latent feature sites. We establish the parameter stability of the LCT representation under admissible perturbations of the canonical matrices. Both modes use chirp multiplication and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) to preserve feature dimensions and support automatic differentiation. Experiments on crack segmentation and single-image deraining evaluate the above two modes with multiple backbones. On four segmentation backbones, the full LCRT mode gives the highest reported point estimates of F1 and IoU for the crack class among the tested variants. The learnable LCT mode gives higher values in 30 of 32 paired PSNR and SSIM measurements across four deraining backbones and four datasets. In ablation studies, the full model has the highest reported PSNR and SSIM among five tested configurations.
Scaled Companion Linearizations for Coefficientwise Backward Stability

A central goal in solving a polynomial eigenvalue problem is to compute eigenpairs that are exact for a nearby polynomial, with each coefficient perturbation bounded by a modest multiple of unit roundoff times that coefficient's norm. A backward stable eigensolver for a linearization does not automatically provide this coefficientwise relative guarantee. Scaling can improve accuracy, but a single scaling may not work across a widely spread spectrum. We construct a family of scaled companion linearizations that covers the nonzero complex plane. Each linearization is paired with a region and an eigenvector recovery rule for which the backward-error amplification factor is bounded at exact pencil eigenvectors, independently of coefficient norm disparities. Tropical roots guide the construction, and their multiplicities reduce the number of required solves. These results provide a basis for coefficientwise relative backward stability across the spectrum.
Topological degree for singular $N$-mean field equations
Mohameden Ahmedou; Zhongwei Tang; Heming Wang

We determine the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Dirichlet $N$-mean field equation on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\geq2$, for every positive nonresonant parameter and singular exponents $-1<α_i\leq0$. The formula depends only on the Euler characteristic of the domain and the weights $(1+α_i)^{N-1}$. We also identify the homotopy type of every sufficiently negative variational sublevel with the corresponding weighted barycenter space. We prove quantization of interior concentration masses and exclude boundary concentration and residual diffuse mass. The degree computation uses common descent fields for nearby parameters, bounds for their trajectories, and a finite-dimensional comparison with the Euler characteristic of negative sublevels. Annular averaging and dilation provide local contractions, which are extended to establish the sublevel homotopy equivalence. The arguments apply to the nonlinear, possibly degenerate $N$-Laplacian with singular weights, without requiring a global Palais--Smale condition or isolation and nondegeneracy of solutions.
An upper bound for valuations of elliptic nets at primes of bad reduction

Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve over a field defined by the short Weierstrass equation and let $\mathbf{P}=(P_1, P_2) \in E(K)^2\setminus \{(O, O), (\pm P, \pm P)\}$ be a pair of non-torsion points, where $O$ denotes the point at infinity. We give a uniform upper bound for the quantity $\min(ν(Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})), 2ν(Ψ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})))$, where $ν$ is a normalised discrete valuation associated to primes where $E$ has bad reduction and $Ψ^2_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$, $Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$ are rational functions for describing $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points $[v_1]P_1+[v_2]P_2$ on $E$, higher--dimensional analogues of division polynomials $ψ^2_n, ϕ_n$ known as net polynomials. They are also elliptic nets, which are $n$--dimensional arrays with values in $K$ satisfying the same nonlinear recurrence relation that division polynomials do as well. Hence, they are useful in studying counting problems on elliptic curves.
Benign Degeneracy for First-Order Methods in Exact Boolean Moment-SOS Relaxations

Pseudo-Boolean optimization -- minimizing a polynomial over $\{\pm 1\}^n$ -- includes MAX-CUT, binary quadratic optimization, and Ising models. The moment-sum-of-squares (Moment-SOS) hierarchy provides certified semidefinite relaxations that are often empirically exact at low order. We ask: once a relaxation is exact, how difficult is the resulting semidefinite program (SDP) to solve with first-order methods? Exactness does not imply regularity. At every order $d \ge 2$, a unique rank-one moment optimum is primal degenerate; moreover, if one optimal SOS certificate is strictly complementary, then the certificate set is positive-dimensional and contains singular boundary points. Thus first-order methods may converge to singular endpoints, around which pointwise analyses that assume regularity at the limit cannot establish a local linear convergence rate. We show that, for exact Boolean Moment-SOS relaxations in their canonical quotient form, this degeneracy is nevertheless benign. We develop an abstract mechanism, which we call residual-field rigidity, that propagates regularity from the relative interior of the optimal set to its singular boundary. For Boolean Moment-SOS, unique rank-one exactness and the existence of one strictly complementary certificate suffice to trigger this mechanism, yielding a uniform error bound around the entire optimal set. Consequently, exact ADMM, exact sGS-ADMM, and fixed-step PDHG converge eventually linearly from every initialization, even when their limiting certificate is singular. Finally, outside a lower-dimensional semialgebraic exceptional set of Boolean objectives, these hypotheses hold simultaneously at every uniquely rank-one exact order.
A new generalization of parking functions: $ρ$-Naples parking functions

We introduce a new model of parking functions, called $ρ$-Naples parking functions, in which each car has a certain number of spots to check preceding its preferred one before looking for available spots by moving forward. This notion, where each car has its own number of previous spots to check, generalizes that of Naples parking function, where this number is the same for all cars. We start by showing that, for a given sequence of preferences for each car, a successful parking strategy (that is, an assignment of how many backward spots each car is allowed to check) remains successful if we increase the number of backwards spots to check for some of the cars. This means that the set of successful strategies for a given parking preference is an up-set in the lattice of parking strategies, which raises the intriguing question of characterizing such up-sets. Though we are not able to completely solve this problem, we provide a characterization of those successful strategies which minimize the total number of allowed backward steps for a given parking preference, and we determine a lower bound for the number of cars which are allowed to move backwards (also showing that it can be attained). To conclude, we analyze the specific situation in which each car can take at most one backward step, and we completely characterize the set of successful parking preferences in this case.
Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
Oskar Broukal; Michael Feischl; Conor Osborne

Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Matérn DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Matérn kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.
Geometric $C^1$-stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow

We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or Hölder control of the normal is assumed. The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre. For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. This produces an instantaneously smooth evolution with the same eventual convexity and smooth exponential convergence.
Nonexistence of Strongly Regular Graphs via Gegenbauer Positivity and SRG Counting
Zhen-Qi Liao; Jiaxin Wang; Wei-Hsuan Yu; Jianfeng Cai

This paper develops a natural extension of the multipoint spherical semidefinite method of Liao and Yu~\cite{LY}, studying the interaction between semidefinite programming and strongly regular graph counting. Starting from the positive semidefinite kernels furnished by Gegenbauer polynomials, we express weighted kernel sums and counting identities in the same labelled induced-subgraph counts. Eliminating the counting equations gives a semidefinite feasibility problem. Numerical dual solutions guide the construction of rational certificates, whose contradiction identities are verified exactly. Our aim is a systematic method that treats many parameter sets through the same construction. For least eigenvalue $-3$, it gives new counting certificates for $(351,140,73,44)$, $(550,162,75,36)$, $(703,182,81,35)$ and $(1344,221,88,26)$, previously excluded by Liao and Yu~\cite[Theorem~1]{LY}, and for six additional parameter sets: \[ \begin{array}{@{}lll@{}} (375,102,45,21), & (405,132,63,33), & (441,88,35,13),\\ (476,133,60,28), & (540,147,66,30), & (575,112,45,16). \end{array} \] Seven certificates use Gegenbauer positivity and counting information alone at the displayed orders. The cases $v=375,441,575$ additionally use proved short-vector restrictions, unique vertex extensions, and integer common-neighbour inequalities. The proofs end in displayed inequalities with incompatible signs. Their justification is given by the dual identities and the proved positivity and counting relations; accompanying code automates the longer rational arithmetic.
The finite basis problem and subvariety intervals for max-plus matrix semirings

Let $S=(\N,\max,+)$ be the max-plus algebra of the nonnegative integers, and let $\overline S$ be obtained from $S$ by adjoining $-\infty$ as a semiring zero. We first prove that the varieties generated by the full matrix semirings $\Mat_n(S)$ and by the upper triangular matrix semirings $\UT_n(\overline S)$ form strictly ascending chains. Every interval between distinct members of either chain has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and contains a chain and an antichain of that cardinality. The proof uses finite syntactic semirings associated with prime-cycle languages and an independent family of identities. We then construct finite commutative ai-semirings from languages of monomials closed under divisibility and prove their bounded-variable property by cancellation, explicit integer evaluations and independence in a free abelian group. A loop-block identity for upper triangular matrices and dimension-independent cubic-padding identities for full matrices show that every variety in each of the above intervals has infinite axiomatic rank. In fact, every variety between $\V(S)$ and the variety generated by all full matrix dimensions has infinite axiomatic rank. These varieties are therefore nonfinitely based, also relative to the ai-semiring axioms. Finally, for every fixed full matrix dimension, we prove equational equivalence over all six positive or nonnegative integer, rational and real coefficient domains. The original convex-ideal countermodels and their full-matrix transfer proof are recalled separately for comparison; they are not used in the algebraic proofs. Throughout, the signature consists of two binary operations and contains no constant symbols.
Guangshi Lü; Zhiwei Wang; Jie Wu

An old conjecture dating back at least to Hildebrand's work in 1989, asserts that the Möbius function exhibits cancellation on shifted primes; that is, $$\sum_{p\le x}μ(p+2)=o(π(x)),\quad \text{or equivalently}\quad \sum_{n\le x}Λ(n)μ(n+2)=o(x).$$ This is also a well-known model case for the parity problem in sieve theory. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. As an application, we show that each of the two sets $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=1\}$ and $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=-1\}$ has asymptotic density $1/2$ among the primes $p$ with $μ^2(p+2)=1$: \begin{equation*} \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\#\{p\le x:\ μ(p+2)=κ\}} {\#\{p\le x:\ μ^2(p+2)=1\}} =\frac12, \quad κ\in\{-1,\,1\}. \end{equation*}
Chow groups of symmetric products of projective spaces

Let $\operatorname{SP}^{d}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the $d$-th symmetric product of complex projective space.We prove that its integral cycle class map is split injective and has finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$.We also compute the ranks of its Chow groups.By constructing compatible integral retractions on Chow groups and singular homology, we prove that addition of a fixed point induces an isomorphism on the Chow group of $q$-dimensional cycles whenever $d\geq q$.For $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq 6$, we construct a nonalgebraic class of order two in codimension two.Its image generates a direct summand of the cycle class cokernel and remains nonalgebraic after addition of fixed points.Consequently, integral surjectivity fails both at certain finite stages with $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product.We further identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology of the smooth configuration space.Finally, we provide an example where multiplication by an even integer annihilates a nonzero Chow class of order two.
The parity module of a matroid
Tom Braden; June Huh; Jacob P. Matherne; Nicholas Proudfoot; Botong Wang

We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded Möbius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.
Exact Cap Response and Aperture Selection for Molecular Communication under Aligned Drift
Yen-Chi Lee; Chun-An Yang; Nan Yang

Spatial reception under directed molecule transport requires balancing useful molecule capture against intersymbol interference (ISI). To characterize this balance, we study a fully absorbing spherical receiver that counts absorption events only within a prescribed cap. Using the known joint first-hitting law under aligned drift, we derive exact cap impulse, cumulative, and eventual responses. We perform stable cumulative evaluation. We then assess the derived responses through particle simulations and time-step comparisons, and demonstrate that our conditional-timing analysis explains when opposite drifts of equal magnitude can favor the same wider aperture. We also show that for the studied geometry and a symbol duration of $0.15$ s, the aperture that maximizes the signal-to-interference difference (SID) increases from $29.13^\circ$ at zero drift to $61.86^\circ$ at a drift magnitude of $40$ $μ$m/s. These results (i) connect joint arrival-time and location statistics to spatial reception design, (ii) characterize the tradeoff between useful molecule capture and ISI, (iii) support SID-based aperture selection for a given drift and symbol duration, and (iv) quantify the SID loss incurred by retaining the zero-drift optimal aperture for the same symbol duration.
Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures

We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_ϕ.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_ϕ$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$
Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise

We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or Lévy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.
Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields

We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.

We prove that every stable atomic (twisted) vector bundle on a projective hyper-Kähler manifold is 1-obstructed. In the appendix, we construct a simple atomic object that is not 1-obstructed, providing a counterexample to Beckmann's conjecture.
$χ$-Independence for BPS Invariants of Warped Local Curves

A well-known conjecture of Toda's asserts that the BPS invariants associated to a Calabi--Yau threefold are independent of the chosen Euler characteristic. We answer the question in the affirmative for a certain class of local surfaces, which we call warped local curves. Along the way we show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a warped local curve can be written as the global critical locus of a function. We also show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a curve fibration over $\mathbb{A}^1$ is the global critical locus of a function.
Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Drézet and Ballico-Ellia
Graham Denham; Rosa Miró-Roig; Hal Schenck

We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.
Characterization of $C^{1,α}$-domains in terms of Carleson-type $\varepsilon$-coefficients

Let $Ω=Ω^+\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary and let $Ω^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus\overline{Ω^+}$. For $x\in\partialΩ$, $r>0$, define \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r):=\frac{1}{r^n} \inf_{H^+}\mathcal{H}^n\left(((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^+)\setminus Ω^+) \cup ((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^-)\setminus Ω^-)\right), \end{equation*} where $\mathcal{H}^n$ stands for $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and the infimum is taken over all open affine half-spaces $H^+$ such that $x\in \partial H^+$. Here $H^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus \overline{H^+}$. In this work we prove that $Ω$ is a $C^{1,α}$ open set, with $0<α<1$, if and only if there exists some constant $C>0$ such that $\varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r)\leq C\,r^α$ for all $x\in\partialΩ$ and all $0<r\leq \mathrm{diam}(\partialΩ)$.
Fast spectral methods for Volterra integral equations

We develop novel methods for the fast construction of spectral approximations to smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra integral operators and for the fast evaluation of smooth nonlinear Volterra integrals. The proposed methods employ the Duffy mapping, which transforms the original indefinite integral into a definite integral and maps the original causal triangular domain to a square, thereby avoiding any artificial extension of the kernel function. For smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra operators, the resulting approximations are almost-banded and lower-banded, respectively. The $N\times N$ principal finite section of these approximations can be constructed in $O(N)$ and $O(N^2)$ flops, respectively, via recurrence relations. For Volterra integrals with a smooth kernel that depends nonlinearly on a given function, recurrence relations lead to fast evaluation with a complexity of $O(N^2\log N)$ when the function is approximated by a degree-$N$ Chebyshev approximant. These spectral approximations and evaluation procedures give rise to fast and stable spectral methods for solving Volterra integral equations, as well as a broad class of problems involving Volterra integral operators. Extensive numerical experiments show that these spectral methods significantly outperform existing methods in terms of stability, speed, accuracy, and ease of implementation.
Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$

We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

We identify a normalization defect in a determinantal construction of fourth-order Hahn difference equations and compare its scalar equation with Foupouagnigni's 1998 elimination and its published 2001 counterpart. On an explicit positive orthogonal family, all five prescribed coefficients vanish: the formula gives \(0=0\) and imposes no condition. Along an explicit regular perturbation, division by \(\varepsilon^2\) before specialization recovers a nonzero equation on that family, the same scalar equation as the correctly executed old shift-and-eliminate procedure. On the common nondegenerate domain specified below, both constructions give the same scalar operator up to a nonzero rational factor. The first-order degree bounds follow directly from valid identities of 1998; preserving cancellations gives a bound that can be arbitrarily sharper on explicit admissible inputs, together with exact top coefficients and cancellation criteria. Explicit coefficient formulas do not by themselves yield a new scalar equation on this domain. Our comparison does not exclude corrective or expository contributions; additional computational gain or exceptional coverage must be demonstrated.
Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
Yanyi Li; Wendao Wu; Haihan Zhang; Qinshi Wang; Chenheng Zhang; Chunyuan Zheng; Cong Fang; Haoxuan Li; Zhouchen Lin

Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.
Macdonald dual in the semilocal case and applications to local homology and local cohomology

This paper extends Macdonald's duality theory and Cuong-Nam's local homology theory -- which is in some sense dual to the local cohomology theory of A. Grothendieck [Gro1] -- to semilocal noetherian rings equipped with the $J$-adic topology. By overcoming the key structural obstructions of the semilocal setting via Zöschinger's structure theory and semilocal Matlis duality, this work establishes topological limit duality isomorphisms and links local homology with local cohomology. Ultimately, this framework provides the foundational machinery required to extend the classical results of Macdonald [Mac] and Cuong-Nam [C-N1] to the semilocal setting.
New bounds for $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ shifted convolution sums

Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$. We also treat the corresponding sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. Here $λ_π(1,n)$ denotes the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke--Maass cusp form $π$ on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$ denotes the number of representations of a positive integer $n$ by a positive definite integral binary quadratic form $\mathcal{Q}$. The proof combines two circle methods with a different organization of the major-arc analysis. A key point is that the nonzero Poisson frequencies are kept together in a single coefficient vector, rather than estimated separately, which allows them to be controlled by a finite matrix norm. The zero Poisson frequency is treated separately: its contribution is independent of the reduced residue class, and its arithmetic mean cancels the constant term in the complementary Jutila weight before absolute values are taken. We make this cancellation explicit, including the relevant normalization and local factors. The same mechanism extends to the binary quadratic-form setting, while the remaining Jutila contribution is handled by the available correlation estimates.
Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability

We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ Γ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(μ)-1-m_3(μ)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ Ψ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(μ)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $ε$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}ε.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $ε$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative Kähler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative Kähler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, Hörmander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.
Reciprocal Dynamics in Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
Max A. Alekseyev; Dmitry I. Khomovsky

For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, alternating monic reciprocal transformations define a rational discrete dynamical system on the finite-dimensional coefficient space of polynomial pairs. This system arises from congruence jumping in polynomial divisibility problems, where a quotient move changes the polynomial state, but its coefficient dynamics can be studied independently. We prove that every state with nonzero constant terms returns after four alternating updates to its rational gauge classes and classify when this return orbit is realized over $\mathbb Z$. The local obstruction is encoded by endpoint $p$-adic valuation defects. After the first integral block, constant-term valuations evolve by an explicit matrix $M_{n,m}\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ whose trace depends only on $s=nm$. This yields a finite-order, elliptic-type regime for $s<4$, a parabolic dilation regime for $s=4$, and a hyperbolic regime for $s>4$. In the hyperbolic case, invariant thresholds, irrational eigencones, and discrete valley formulas give finite criteria for forward and bi-infinite integral orbits; nevertheless, failure can be delayed arbitrarily long. At the pointwise level, separated auxiliary-relation transport factors through the jumped-variable projection. One jump preserves the visible support rank, while two alternating jumps collapse it to dimension at most one; saturation cannot restore rank. In the quadratic specialization, a rank-two $p$-adic relation lattice gives an exact local cancellation-depth formula and a finite criterion on periodic Vieta orbits. We classify the fixed auxiliary relations that saturate indefinitely on an irreducible six-cycle and construct arbitrarily long persistence on parabolic and fixed hyperbolic orbits.
Continuous-Time q-Learning with Nonsmooth Value Functions: a BSDE Approach
Manuel Asero; Elena Bandini; Andrea Cosso; Laura Perelli

We study continuous-time q-learning for entropy-regularized diffusion control without assuming classical differentiability of the value function. Rewards and admissible policies need only be Borel measurable, which allows discontinuous rewards. The diffusion coefficient $σ$ is action independent and locally uniformly elliptic, and the drift is $b_0 + σψ$, with $b_0$ action independent and $ψ$ bounded. In this setting the q-function involves the value only through its gradient. For each admissible policy, we represent its value by a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and prove that this value is continuous before the horizon, although the data are only measurable. Replacing the gradient with a measurable representation of the martingale integrand, we define the q-function up to Lebesgue-null sets and recover the classical definition when the value function is smooth. We then prove policy improvement, when the Gibbs update is admissible, and martingale characterizations of the value and the q-function from on-policy and off-policy observations. Here the candidate value need only be continuous before the horizon, and actions are sampled on a deterministic finite grid and held constant between sampling times. Under an integrability condition on the reward, we show that a second BSDE gives an upper bound for the optimal value, attained when its Gibbs policy is admissible, and we characterize its solution in the same way.
Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs

A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.
Integral Specializations of Polynomials: Hilbert Irreducibility, Coprimality, and Density
Angelot Behajaina; Pierre Dèbes; Martin Widmer

The Hilbert specialization property of a field, whereby irreducibility of polynomials is preserved under specialization of some of the variables, admits an integral counterpart where specialization takes place inside a ring and irreducibility is required over the ring. It is known that the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of integers of any global field $K$ satisfies this integrally Hilbertian property. Using a different approach, we reprove this result and strengthen it by showing that the corresponding integral Hilbert subsets of $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ are not only Zariski-dense, as required by integral hilbertianity, but also of positive density. A central ingredient is a generalization to the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of the Ekedahl--Poonen formula originally proved for $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. This formula, of independent interest, gives the density of tuples in $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ for which coprime polynomials in $k$ variables and with coefficients in ${\mathcal O}_K$ take coprime values. Our generalization requires estimates for the number of points of bounded height in an arithmetic progression. We obtain such estimates as our third main result, thereby contributing to the theory of heights.
Exact analytical spectra of an effective field-modified radial Schrödinger equation by the Nikiforov--Uvarov method

We revisit the effective radial Schrödinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter $C=\cosθ$, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form $V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr$. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component $\Vt(r)$ is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulthén-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of $s$-wave bound states. For each case we obtain the energy spectrum, the normalized eigenfunctions in terms of Laguerre or Jacobi polynomials, the location of the potential minimum, and closed-form radial moments. The spectra are independent of the orientation $θ$ and of the electric field, in agreement with the structure found by the TRA, while the field enters through the shape of $V(r)$, the radial moments, and the expectation value $\langle V\rangle_k$. All analytical results are confirmed by an independent finite-difference diagonalization.
On the generalized cohomologies of almost abelian solvmanifolds
Mauro de Andrade Pinto; Letícia Camponês do Brasil Maia; Leonardo F. Cavenaghi; Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

Generalized complex structures give rise to generalized Dolbeault, Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomologies. We study these cohomologies for invariant generalized complex structures on almost abelian Lie algebras $\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb R e_0\ltimes_A\mathfrak h$, where $\mathfrak h$ is an abelian ideal of codimension one, and on almost abelian solvmanifolds $Γ\backslash G_A$. We first show that the invariant generalized Dolbeault cohomology can be identified with the Chevalley--Eilenberg cohomology of the complex Lie algebra $\mathcal L$, the $+{\mathbf i}$-eigenspace of the structure, with coefficients in a character determined by the canonical line. We prove that $\mathcal L$ is itself an almost abelian Lie algebra; thus the cohomology reduces to the kernel and cokernel of an explicit derivation. Assuming that $A$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the cohomology dimensions and compare with compact quotients. Other comparison results are discussed, noting that the cohomology of invariant forms always injects into that of $Γ\backslash G_A$.
Elementary Proofs of Commonality of the House Graph and $K_4$ with One Edge Subdivided

A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random coloring with an equal proportion of each color. The house graph and $K_4$ with one edge subdivided once are known to be common by the flag algebra method. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický, and Volec asked for ``human-friendly'' proofs of the commonality of these two graphs. In this short note, we give flag-algebra-free proofs that both graphs are common.

Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnafé and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$. We prove the conjecture for $W=S_{3}$.
Model order reduction of HDG discretizations for harmonic wave propagation
Hélène Barucq; Florian Faucher; Ha Pham; Ishak Tifouti

We propose and analyze a projection-based model reduction method for the rapid and reliable solution of time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation problems over a frequency band, with particular emphasis on seismic applications. The high-fidelity model is based on a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization, formulated as a generalized saddle-point system coupling the volume and trace unknowns. The basis construction combines residual-based greedy sampling of the frequency parameter, enrichment with frequency derivatives of the HDG solution, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) compression. We establish the well posedness of both the high-fidelity and reduced problems and characterize their stability with inf-sup constants. We investigate the interaction between static condensation, inherent to the HDG discretization, and projection onto the reduced spaces, characterizing its implications for the reduced formulation and approximation errors. Since these operations do not commute in general, we derive a priori error estimates for both the trace and volume variables to quantify the gap between the two operations. We further identify a lifting condition on the volume reduced space that eliminates these gaps and yields a trace error estimate independent of the volume approximation error. Numerical experiments on the two-dimensional Marmousi model and a three-dimensional heterogeneous medium, with more than $10^{7}$ unknowns, illustrate the theoretical estimates and show that the reduced model achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude compared to the high-fidelity solver.
An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint

We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.
