In particular, by introducing the notion of a separating quiver, we find a condition on the quiver which is equivalent to the module of differential forms being a projective bimodule. For such quivers, one can construct bimodule connections, as well as bimodule forms which serve as noncommutative analogues of the Riemannian metric. As an illustration of the above concepts, we present a class of quivers for which one can construct Levi-Civita connections, i.e. torsion free connections compatible with a bimodule form.
On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points of p-th Order Hölder Smooth Functions in One Dimension

We study the query complexity of finding an an $\varepsilon$-stationary points of a one-dimensional non-convex function whose $p$-th derivative is $β_p$-Hölder continuous. We determine the optimal complexity for deterministic and randomized algorithms and for oracles that return only derivatives, only function values, or full local information. Randomness provably helps when only derivatives are available, function values help in all cases, and higher-order derivatives never do. Together with known results in higher dimensions, this shows how these benefits depend on the dimension. Our deterministic lower bound also implies that the optimal accuracy exponents of objective-function-free adaptive regularization of order $p$ (OFFAR$p$) in every dimension $d\ge1$ and of deterministic gradient-only trapping in dimension $d=2$.

We study Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone in $\R^{n+1}$ with weights satisfying an $m$-dimensional ball condition only at radii between $1$ and $R^{1/2}$, where $0<m\le n-1$. Within the discrete induction framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we obtain a family of bounds by combining multilinear refined Strichartz inequalities, narrow decoupling, and Lorentz rescaling. We also give lightplank, lattice, and hybrid lattice--Knapp examples.
Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups

For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.
Generalized Hamming Weights and Subcode Support Weight Distributions of Twisted Reed-Solomon Codes
Chao Liu; Hao Chen; Dabin Zheng; Yaqi Chen

In this paper, we determine the generalized Hamming weight hierarchies of two classes of twisted Reed--Solomon (TRS) codes. For TRS codes with one twist, we first determine all possible values of the generalized Hamming weights. We then give a complete characterization of the weight hierarchy in terms of the minimum distance of the dual code. Explicit conditions are derived for the minimum distances of the code and its dual, which make the whole weight hierarchy explicitly computable. As special cases, the obtained results recover several known characterizations for TRS codes to be MDS, NMDS codes, and $s$-gap AMDS codes. For TRS codes with two twists, we similarly determine the complete generalized Hamming weight hierarchy. In this case, the higher generalized Hamming weights are determined by the first two generalized Hamming weights of the dual code, for which explicit rank conditions are also obtained. In addition, we further determine the subcode support weight distributions of this class of single-twist TRS codes. More precisely, for each $1 \le r \le k$, we derive an explicit formula for the number of $r$-dimensional subcodes with a prescribed support size, thereby giving a complete description of the support distribution of subcodes.
Weighted and Sobolev Estimates for Fractional Schrödinger Operators with Reverse Hölder Potentials

We study weighted and Sobolev estimates for two fractional Schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq3$ and $0<s<1$. For the additive operator $L=(-Δ)^s+V$, with a nonnegative, nontrivial potential $V$ belonging to a suitable reverse Hölder class, $RH_q$, we establish a critical-radius form inequality and decay estimates for the semigroup mass. These yield a heat-kernel bound combining polynomial off-diagonal decay with a fixed positive exponent of decay relative to the fractional critical radius $ρ_s$. A decomposition at this scale gives weighted strong-type estimates for the semigroup maximal operator and weighted Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev estimates for $L^{-α/2}$, $0<αs<n$, together with the corresponding endpoint weak-type estimates. The admissible weights satisfy explicit growth restrictions determined by the kernel decay, and the fractional integration order is $αs$. We also consider the spectral operator $Q=(-Δ+V)^s$. Assuming $V\in RH_{q_1}$ with $n/(1+s)\leq q_1<n$ and classical critical radius $ρ_1(x)\geq1$, we prove that $\nabla Q^{-1/2}$ maps $H^{1-s,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $1<p\leq p_0$, where $1/p_0=1/q_1-1/n$. By duality, its adjoint maps $L^{p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $H^{s-1,p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $p_0^{'}\leq p^{'}<\infty$.
Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
Wentao Zeng; Yifan He; Xian Wu

We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.
Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach

In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $α$-$z$ relative entropies for $α<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.
Towards a Sum-of-Squares Proof for the Nonexistence of Conway's 99-graph

Conway's $99$-graph is a strongly regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ) = (99,14,1,2)$ and whose existence has long been an open problem. We use both a sum-of-squares program and the fact that a strongly regular graph with $λ= 1, μ= 2$ has no diamond or $K_{2,3}$ subgraph to derive a loose upper bound for the number of triangles that such a graph could contain. This bound is less than the number of triangles that the graph's spectrum asserts, implying that it does not exist.
Well-Posedness and Strong Convergence of Infinite-Dimensional Port-Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics
O. V. Iftime; A. J. van der Schaft

We establish a functional-analytic framework that justifies the LaSalle convergence argument outlined in [van der Schaft, 2026] on port-Hamiltonian primal-dual gradient dynamics for finite-horizon optimal control of linear systems. In addition to strict convexity of the running cost as in \cite{vanderSchaft2026PDGJuly}, our analysis requires global Lipschitz continuity of the cost gradient. This ensures that the nonlinear gradient operator is well-defined and Lipschitz on the entire underlying space. We establish global well-posedness of the optimizer dynamics: every initial value determines a unique global mild solution, and the associated solution operators form a contraction semigroup. Similar to [Gernandtand Schaller, 2025], this is proved using tools from maximal monotone operator theory. Assuming existence of an optimal solution, we combine a dissipation inequality with an infinite-dimensional LaSalle invariance principle to prove strong convergence of every trajectory with a relatively compact positive orbit to the unique optimal state, control, and costate. Moreover, we present a sufficient condition for compactness through uniform control regularity and show that convergence holds for all initial states. Finally, we present an example with a strictly but not strongly convex running cost for which every mild solution converges strongly to the unique equilibrium, while no global exponential estimate uniformly over initial values can be obtained.
Narayanan N; Nandana K. Vasudevan; K. Somasundaram

A graph is \emph{elementary} if its edges can be coloured with two colours so that the two edges of every induced path on three vertices receive different colours. Elementary graphs are one of the two basic classes in the Chvátal--Sbihi decomposition of claw-free perfect graphs; they include all line graphs of bipartite multigraphs and all complements of bipartite graphs. We prove that every elementary graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=χ(G)=ω(G)$, confirming for this class the conjecture of Gravier and Maffray that claw-free graphs are chromatic-choosable. The proof combines the Maffray--Reed description of elementary graphs as augmentations of line graphs of bipartite multigraphs, Galvin's theorem, an extremal (edge-maximal) choice of counterexample, and a Hall-type lemma describing how list colourings of a complete graph minus a matching can fail.
A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry

We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).
$H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
Andrea Angino; Tamás Dózsa; Matthias Voigt

We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.
Reflected Proximal Dynamics for Accelerated High-Accuracy Log-Concave Sampling
Bo Yuan; Wei Guo; Yongxin Chen

We study sampling from $π(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ is $α$-strongly convex and $β$-smooth with condition number $κ=β/α$. For this problem, the proximal sampler preserves the target exactly and recovers overdamped Langevin dynamics in the small-step limit, but its Gaussian resampling step discards directional information. Underdamped Langevin dynamics retains such information through momentum to accelerate exploration, motivating a proximal construction that combines target preservation with directional persistence. We introduce \textit{reflected proximal dynamics}, which combines proximal sampling with an exact reflection of the auxiliary variable, conditional kinetic motion, and controlled refreshment. We develop two realizations: a flux-resampled underdamped half-turn and a persistent-momentum quarter-turn. From a warm start with constant $χ^2$ divergence, both methods achieve total variation error $\varepsilon$ using $\widetilde O(\sqrtκd^{1/4})$ expected oracle queries. We further remove the supplied warm-start assumption by combining either sampler with existing posterior samplers in a proximal initialization stage with an optimized coarse step size. Accounting for both initialization and sampling yields $\widetilde O(κ^{6/7}d^{1/4})$ expected oracle queries. In both regimes, the dependence on the target accuracy $\varepsilon$ is $\mathrm{polylog}(1/\varepsilon)$, making reflected proximal dynamics a promising framework for accelerated high-accuracy log-concave sampling.

The object of interest is the maximum number, $h(n)$, of Hamilton cycles in an $n$-tournament. By considering the expected number of Hamilton cycles in various classes of random tournaments, we obtain new asymptotic lower bounds on $h(n)$. The best result so far is approximately $ 2.85584...$ times the expected number $g(n)$ of Hamilton cycles in a random $n$-tournament, and it is conjectured that $h(n)\sim cg(n)$ where $c\approx 2.855958$. The same statements hold for Hamilton paths.
A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group

We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.
RPA Decoding with Few Subspace Projections for Correcting Structured Error Patterns in RM Codes
Shiv Pratap Singh Rathore; Navin Kashyap

The Recursive Projection Aggregation (RPA) decoder for Reed-Muller codes uses, in its default implementation, all one-dimensional subspaces at each level of recursion. We restrict our attention to the case where the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$. It is known that if the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, then $2t+1$ subspaces at each level of recursion are sufficient to correct these errors. We show that, for structured error patterns, the number of subspaces required for correction can be reduced further by appropriately selecting the subspaces used for projection. In particular, when errors occur as a single burst of length $t < d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, three subspaces at each level of recursion suffice for correction. We obtain similar results for multiple bursts and other structured error patterns as well.
Subgroup Perfect Codes in Bi-Cayley Graphs
Masoumeh Koohestani; Nasrin Soltankhah; Mohsen Ghasemi

In this paper, we study perfect codes in bi-Cayley graphs, focusing on when two subgroups $H$ and $K$ of a group G can form a perfect code of the form $H_0 \cup K_1$. We first consider the problem for a general group G and then examine what happens for special classes of groups, particularly abelian groups. Along the way, we obtain several results, including a necessary and sufficient condition for normal subgroups to form a perfect code, as well as an equivalent condition for abelian groups in terms of their Sylow 2-subgroups. Finally, we study the same problem for dihedral groups, providing results for this important class of non-abelian groups.
Learning Rules, Memorizing Facts: An Information-Theoretic View of Hallucination
Gengze Xu; Anxin Guo; Yifei Hu; Xiangyu Wu; Yong Liu; Ziqiao Wang

Understanding the relationship between generalization and hallucination requires clarifying the role of memorization. We study this relationship from an information-theoretic perspective through a Selector-Density Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework. In the sparse random-fact limit, a uniformly bounded information budget per fact forces a nonvanishing false-positive rate at recall bounded away from zero, even when all facts are observed during training. In a rules-and-facts setting, we decompose model-data mutual information into rule learning, atomic-fact memory, and excess memorization, revealing competition between rule learning and factual memory even without excess memorization. A joint budget bound quantifies the resulting constraint on atomic hallucination under perfect atomic recall. Moreover, an additive Gaussian model shows that maintaining high recall for atomic and composite facts incurs false positives even under optimal data mixing. Finally, controlled relational experiments hint how training exposure, rule complexity, and model capacity shape these trade-offs.
Mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes

This work studies the relationship between the multigrading in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes, introduced by V. Buchstaber and T. Panov in their computation of these cohomology groups, and the multigrading in the cohomology of the corresponding complements of coordinate subspace arrangements, arising from the mixed Hodge structure. It is shown that these multigradings coincide. This result refines a theorem from Yu. Eliyashev's 2013 dissertation. Furthermore, results on the mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of complements of coordinate subspace arrangements are applied to the study of the same varieties over finite fields. In particular, various formulas are obtained for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and for the associated global $ζ$-functions.
Sharp decay characterization for the Oldroyd-B system with only velocity dissipation
Zhi Chen; Mingwen Fei; Lvqiao Liu; Jiahong Wu

We study the incompressible Oldroyd-B system on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, in the regime in which the velocity is the only dissipated quantity: the stress tensor undergoes neither relaxation nor diffusion. In this regime the operator $\mathbb P\operatorname{div}$ acting on symmetric stresses has an infinite-dimensional kernel consisting of exact stationary states, so no decay estimate can hold for the full stress tensor and the existing sharp-decay theory for dissipative systems does not apply. We identify the active pair $U=(u,Λ^{-1}\mathbb P\operatorname{div}τ)$ as the correct decaying observable and establish, in a critical hybrid Besov framework, a complete characterization of its large-time behavior. For $-d/2<σ_1<σ\le d/2-1$ we prove that $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^σ}=O(t^{-(σ-σ_1)/2})$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to $\dot B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$, and, for $σ<d/2-1$, that the two-sided estimate $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^σ}\simeq t^{-(σ-σ_1)/2}$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to a nondegenerate subclass $\mathfrak B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$ of $\dot B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$.
Contractivity of Rudin's diagonal restriction operator for $H^p$ of the polydisc
Ole Fredrik Brevig; Javier Gómez-Serrano; Joaquim Ortega-Cerdà; Kristian Seip

We establish that Rudin's diagonal restriction operator is contractive from the Hardy space $H^p$ of the bidisc to the Bergman space $A^p$ of the disc for $2\leq p<\infty$, and characterize all cases of equality. We extend the result to polydiscs and obtain applications to polynomial point evaluation among others. The proof relies on an explicit formula, deduced from certain Green's formulas, for the defect between the $p$th powers of the two $L^p$ norms.
Irreducible components of crystabelline deformation rings: the wildly ramified case

Let $p\geq11$ be a prime, and let $\barρ:\Gal(\bar\QQ_p/\QQ_p)\rightarrow\GL_2(\bar\FF_p)$ be a reducible and very generic representation. In this paper, we use ghost series \cite{Lghost2} to study the irreducible components of Kisin's potentially crystalline deformation rings of $\barρ$. For wildly ramified principal series inertial types and arbitrary regular Hodge--Tate weights, we distinguish the components by the crystabelline slopes on their generic fibers and determine the total number of irreducible components. Combining this with an explicit formula for the total Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber obtained from the Breuil--Mézard conjecture, we compute the Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber of each component. Every such multiplicity is one when $\barρ$ is non-split, and is either one or two when $\barρ$ is split, according to whether the generic fiber of the corresponding component parametrizes reducible or irreducible Galois representations.
Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
Marcus T. C. Lau; Alejandro Bravo-Doddoli

We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincaré equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{π\sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.
Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$

We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4πA\\ \le& \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\fracπ{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2κ|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2π}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau. A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.
Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes

We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.
Representation Type and Schurian Finiteness of Tits Algebras

We determine the representation type and Schurian finiteness of the Tits algebra of a finite central real hyperplane arrangement over an algebraically closed field. The algebra is representation-finite when the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes, tame when it has three, and wild when it has at least four. Moreover, it is Schurian-finite if and only if the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes. Both classifications hold over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. The proof combines Saliola's bound-quiver presentation with explicit module constructions, convex subquivers, essentialization, and deletion. In the $\mathbb{R}^2$ case, we describe all eleven indecomposable modules for two lines and construct a full exact embedding of modules over a free algebra for at least four lines.
C^(sigma+alpha) regularity for fractional Hamilton-Jacobi equations, and rates of convergence in periodic homogenization
Adina Ciomaga; Andrei Rodriguez-Paredes; Erwin Topp

We study two related questions for nonlocal equations of Bellman type: the regularity of solutions when the set of controls depends on the state variable, and the periodic homogenization of stationary nonlocal Hamilton-Jacobi equations driven by uniformly elliptic integro-differential operators of order $σ\in(0,2)$, whose kernels depend simultaneously on the slow variable, the fast periodic variable and the control. The effective equation is again a nonlocal Bellman equation, but its supremum runs over a set of viscosity Mather measures that varies with the space variable, in a merely Hölder continuous way. We first develop a $C^{σ+α}$ regularity theory for nonlocal Bellman equations with Hölder continuous, state-dependent index sets, extending the Schauder estimates of Caffarelli-Silvestre and Serra, in a general framework independent of homogenization. We then use these estimates as a source of compactness to construct a classical solution of the effective problem, unique among bounded classical solutions. Finally, combining this regularity with discounted approximate correctors, we make the perturbed test function method quantitative, and prove that the whole family of solutions converges to the effective solution, with the explicit rate $ε^{σα/(2+α)}$, where $α$ is the Hölder exponent of the data.
Geometric bulk conductances in even dimensions

Let $P$ be a short-range projector on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^{2n},\mathbb{C}^m)$ and $U=(U_1,\dots,U_{2n})$ be a transverse family of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. We give an elementary proof of a recent result of Martinian-Stoiber, which extends a two-dimensional result of Drouot-Zhu to all even dimensions. Specifically, using only Stokes' theorem and the Poincaré lemma, we show that the geometric Kubo formula $\operatorname{Tr}\big(P[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_1}]\wedge\cdots\wedge[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_{2n}}]\big)$ is the product of a topological integer $\mathcal{X}_U$, which depends only on the relative positions of $U_1, \dots, U_{2n}$, and of the bulk conductance of $P$. Our proof writes the geometric bulk conductance as the pairing of $P$ with a cochain on $\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$ - an idea originally due to Kitaev - and deforms the cochain rather than the sets $(U_1, \dots, U_{2n})$. The proof presented in this paper is due to Claude Opus 5.5.
Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero

We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.
A Proof of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
Cheng Chi; Shuang Sun; Yan Wang

We resolve a conjecture of Łuczak, Mieczkowska and Šileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erdős Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.
Repairing covariance functions on metric trees through a Hausdorff-type distance

A compact metric tree is the natural domain of spatial data recorded along a river network, a root system, or the branched processes of a cell, and a suitable distance between two points is the length of the path joining them. That distance admits almost none of the covariance models of spatial statistics, since only the roughest members of each family stay nonnegative definite, and the resulting fields are nowhere mean square differentiable. The repair proposed here is a change of metric. Comparing two points through their distances to the leaves gives a Hausdorff-type metric built from the shortest-path one. The new metric has a closed form, agrees with the shortest-path one inside every edge, and is strictly smaller across branching points. Any correlation function valid in a Euclidean space of dimension equal to the number of leaves may then be composed with it, returning the Matérn, powered exponential, and generalized Cauchy families at every degree of smoothness, and, on trees with few leaves, also correlations that change sign or have compact support. The same construction yields the multivariate Matérn and space-time models of the Gneiting class. In simulations covering a range of smoothness and of spatial scale, maximum likelihood provides estimates without appreciable bias, and on a reconstructed microglial cell the smooth models reduce the cross-validated prediction error by half.
Exploration strategies for Gaussian process bandit optimization with inference regret guarantees
Hwanwoo Kim; Jungwoo Hong; Kyungjae Lee

Existing cumulative regret guarantees for Bayesian optimization (BO) do not necessarily characterize the quality of the algorithm's final output. This gap is critical under noisy evaluations, where the goal is to return a single high-quality recommendation. To address it, we introduce efficient exploration strategies that can be incorporated into any BO procedure by occasionally replacing the acquisition query with an exploration query. To validate this approach, we bound the Gaussian process posterior standard deviation over the search space via the fill distance of the queries, which measures the largest region left unexplored. We then use this result to derive upper bounds on the inference regret, i.e., the gap between the global optimum and the function value at the algorithm's returned point. Empirically, these exploration strategies improve the final recommendations of existing BO algorithms on synthetic benchmarks, hyperparameter optimization, and a control task.
Regularity of the Price of Anarchy in Routing Games over the Multivariate Demand Space
Jiawen Wang; Hu Shao; Ting Wu

We study the price of anarchy (PoA) in nonatomic routing games as a function of the full vector of origin--destination demands. We show that the Beckmann value function is continuously differentiable on the positive demand cone, with gradient equal to the equilibrium origin--destination cost vector; hence the PoA is continuously differentiable on the regular demand region. We prove that the nondifferentiability set has Lebesgue measure zero and, when every edge cost is strictly increasing or constant, is covered by countably many codimension-one submanifolds. Under the same cost structure, all equilibrium objects are cellwise as smooth as the edge costs. For affine costs, the exceptional sets become finite unions of lower-dimensional polyhedral cells linked by an exact scaling law, and the maximum of the PoA over a cell closure is attained on the cell boundary, generalizing the one-dimensional endpoint result. The theory is illustrated on the Sioux Falls benchmark network.
Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing

The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.

We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.
Ambar Dubey; Tushar Singh; Shiv Datt Kumar

In this paper, introduce a new finiteness condition for commutative rings, called $Z$-Noetherian, under which every ideal contained in the set of zero-divisors $Z(R)$ is finitely generated. This condition lies properly between Noetherian and $Nil_{*}$-Noetherian. We establish intrinsic characterizations of $Z$-Noetherian rings and investigate their stability under nilpotent quotients and localizations. Under the assumption that $Z(R)$ is an ideal, we obtain a primary decomposition theorem for ideals contained in $Z(R)$. For $ZD$-rings, we prove a Cohen-type criterion characterizing $Z$-Noetherian in terms of the finite generation of prime ideals contained in $Z(R)$. We further establish $Z$-Noetherian analogues of the Hilbert Basis Theorem and Krull's Intersection Theorem. Finally, we establish a principal ideal theorem for $Z$-Noetherian rings. Collectively, these results show that several fundamental finiteness and structural properties of Noetherian rings extend to the broader class of $Z$-Noetherian rings.
A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions

On a complete noncompact Kähler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.
Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums

Let $μ_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(μ,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $μ$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.
A characterization of the finite model property for $ω$-categorical theories

A first-order theory $T$ has the {\em finite model property} if every first-order sentence that is implied by $T$ has a finite model. We give a characterization of when a complete $ω$-categorical theory $T$ has the finite model property. The characterization makes it possible to transfer stability theoretic results in [29] to certain classes of finite structures. This approach also gives information concerning properties that a sequence of finite ``base structures'' of ever larger size must have in order for its random expansions to a larger vocabulary to have a chance to satisfy a convergence law for first-order logic.
A counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for a nonlocal operator

We construct a counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for nonlocal inequalities of the form \begin{equation*} L_au(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}δ_yu(x) \frac{a(x,y)}{|y|^{n+σ}}\,dy \ge-f(x)\quad\text{in }B_1, \end{equation*} with $u\le0$ in $\mathbb R^n\setminus B_1$, where $δ_yu(x)=u(x+y)+u(x-y)-2u(x)$, and the measurable coefficient satisfies \begin{equation}\tag{C} λ\le a(x,y)\leΛ,\qquad a(x,y)=a(x,-y),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,\quad y\ne0. \end{equation} More precisely, for every $n\ge1$, $0<σ<2$, and $0<λ<Λ$, there exist a fixed coefficient $a(x,y)$ satisfying \textup{(C)}, a constant $d>0$, and nonnegative functions $u_j,f_j\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ such that $L_au_j\ge-f_j$ in $B_1$, $0\le f_j\le1$, and $|\operatorname{supp}f_j|\to0$ as $j\to\infty$, while $u_j\ge d$ on $B_{1/4}$ for every $j$. Consequently, this fixed operator admits no $L^p$ maximum estimate for any $1\le p<\infty$.
Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces

We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $λ$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(λ^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\logλ)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
Superintegrable systems in curved spaces via coalgebras and deformed Racah algebras
Samuel Jimenez-Swain; Ian Marquette; Yao-Zhong Zhang

We determine the Poisson algebras generated by partial Casimirs of undeformed and non-standard $q$-deformed $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ coalgebras, respectively. The derivation is performed on the abstract algebraic level and does not depend on any particular symplectic realization. For the 3- and 4-site cases the constructions associated with the undeformed $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ produce the rank-one and rank-two Racah Poisson algebras, respectively, while those with the non-standard deformed $\mathfrak{sl}$ yield finite quadratic Poisson algebras generated by connected partial Casimirs. At both the three and four sites, the final closure coefficients do not explicitly depend on the deformation parameter. The results hold at the Poisson coalgebra level and hence apply to any realizations which preserve the defining brackets and coproducts. Canonical symplectic realizations give rise to Hamiltonians in spaces of non-constant curvature. For the Stäckel $q$-deformed Smorodinsky-Winternitz model we show explicitly how the universal coalgebra sector is completed to maximal superintegrability. An exact two-block identity, proved directly in the localized Poisson algebra without appealing to a symplectic realization, controls the additional Stäckel integrals. In three dimensions, it generates a quadratic Poisson block with its own Casimir relation; in four dimensions, its coupling to the full left/right coalgebra family is organized into three nested quadratic blocks, and the same identity extends this nested coupling to arbitrary $N$. Explicit higher-site partial Casimirs and factorized bracket generators are collected in the appendices.
A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography

A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break. In the resulting scheme, the ghost values are interpolated bilinearly at the image point; solid and dry nodes are excluded, and the weights of the remaining nodes are renormalized. Mass is conserved by solving the continuity equation in cut-cell form, while the momentum equations are left unchanged. The proposed scheme is about as accurate as the ghost-cell method without this modification and preserves a lake at rest whose shoreline crosses an immersed wall. Because only the continuity equation is modified, it avoids the treatment of the momentum equations on cut cells (wall pressure, cell merging) that a full cut-cell method requires.
Distributional Regression for Arbitrary Response Variables Using ReLU Neural Networks
Junpeng Ren; Carlos Misael Madrid Padilla; Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla

This paper develops a unified framework for distributional regression with arbitrary response variables. Rather than relying on scalar thresholds or Euclidean structure, we model conditional event probabilities indexed by measurable sets, which extends distributional regression to general response spaces while retaining a direct connection to classical event-based formulations. Within this framework, we study two complementary estimators: a preliminary estimator based on separate regression of event indicators, and a constrained estimator that enforces inclusion-consistent predictions through a directed acyclic graph (DAG) over a finite set family. We establish general error bounds for both estimators and further specialize the results to dense ReLU networks, yielding explicit convergence rates overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Simulation studies and real-data experiments further demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Fisher Information and Differentiability for $r$-Largest Generalized Extreme-Value Models
Jihong Park; Yire Shin; Jeong-Soo Park

The $r$ largest observations of a block form a dependent random vector whose support moves with all three parameters of the $r$-largest generalized extreme-value ($r$GEV) model. For a fixed number $r$ of order statistics, we show that the model is differentiable in quadratic mean if and only if $k_0<1/2$, where $k=-γ$ is the shape parameter; the threshold is thus the same as for block maxima, because only the largest or the smallest retained order statistic can reach the moving boundary. In this range the Fisher information is positive definite and decomposes into the block-maximum information plus contributions of the lower order statistics, and it equals the negative expected Hessian, which we prove without using any estimator. The model is then locally asymptotically normal, whereas for $k_0\ge1/2$ root-$n$ local asymptotic normality fails. Numerically, using the five largest order statistics instead of the block maximum alone lowers the efficient asymptotic standard error by about $45\%$ for the shape parameter and by $20$--$24\%$ for the 100-year return level in heavy-tailed cases ($k_0\le-0.2$), but by only about $2\%$ for the return level when $k_0=0.4$.
Two-weight T1 theorem for fractional Riesz transforms: one measure supported on a $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve
Ji Li; Chun-Yen Shen; Eric Sawyer; Brett Wick

Let $0\leqα<n$, and let $σ$ and $ω$ be locally finite positive Borel measures on $\R^n$, possibly with common point masses. Suppose that one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve. We prove that the $α$-fractional Riesz vector maps $L^2(σ)$ to $L^2(ω)$ if and only if the two $\cA_2^α$ conditions with holes, the two punctured $A_2^α$ conditions, and the forward and dual testing conditions over rotated cubes hold. The theorem includes curves whose tangent is not Hölder continuous of any positive order. Straightening such a curve produces a kernel whose first derivatives need not satisfy the Hölder estimates required by the energy-side-condition $T1$ theorem. We prove both strong energy conditions in the straightened coordinates using only a sufficiently small graph slope, and show that these conditions are preserved under biLipschitz changes of variables. The Dini condition makes the errors in the kernel and testing comparisons summable. We then transfer the energy conditions back and apply the $T1$ theorem to the original smooth Riesz kernel. We also obtain a two-weight criterion for Green gradients with curve-supported sources. For arclength measure on the curve and observation measure $\dist(x,Γ)^β\,dx$, the range is $β>n-3$ in a bounded tube and $n-3<β<n-2$ in $\R^n$. The endpoints fail logarithmically whenever the measure is locally finite. In dimension three, the corresponding whole-space range for the Biot--Savart field with arbitrary vector densities is $0<β<1$.
Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
Xingxing Xu; Minjia Shi; Jon-Lark Kim

Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.
On the convexification of a bilinearly constrained set with a common variable

We study the convexification of sets defined by box constraints and bilinear inequality constraints in which all bilinear terms share a common variable. For this structured class of nonconvex sets, we provide a complete characterization of the extreme points of the convex hull and derive an explicit description of all facet-defining inequalities, thereby obtaining a full polyhedral description of the convex hull. In addition, we develop a polynomial-time separation algorithm for the facet-defining inequalities and illustrate its effectiveness through examples. These results offer both structural insight into the geometry of the convex hull and algorithmic tools for identifying violated inequalities.
Constraint-Lifted Sector-Constrained Guidance for Rear-Approach Interception
Jhon Manuel Portella Delgado; Dennis S Bernstein; Ankit Goel

This paper develops a sector-constrained guidance (SCG) law for interception of a maneuvering target while maintaining a prescribed approach geometry. The line of sight is required to remain within a specified angular sector behind the target throughout the engagement, resulting in a state-constrained guidance problem. To enforce this constraint, the directional angle between the target heading and the line of sight is mapped from the prescribed sector to an unconstrained coordinate using a sigmoid diffeomorphism. A guidance law is then designed in the lifted coordinate to generate a desired transverse velocity and corresponding pursuer lead angle. The desired lead angle is tracked through an inner-loop turn-rate controller, which is implemented through the normal-acceleration command of a nonlinear point-mass model. This construction embeds the sector constraint directly into the guidance law and does not require online constrained optimization. Numerical simulations against a maneuvering target show that SCG achieves interception while maintaining the prescribed rear-sector constraint, including when the pursuer normal-acceleration command is subject to actuator saturation. Comparisons with proportional guidance under the same engagement conditions demonstrate that proportional guidance may achieve interception but does not maintain the prescribed directional constraint.
On Mattila's intersection problem in the plane: sharp dimension and positive measure of rotated difference sets
Thang Pham; Chun-Yen Shen; Dung The Tran

Let \(A,B\subset\R^2\) be nonempty Borel sets. We prove that \[ \dimH(gA-B)\ge\min\{\dimH A+\dimH B,2\} \] for almost all \(g\in\mathrm O(2)\). This bound is sharp in general, and the proof gives a corresponding statement for the lower Hausdorff dimension of convolutions of Frostman measures. We also prove that \(\LL^2(gA-B)>0\) for almost all \(g\) if both dimensions exceed \((\sqrt{13}-1)/2\). The second result follows from an angular decomposition, refined decoupling and a two-ends Furstenberg estimate. Some applications on intersection patterns are also addressed.
Boundary regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded domains
Mengyu Huo; Tianling Jin; Jingang Xiong

We prove boundary Hölder regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded smooth domains with zero exterior data. For $0<σ<1$, $n>2σ$, and $m>1$, we show that nonnegative weak dual solutions $v$ of $\partial_t v+(-Δ)^σ(v^m)=0$ satisfy \[ \frac{v}{d^{σ/m}}\in C_{x,t}^{α,\frac{αm}{σ(m+1)}} \] up to the boundary and away from the initial time, for some $α\in(0,σ)$, where $d$ denotes the distance to the boundary. More generally, we establish boundary Hölder estimates for $u/d^σ$ for nonnegative viscosity solutions of $\partial_t u=u^γLu$, with $0<γ<1$ and initial data comparable to $d^σ$. Here $L$ is a symmetric stable operator of order $2σ$ whose measurable angular density is bounded above and below by positive constants. Our proof combines comparison principles and boundary barriers with a blow-up and compactness argument based on a Liouville theorem for ancient solutions in a half-space.
Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields

We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman. To obtain these point counts, We prove a unitary big monodromy theorem generalizing big monodromy theorems of Yu and Achter-Pries by appealing to an arithmeticity theorem of Venkataramana.
Admissibility-Preserving Constraint Lifting for Conditional Deadbeat Control of Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems
Jhon Manuel Portella Delgado; Ankit Goel

This paper presents a constraint-enforcing control framework for a class of discrete-time strict- feedback nonlinear systems. The objective is to guarantee closed-loop stability while ensuring forward invariance of a prescribed safe set defined by state constraints. The pro- posed approach transforms the constrained control problem into an equivalent unconstrained one through smooth constraint-lifting mappings constructed using strictly increasing sigmoid functions. Controller synthesis is then performed in the lifted coordinates, enabling recursive backstepping design while preserving the admissibility of the constrained states. Conditions on the controller gains are derived to guarantee both asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system and forward invariance of the admissible domain of the lifting functions. The analysis also establishes a conditional deadbeat property for the second backstepping step once the system trajectory enters a region in which the lifting-domain admissibility conditions are satisfied. Numerical simulations of a constrained Roup oscillator demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in enforcing state constraints while tracking a reference command.
Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem

We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and combine local boundary analysis with a global argument on an algebraic curve. We exclude Diagrams~1, 2, 4, 6 and~8 for complex germs, Diagram~7 on curves through real configurations, and Diagram~3 on curves with a positive arc. For Diagrams~5 and~9, direct order estimates show that the product $Δ$ of all squared mutual distances tends to zero. On a hypothetical curve containing a positive arc, a first pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $Δ$. On the completed curve, $Δ$ must then have a pole elsewhere. The identity $Δ^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$ forces a four-product to have a pole there, contradicting the same vanishing conclusion. The computer-assisted inputs concern Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 and use exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.
Stable Matrix-Free Q-less QR via Preconditioning and Randomization
Oleg Balabanov; Maksim Melnichenko; Michael W. Mahoney

This article develops matrix-free Q-less QR algorithms for orthogonalizing tall linear operators. Our main algorithm, CQRRTO, uses randomized preconditioning to make a single Cholesky QR pass numerically safe for any numerically full-rank operator, overcoming the stability issues of Cholesky QR and related methods that operate on the Gram matrix. Compared with deterministic stabilized variants such as Q-less Cholesky QR2 (reorthogonalized Cholesky QR), it remains numerically stable under substantially weaker conditioning assumptions while requiring fewer operator applications. Matrix-free Q-less QR can be useful for improving the numerical robustness of least-squares solves via the normal equations, spectral approximations in a low-dimensional basis, and inversion of operators with low-rank updates via the Woodbury identity. We present a componentwise stability analysis of preconditioned Q-less Cholesky QR that applies to matrix-free operators and is modular with respect to the preconditioner, yielding guarantees for Q-less Cholesky QR, Cholesky QR2, shifted Cholesky QR3, and CQRRTO as special cases. All methods are implemented in the open-source RandLAPACK library.
(Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation

We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schrödinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+δ}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $δ>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.
The Multiplicity One Defect and Congruence-Modular Exponent Ratios

We introduce a multiplicity one defect that quantitatively measures the failure of multiplicity one for the Jacobian of the Shimura curve \(X^D(M)\) attached to an indefinite rational quaternion algebra of discriminant \(D\) and level \(M\), localized at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra. By constructing a certain lattice inside the local Tate module, we obtain an explicit upper bound for the defect in terms of congruences between eigenforms and the lattice-Tate module discrepancies associated with the individual newforms. We then show that the local ratio between the congruence exponent and the modular exponent of modular abelian varieties attached to newforms is bounded above by the multiplicity one defect. Finally, we examine the relation with the Gorenstein property and give an explicit example at level \(126\) where the local Hecke algebra is Gorenstein even though multiplicity one fails. In this example, we compute the multiplicity one defect to be \(3\), which is also the local congruence--modular exponent ratio.
Mingming Cao; Binyu Du; Kôzô Yabuta

We develop a unified multi-scale framework for sparse domination of multilinear operators beyond the multilinear Calderón--Zygmund theory. More precisely, under mild hypotheses on a support condition, weak type and restricted strong type uniform bounds for finite partial sums, and single-scale improving and regularity estimates, we establish $(r_1, \ldots, r_m, s')$-sparse form bound for a family of localized $m$-linear operators uniformly over all finite partial sums. This sparse bound yields weighted norm inequalities for the corresponding multilinear Muckenhoupt classes $A_{\vec{p}, (\vec{r}, s)}$, including the quasi-Banach range. As applications, we determine the optimal open sparse range for multilinear rough singular integrals, and characterize sparse domination for bilinear pseudo-differential operators. Further applications include sparse bounds for bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers, bilinear spherical maximal operators, and bilinear Bochner--Riesz means.
Using the Renormalized Energy from Ginzburg-Landau Theory to Compute Solution Landscapes in the Reduced Landau-de Gennes Theory

We study nematic liquid crystal phases confined to bounded, two-dimensional (2D) domains, in the reduced Landau-de Gennes (rLdG) theoretical framework. The rLdG framework is equivalent to the celebrated Ginzburg-Landau (GL) theoretical setting, under certain assumptions. In the asymptotic limit of large domains (or low temperatures), we recall the concept of the finite-dimensional renormalized energy in the GL theory [Bethuel et al., GL Vortices, Prog. Nonlinear Differ. Equ. Appl. 13, Birkhäuser, 1994.] and generalize it to polygons with sharp corners. The renormalized energy is fully defined by the triplet, $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c}, \mathbf{d}$), of topological degrees of the interior defects ($\mathbf{d}$) and the winding number contribution of polygon vertices ($\mathbf{c}$) and interior defect locations ($\mathbf{a}$), subject to sum rules dictated by the imposed Dirichlet boundary condition. We use the critical points of the renormalized energy to construct initial conditions for the rLdG solver, recover known energy-minimizing and non-energy minimizing saddle points of the rLdG energy on a disc, regular hexagon and rectangle along with the discovery of previously unreported rLdG solution branches. The renormalized energy approach is computationally substantially more efficient than a direct PDE-solver in the rLdG setting but misses solution branches with line defects and finite-size effects.
The Fröhlich Polaron at large total momentum in d=3

We consider the three-dimensional Fröhlich polaron at fixed coupling strength $α>0$ and total momentum $P \in \bbR^3$. We show that the bottom of the spectrum reaches the essential spectrum at a finite value of $|P|$, implying that the fiber Hamiltonian has no ground state at sufficiently large total momentum. This extends the known weak-coupling result to arbitrary coupling. Our approach describes states near the spectral threshold by a fully interacting polaron with small residual momentum and one additional phonon carrying almost all of the total momentum.
The moduli space of cubic surfaces and its orbifold fundamental group
Daniel Allcock; Tathagata Basak; Eduard Looijenga

We find a new presentation of the orbifold fundamental group of the moduli space of cubic surfaces, based on the Artin group of the Petersen graph. This group has two well-known quotients, which appear in the simplest possible way: killing the squares resp. sixth powers of our generators yields the Coxeter group $W(E_6)$ resp. a certain arithmetic group in $\operatorname{PU}(1,4)$. Along the way we present a certain central extension by $\mathbb{Z}$, of the genus zero mapping class group with any number of punctures. The $6$-puncture case is essential in this paper, and the general case may have independent interest.
From isolated singular wells to exact Bloch bands: the trigonometric Pöschl-Teller lattice

An exactly solvable lattice with periodic inverse-square singularities exhibits two physically distinct mechanisms of spectral-gap closure. The model arises from the generalized trigonometric Pöschl-Teller potential in the coupling range where both local solutions at each singularity are square-integrable. A transmitting, current-preserving self-adjoint matching condition connects neighboring cells and generates a nontrivial Bloch spectrum. For a generic lattice with two inequivalent singular sublattices, the spectrum contains two alternating families of gaps, and the band edges reproduce the scale-invariant spectra of the associated finite singular system. One gap family closes when the two sublattices become equivalent. In this symmetric limit, however, the primitive period halves, so the apparent band crossing results from Brillouin-zone folding. A different family closes at a critical but genuinely asymmetric configuration. Because the primitive period is preserved, adjacent bands then meet at the center of the original Brillouin zone in a genuine massless Dirac-like cone. Near either critical limit, a small finite gap acts as an effective Dirac mass: the dispersion remains quadratic near a band edge but crosses over to a massive Dirac-like form beyond that narrow region. The band curvatures define effective electron and hole masses. Exact Bloch eigenfunctions further reveal that isospectral lattices can display different single-particle probability densities. This model therefore provides an analytically controlled one-dimensional setting in which conventional quadratic carriers, massive Dirac-like band dispersions, and a tunable massless contact coexist within the same singular lattice.
Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions

We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.
A Generalized Elephant Random Walk with Time-Dependent Memory

The elephant random walk (ERW) is a discrete-time random walk with complete memory. At every step the walker chooses one of the previous increments at random and then either repeats with a constant probability $p\in [0,1]$ or reverses it. Since its introduction by Schütz and Trimper, the model has become a useful probabilistic framework for studying long-range dependence, anomalous diffusion, reinforcement, and phase transitions. This paper proposes a generalized ERW model with time-dependent memory. In this generalized model, the usual constant memory parameter $p$ in the standard ERW is allowed to change with time. The cental limit theorems, and the law of the iterated logarithm and some other strong laws are obtained.
Online Submodular Welfare Maximization: Computation is not the Bottleneck

We revisit the online submodular welfare maximization problem (OSW), a vast generalization of numerous well-studied online allocation problems, including online bipartite matching, display ads and AdWords. A natural greedy OSW algorithm achieves a competitive ratio of $1/2$ [LLN06], and $1-1/e$ under i.i.d. arrivals [KPV13]. Both bounds are tight for polynomial-time algorithms unless NP=RP [KPV13]. The information-theoretic limits for OSW, in contrast, remained open. This prompted researchers to ask for tighter upper bounds [Mehta13] or conjecture the existence of better-competitive (slow) algorithms [Huang23, LTX+23, CHS24, Huang2024, HTW24}. We resolve Mehta's question and refute the subsequent conjectures, proving that the greedy algorithm is in fact tight for both adversarial and i.i.d. arrivals, regardless of computation time. Seemingly contradicting recent $(1-1/e)$-competitive fractional algorithms for OSW [HJP+24,Patton26], we show that this impossibility even holds for fractional algorithms, provided their outputs correspond to marginals that are roundable in hindsight. Conceptually, our proofs can be seen as identifying that a bottleneck for OSW, even under (deterministic) adversarial arrivals, is the inherently random notion of correlation gap [ADSY12].
Baire measurable functions and automorphisms of the truth-table degrees

We show that if an automorphism $π$ of the truth-table degrees is induced by a Baire measurable function $F\colon 2^ω\to 2^ω$, or merely induced on some comeager set by a continuous function, then $π$ is the identity. The same results hold for the weak truth-table degrees. The argument is an adaptation to truth-table reducibility of OpenAI's recent proof that the Turing degrees are rigid.
Loop Fundamental Quandles: A Geometric Generalization of the Knot Quandle

The knot quandle, introduced independently by Joyce and Matveev, admits a geometric description in terms of nooses. Motivated by this description, we introduce the \textit{loop fundamental quandle} $LQ(X,A,\ast)$ of a pair $(X,A)$ with a fixed base point $\ast\in X$. Its elements are represented by pairs consisting of a loop in $A$ and a path joining the base point of the loop to the fixed base point $\ast$. More generally, for a loop condition $P$ on $A$, invariant under free homotopy, we define the loop fundamental quandle $LQ(X,A,\ast;P)$. We establish functoriality and homotopy invariance of the loop fundamental quandle and show that it admits a natural augmented quandle structure over $π_1(X,\ast)$. For a knot $K$ in $S^3$, applying the construction to its exterior gives the \textit{knot loop quandle} $LQ(K,\ast;P)$. Appropriate choices of the loop condition recover the knot quandle, its $n$-th power quandles, and the full knot quandle. The construction is inspired by Joyce's noose-theoretic approach, but allows loop data that need not arise as the boundary of a disk satisfying the noose condition.
Robust Quickest Change Detection with Cost-Efficient Experiment Design and Unknown Post-Change Model

A quickest change detection problem is studied where the decision-maker has access to multiple experiments, but can choose only one experiment at a time to detect the change. The true post-change distribution under each experiment is unknown, but known to belong to a family of distributions. It is assumed that each of these families of distributions has an element that is least favorable in a well-defined sense. An algorithm is proposed that is designed using the least favorable distributions. It is shown that the algorithm is first-order asymptotically optimal, as the rate of false alarms goes to zero. This algorithm minimizes the worst-case average detection delay over all post-change distributions within the assumed families, subject to a constraint on the average run length to false alarm and constraints on the average fraction of time each experiment is performed before change.
High-order uniformly accurate fully discrete schemes with long time near-conservations for two nonlinear coupled dispersive models in the nonrelativistic regime
Lina Wang; Jiyong Li; Bin Wang

Nonlinear coupled dispersive models arise in numerous physical settings, including quantum electrodynamics, nonlinear optics, and plasma dynamics. In the nonrelativistic limit, such systems exhibit rapid temporal oscillations of wavelength $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{2})$, controlled by a dimensionless parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$. Moreover, owing to the Yukawa-coupled interaction terms, numerical schemes that simultaneously achieve high-order uniform accuracy and approximately preserve the mass and the energy are essential for reliable simulations. In this work, we propose a class of fully discrete schemes for nonlinear coupled dispersive models in the nonrelativistic regime that achieve higher-order uniform accuracy and approximately preserve both invariants over long times. Spatial discretization is based on the Fourier pseudospectral method, and time advancement employs two-scale exponential Runge-Kutta methods. Numerical experiments on the highly oscillatory Klein-Gordon-Dirac and Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger equations in one, two, and three dimensions confirm that the resulting schemes attain the theoretically predicted uniform accuracy and the long-time near-conservation of both invariants.
CLNO: Conservative Local Neural Operator for Compressible Flow Prediction
Buxuan Wang; Rongzu Li; Qingsong Zou

We propose a conservative local neural operator (CLNO) for accurate and generalizable autoregressive prediction of compressible flows. Building upon the locality and translation invariance of the local neural operator (LNO), CLNO introduces a conservative evolution framework based on local subdomains of fixed physical size, separating local mean-state evolution from fine-scale reconstruction. The flow is encoded into subdomain-integrated conservative states and fine-scale features, while a shared local network predicts interface fluxes for finite-volume updates that enforce discrete conservation. A convolutional reconstruction network recovers fine-scale structures using zero-mean basis functions, preserving the updated local means and providing information for subsequent evolution. To accommodate different physical parameters, Reynolds--Mach number conditioning modulates the encoding, flux-prediction, and reconstruction networks, enabling a single model to learn parameter-dependent dynamics and generalize to unseen parameter combinations without retraining. CLNO supports prediction across spatial resolutions, computational domain sizes, and boundary conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved generalization and competitive or higher accuracy compared with LNO, including order-of-magnitude error reductions in representative cases, at approximately three to five times the inference cost on periodic benchmarks. These results demonstrate accurate, generalizable, and physically consistent flow prediction through conservative local evolution and fine-scale reconstruction.
Delay-Doppler Duality: Simplifying Exact Equalization of Zak-OTFS in Time or in Frequency

The Zak-OTFS carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, and given the input-output (I/O) relation at one DD point in a frame, we can predict the I/O relation at all other points. While it is simple to acquire the effective wireless channel with Zak-OTFS, the cost of embracing inter-carrier interference is equalization complexity. The cost of linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) equalization grows cubically with the frame size. We describe how to use channel knowledge to reduce equalization complexity. For any pulse shaping filter, and for fractional delays and Dopplers, we show that the DD channel matrix is unitarily similar, through the discrete Zak transform, to a time-domain (TD) matrix that is a weighted sum of cyclic delay and Doppler operators, where the weights are the taps of the effective channel. We also obtain a dual frequency-domain (FD) form through an additional Fourier transform. The TD matrix is banded with a width set by the delay spread that is independent of the Doppler spread, whereas the FD matrix is banded with a width set only by the Doppler spread. We design a receiver that reads off the two widths from the channel estimate, selects the cheaper domain, and solves the banded system exactly, using a bordered Cholesky factorization that treats the quasi-periodic wrap-around without sacrificing degrees of freedom. Filters that decay slowly need a few preconditioned conjugate gradient steps. We show that the complexity of equalization becomes linear in the frame size. Simulations match direct DD-LMMSE error rates with three to four orders of magnitude fewer multiplications. A single receiver handles channels with very different delay and Doppler characteristics.
Osmin Ferrer Villar; Jose Naranjo Martinez; Breiner Rivero Reyes

This paper, we introduce and study biatomic systems in Hilbert spaces, a natural generalization of classical atomic systems; this new concept allows us to represent bounded linear operators using two Bessel sequences simultaneously. In addition, we establish equivalent characterizations of these systems, study their relationship with Bessel biframes and demonstrate the stability of the class under natural operations: duality with respect to the adjunct, orthogonal projections, unit operators and concatenation.
Limit Theory for Online Expectile Estimation under Short and Long Range Dependence
Younghun Lee; Jake Zummo; Wei Biao Wu

Expectiles are tail-sensitive distributional summaries with important applications in financial risk measurement and forecasting, yet statistical theory for their online estimation from dependent data remains limited. We study a one-pass, stochastic-gradient algorithm with constant learning rate $γ$ for estimating the marginal expectile of a stationary causal process. The recursion admits a unique stationary causal solution and geometrically forgets its initialization.
